all-star-ghani::bde-golden-triangle-port.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary from Hurghada explores Egypt’s most renowned offshore marine parks: the Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, and Elphinstone Reef. It is ideal for advanced divers who enjoy challenging dives, strong currents, and close encounters with large pelagics in clear, blue waters.

Elphinstone Reef, located near Marsa Alam, is among the most famous dive sites in Egypt. Steep walls covered in colorful soft corals drop into the depths, where oceanic whitetip sharks are commonly seen from October to December. Depending on the season, divers may also encounter manta rays, hammerheads, and whale sharks.

The Brothers Islands rise dramatically from deep water and are known for their exceptional corals and abundance of marine life. Little Brother features pristine coral walls and schools of barracudas and jacks, while Big Brother is home to the historic wrecks of the Numidia and Aida II. Both islands attract grey reef, thresher, and oceanic whitetip sharks.

Daedalus Reef, situated in open water further south, is marked by its lighthouse and vast coral-covered walls. It is one of the best sites in the Red Sea for schooling hammerheads, particularly between May and August, and also hosts oceanic whitetips, mantas, and trevallies.

This route offers a perfect combination of thrilling shark dives, impressive wrecks, and pristine coral reefs, providing an unforgettable Red Sea liveaboard experience.

all-star-ghani::brothers-daedalus-elphin.highlightsDescription:
This itinerary explores the northern Red Sea, combining Egypt’s most famous wrecks and reefs with the crystal-clear waters of the Straits of Tiran. It offers a perfect balance of history, color, and marine life, ideal for divers of all experience levels.

The adventure begins with the iconic wrecks of Abu Nuhas, home to four well-preserved ships—the Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, and Kimon M—each offering easy access, vibrant coral growth, and schools of reef fish. The world-famous SS Thistlegorm follows, a must-dive site loaded with wartime relics such as trucks, motorcycles, and ammunition, now home to batfish, scorpionfish, and nudibranchs.

Further north, Ras Mohammed National Park impresses with spectacular walls, vivid coral gardens, and dense schools of barracuda, snappers, and trevallies. Shark Reef and Yolanda Reef are among the region’s most celebrated sites, known for their breathtaking topography and marine biodiversity.

The journey continues to the Straits of Tiran, where the reefs of Jackson, Thomas, Woodhouse, and Gordon rise from the deep. These vibrant coral pinnacles attract a wealth of marine life, including turtles, reef sharks, and large schools of fish. Strong currents and dramatic drop-offs make for exciting drift dives and stunning photo opportunities.

Combining historic wrecks, thriving reefs, and exhilarating drifts, this 7-night itinerary showcases the very best of Egypt’s northern Red Sea.

all-star-ghani::north-hurghada-hurghada-.highlightsDescription:
This itinerary brings together the best of the northern Red Sea and the offshore Brothers Islands, combining legendary wrecks, colorful coral reefs, and thrilling shark encounters. Departing and returning to Hurghada, it’s a route that offers variety, adventure, and stunning underwater scenery.

The journey begins in the northern region, where divers can explore iconic sites such as Abu Nuhas with its cluster of accessible wrecks — Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, and Kimon M — each rich in marine life and history. The SS Thistlegorm, one of the most famous wrecks in the world, is another highlight, filled with preserved World War II artifacts and surrounded by schooling fish and vibrant reef life.

Further north, Ras Mohammed National Park and Gubal Island showcase the pristine beauty of the Sinai Peninsula. Expect steep walls, colorful coral gardens, and dense schools of barracuda and trevallies, along with the occasional dolphin sighting.

The itinerary concludes with the Brothers Islands, located more than 40 miles offshore. These twin pinnacles rise dramatically from the deep and offer some of the most exhilarating dives in Egypt. The steep coral walls are alive with color and frequented by grey reef, thresher, and oceanic whitetip sharks. Big Brother also features the famous wrecks of the Numidia and Aida II, now beautifully overgrown with coral and teeming with fish.

Combining the north’s historic wrecks and lively reefs with the remote, pelagic-rich Brothers, this route delivers a complete Red Sea experience in one unforgettable week.

Combining historic wrecks, thriving reefs, and exhilarating drifts, this 7-night itinerary showcases the very best of Egypt’s northern Red Sea.

all-star-scuba-scene::brothers-daedalus-.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary from Hurghada explores Egypt’s most renowned offshore marine parks: the Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, and Elphinstone Reef. It is ideal for advanced divers who enjoy challenging dives, strong currents, and close encounters with large pelagics in clear, blue waters.

Elphinstone Reef, located near Marsa Alam, is among the most famous dive sites in Egypt. Steep walls covered in colorful soft corals drop into the depths, where oceanic whitetip sharks are commonly seen from October to December. Depending on the season, divers may also encounter manta rays, hammerheads, and whale sharks.

The Brothers Islands rise dramatically from deep water and are known for their exceptional corals and abundance of marine life. Little Brother features pristine coral walls and schools of barracudas and jacks, while Big Brother is home to the historic wrecks of the Numidia and Aida II. Both islands attract grey reef, thresher, and oceanic whitetip sharks.

Daedalus Reef, situated in open water further south, is marked by its lighthouse and vast coral-covered walls. It is one of the best sites in the Red Sea for schooling hammerheads, particularly between May and August, and also hosts oceanic whitetips, mantas, and trevallies.

This route offers a perfect combination of thrilling shark dives, impressive wrecks, and pristine coral reefs, providing an unforgettable Red Sea liveaboard experience.

all-star-scuba-scene::brothers-daedalus-.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary from Hurghada explores Egypt’s most renowned offshore marine parks: the Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, and Elphinstone Reef. It is ideal for advanced divers who enjoy challenging dives, strong currents, and close encounters with large pelagics in clear, blue waters.

Elphinstone Reef, located near Marsa Alam, is among the most famous dive sites in Egypt. Steep walls covered in colorful soft corals drop into the depths, where oceanic whitetip sharks are commonly seen from October to December. Depending on the season, divers may also encounter manta rays, hammerheads, and whale sharks.

The Brothers Islands rise dramatically from deep water and are known for their exceptional corals and abundance of marine life. Little Brother features pristine coral walls and schools of barracudas and jacks, while Big Brother is home to the historic wrecks of the Numidia and Aida II. Both islands attract grey reef, thresher, and oceanic whitetip sharks.

Daedalus Reef, situated in open water further south, is marked by its lighthouse and vast coral-covered walls. It is one of the best sites in the Red Sea for schooling hammerheads, particularly between May and August, and also hosts oceanic whitetips, mantas, and trevallies.

This route offers a perfect combination of thrilling shark dives, impressive wrecks, and pristine coral reefs, providing an unforgettable Red Sea liveaboard experience.

all-star-scuba-scene::daedalus-rockyzaba.highlightsDescription:
This southern Red Sea itinerary combines two iconic regions, Daedalus Reef and St. John’s Plateau, offering an exceptional mix of shark encounters, coral diversity, and spectacular underwater scenery. Ideal for experienced divers, it features deep walls, open-water drift dives, and remarkable marine life in Egypt’s far south.

Daedalus Reef rises from the deep in open water and is marked by its distinctive lighthouse. This large reef is known for year-round hammerhead sightings, with schooling events most common from May to August. Divers may also see oceanic whitetips, grey reef and thresher sharks, as well as tunas, trevallies, and manta rays. The vertical walls are covered in vibrant hard and soft corals, protected within a marine park that showcases some of the healthiest reefs in the Red Sea.

St. John’s lies at the southernmost tip of Egypt near the Sudanese border and offers a wide range of dive sites, each with unique features. The area’s plateau system includes caverns, tunnels, and swim-throughs decorated with colorful soft corals, sea fans, and whips. Reef sharks, turtles, and schools of fish are often encountered, while the calm, clear waters make diving here both exciting and relaxing.

Together, Daedalus and St. John’s deliver the best of the southern Red Sea, combining thrilling pelagic encounters with peaceful coral gardens and unforgettable underwater landscapes.

all-star-scuba-scene::daedalus-rockyzaba.highlightsDescription:
This itinerary offers one of the most exhilarating diving experiences in the southern Red Sea, perfect for advanced divers seeking close encounters with sharks and pelagic species. Departing and returning to Port Ghalib, the route focuses on Egypt’s most remote and spectacular offshore reefs, where nutrient-rich currents attract large marine life all year round.

At Daedalus, divers explore a vast reef crowned by a working lighthouse and surrounded by deep blue waters. This is one of the best places in the Red Sea to spot hammerhead sharks, both solitary and schooling, particularly between May and August. Oceanic whitetips, thresher sharks, and grey reef sharks are also frequent visitors. The vertical walls are draped in colorful soft corals and massive hard coral formations, offering world-class photo opportunities and pristine reef life.

Rocky Island, a small exposed site known for its challenging conditions, rewards divers with thrilling drift dives and the chance to encounter whale sharks, mantas, and leopard sharks. The walls are densely covered with gorgonians, sponges, and soft corals, creating a vibrant backdrop for pelagic encounters.

Nearby Zabargad Island is both mysterious and beautiful, featuring unique underwater landscapes of pinnacles, slopes, and canyons covered in soft corals. A Russian wreck lies in the shallows, now home to abundant marine life. Green turtles use the island as a nesting site, and pelagic visitors such as tunas and barracudas are often seen cruising in the blue.

Combining breathtaking coral gardens, remote island seascapes, and world-class shark action, this route promises a true adventure for those eager to explore the wilder side of the Red Sea.

all-star-scuba-scene::north-brothers-hur.highlightsDescription:
This itinerary explores the northern Red Sea, combining Egypt’s most famous wrecks and reefs with the crystal-clear waters of the Straits of Tiran. It offers a perfect balance of history, color, and marine life, ideal for divers of all experience levels.

The adventure begins with the iconic wrecks of Abu Nuhas, home to four well-preserved ships—the Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, and Kimon M—each offering easy access, vibrant coral growth, and schools of reef fish. The world-famous SS Thistlegorm follows, a must-dive site loaded with wartime relics such as trucks, motorcycles, and ammunition, now home to batfish, scorpionfish, and nudibranchs.

Further north, Ras Mohammed National Park impresses with spectacular walls, vivid coral gardens, and dense schools of barracuda, snappers, and trevallies. Shark Reef and Yolanda Reef are among the region’s most celebrated sites, known for their breathtaking topography and marine biodiversity.

The journey continues to the Straits of Tiran, where the reefs of Jackson, Thomas, Woodhouse, and Gordon rise from the deep. These vibrant coral pinnacles attract a wealth of marine life, including turtles, reef sharks, and large schools of fish. Strong currents and dramatic drop-offs make for exciting drift dives and stunning photo opportunities.

Combining historic wrecks, thriving reefs, and exhilarating drifts, this 7-night itinerary showcases the very best of Egypt’s northern Red Sea.

all-star-scuba-scene::south-port-ghalib-.highlightsDescription:
This itinerary offers a complete Red Sea experience, combining the highlights of the central and southern regions into one unforgettable journey. Departing from Port Ghalib and ending in Hurghada, it includes a variety of dive sites featuring dramatic walls, colorful coral gardens, drift dives, and possible encounters with pelagic species.

This one-way itinerary is designed for experienced divers who want to discover the Red Sea’s incredible diversity in a single week of adventure.

all-star-scuba-scene::ultimate-red-seapo.highlightsDescription:
This itinerary brings together the best of the northern Red Sea and the offshore Brothers Islands, combining legendary wrecks, colorful coral reefs, and thrilling shark encounters. Departing and returning to Hurghada, it’s a route that offers variety, adventure, and stunning underwater scenery.

The journey begins in the northern region, where divers can explore iconic sites such as Abu Nuhas with its cluster of accessible wrecks — Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, and Kimon M — each rich in marine life and history. The SS Thistlegorm, one of the most famous wrecks in the world, is another highlight, filled with preserved World War II artifacts and surrounded by schooling fish and vibrant reef life.

Further north, Ras Mohammed National Park and Gubal Island showcase the pristine beauty of the Sinai Peninsula. Expect steep walls, colorful coral gardens, and dense schools of barracuda and trevallies, along with the occasional dolphin sighting.

The itinerary concludes with the Brothers Islands, located more than 40 miles offshore. These twin pinnacles rise dramatically from the deep and offer some of the most exhilarating dives in Egypt. The steep coral walls are alive with color and frequented by grey reef, thresher, and oceanic whitetip sharks. Big Brother also features the famous wrecks of the Numidia and Aida II, now beautifully overgrown with coral and teeming with fish.

Combining the north’s historic wrecks and lively reefs with the remote, pelagic-rich Brothers, this route delivers a complete Red Sea experience in one unforgettable week.

alsuraya::brother-deadalus-and-elphinsto.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night liveaboard itinerary explores three of the Red Sea’s most renowned and remote dive sites: the Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, and Elphinstone. Known collectively as the BDE route, this circuit offers dramatic wall dives, strong currents, and the chance to encounter pelagic species including oceanic whitetip sharks, hammerheads, and schooling barracuda.

The Brothers Islands feature steep drop-offs, vibrant coral growth, and historic wrecks like the Aida and Numidia. Daedalus Reef, located in the open sea, is famous for its large schooling fish and frequent shark sightings along its vertical walls. Elphinstone, closer to shore but equally dramatic, offers vibrant soft corals and the possibility of late afternoon drift dives with reef sharks.

This route is ideal for divers seeking remote sites, big animal encounters, and some of the most exhilarating diving the Red Sea has to offer.

alsuraya::brother-deadalus-and-elphinsto.otherLogisticsInfo:
• Required Equipment
    The following equipment is mandatory for each diver:
    • Dive computer
    • Surface Marker Buoy (SMB)
    • Basic gear (mask, snorkel, fins)
    • Regulator with alternate air source (octopus)
    • Buoyancy Control Device (either weight-integrated or with weight belt)
    • Wetsuit (long wetsuits recommended year-round)
    • Dive light for night dives
    Missing equipment can be rented for an additional fee. Rental requests must be made at least 2 weeks prior to departure, as rental gear is not stored onboard.
    It is strongly recommended to bring essential spare parts and repair kits, as well as extra batteries for dive computers, cameras, lights, and other electronic devices. Rechargeable devices may be charged onboard at any time.
  • Check-In
    Check-in is available from 4:00 PM on the day of arrival. Early boarding is not possible, as the crew will be preparing the vessel, cleaning, and performing routine maintenance. The first night is spent in the harbor, with departure scheduled for the following morning.
  • Check-Out
    The vessel returns to the harbor on the afternoon of the day before disembarkation. Luggage will be made available to guests in preparation for departure. Final check-out takes place after breakfast on the last day. Return travel information will be provided onboard.

alsuraya::brother-deadalus-and-elphinsto.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night liveaboard itinerary explores three of the Red Sea’s most renowned and remote dive sites: the Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, and Elphinstone. Known collectively as the BDE route, this circuit offers dramatic wall dives, strong currents, and the chance to encounter pelagic species including oceanic whitetip sharks, hammerheads, and schooling barracuda.

The Brothers Islands feature steep drop-offs, vibrant coral growth, and historic wrecks like the Aida and Numidia. Daedalus Reef, located in the open sea, is famous for its large schooling fish and frequent shark sightings along its vertical walls. Elphinstone, closer to shore but equally dramatic, offers vibrant soft corals and the possibility of late afternoon drift dives with reef sharks.

This route is ideal for divers seeking remote sites, big animal encounters, and some of the most exhilarating diving the Red Sea has to offer.

alsuraya::brother-deadalus-and-elphinsto.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night liveaboard itinerary combines three of the Red Sea’s most spectacular and remote diving regions: Daedalus Reef, the reef systems of St. John's Reef, and the legendary Elphinstone Reef. Located in the deep south of Egypt, these sites offer dramatic underwater topography, vibrant coral formations, and excellent opportunities to encounter large pelagic species.

Daedalus Reef, rising from the open sea, is renowned for its sheer walls, schooling fish, and frequent sightings of hammerheads and oceanic whitetip sharks. St. John’s, near the Sudanese border, features an intricate maze of coral gardens, tunnels, caverns, and pinnacles teeming with reef fish, turtles, and occasional manta rays.

Elphinstone Reef adds another highlight to the itinerary with its steep drop-offs, colorful soft corals, and strong currents that attract oceanic whitetip sharks, hammerheads, and other pelagics.

This itinerary offers a balanced mix of exhilarating drift dives, rich biodiversity, and remote, uncrowded sites—ideal for experienced divers seeking adventure and variety in one of the Red Sea’s most pristine regions.

alsuraya::north-and-brothers-hurghada-hu.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night liveaboard itinerary explores three of the Red Sea’s most renowned and remote dive sites: the Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, and Elphinstone. Known collectively as the BDE route, this circuit offers dramatic wall dives, strong currents, and the chance to encounter pelagic species including oceanic whitetip sharks, hammerheads, and schooling barracuda.

The Brothers Islands feature steep drop-offs, vibrant coral growth, and historic wrecks like the Aida and Numidia. Daedalus Reef, located in the open sea, is famous for its large schooling fish and frequent shark sightings along its vertical walls. Elphinstone, closer to shore but equally dramatic, offers vibrant soft corals and the possibility of late afternoon drift dives with reef sharks.

This route is ideal for divers seeking remote sites, big animal encounters, and some of the most exhilarating diving the Red Sea has to offer.

Early departure towards the northern Red Sea. Check dive at Gubal Island (Barge site), followed by two dives on the iconic wreck of the SS Thistlegorm, exploring the exterior and cargo holds filled with wartime relics. Night anchorage at Shaab Ali.

Shaab Mahmoud, Abu Nuhas & Overnight to Brothers

Morning dive at Shaab Mahmoud (Small Crack), followed by a drift dive along Abu Nuhas reef, home to several famous wrecks. In the afternoon, the yacht begins the offshore crossing to the Brothers Islands. Overnight navigation.

Big Brother Island

Two to three dives around Big Brother Island, including the legendary wrecks of Numidia and Aida and spectacular wall dives. Strong currents and the chance of encounters with pelagic species characterize this exposed offshore site. Overnight at anchor (weather permitting) or begin return navigation.

Small Brother Island & Return

Morning dives at Small Brother Island, including Shark Point and the Coral Plateau. In the afternoon, return cruise towards Hurghada.

Breakfast on board followed by check-out and transfer to the airport or hotel. End of services.

With a mix of history, biodiversity, and adrenaline-filled dives, this itinerary offers an unforgettable Red Sea experience both above and below the surface.

2 dives @ SS Thistlegorm – Discover the legendary WWII British freighter, packed with trucks, motorcycles, and wartime relics

Night Dive: Sha’ab Ali or Thistlegorm – Optional guided night dive

Overnight near the wreck

Abu Nuhas Wrecks

Carnatic – Elegant 19th-century wreck draped in soft corals

Giannis D – A modern cargo wreck known for its photogenic layout and fish life

Drift or Reef Dive near Abu Nuhas

Overnight cruise to Ras Mohamed

Ras Mohamed & SS Dunraven

Shark & Yolanda Reef – Spectacular drift dive among large pelagics and surreal coral gardens

SS Dunraven – Wreck dive on a Victorian-era steamer, now a haven for marine life

Sha’ab Mahmoud – A macro paradise with colorful reef fish and nudibranchs

Overnight in Ras Mohamed area

More Reefs & Channels

Jackfish Alley or Alternatives – Great visibility, coral caves, and the chance of seeing rays and reef sharks

Small Crack – Scenic coral corridor with playful fish and coral diversity

Umm Gamar – Sloping reef with coral towers and reef plateaus

Cruise towards Hurghada coast

Near Hurghada

Fanadir or similar local reef – Great final chance for underwater photos or exploring new coral spots

Sha’ab El Erg – Dolphin encounters are possible at this relaxed, sandy lagoon

Final Dives Near Hurghada

El Mina Wreck – A small military wreck ideal for photography and relaxed

Gota Abu Ramada ("The Aquarium") – A colorful fish-rich reef for a perfect ending

Farewell dinner and overnight onboard in the marina

alsuraya::north-hurghada-hurghada-7-nigh.highlightsDescription: This 7-night itinerary explores the northern Red Sea, offering a mix of fascinating shipwrecks and vibrant reef systems. Highlights include dives on legendary wrecks such as the SS Thistlegorm, a World War II cargo ship now home to schools of fish and soft corals, as well as the Carnatic and Giannis D., both rich in history and marine life. The journey continues through Ras Mohamed National Park, known for its spectacular underwater scenery and dense fish populations, with frequent sightings of turtles, rays, and reef sharks. Colorful coral gardens, drift dives along vertical walls, and calm lagoons provide a variety of underwater landscapes throughout the trip. Between dives, guests enjoy the comfort and service aboard Alsuraya Liveaboard, creating a relaxing and well-rounded Red Sea experience.

Arrival & Check-in

Arrival at Hurghada Airport

Transfer to Alsuraya Liveaboard (Check-in from 4pm)

Welcome briefing, safety instructions, equipment setup

Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforeseeable factors.

Ras Mohamed National Park

Ras Za’atar – Check dive at a lush coral garden teeming with marine life

Shark & Yolanda Reef – A world-renowned dive with dramatic walls and a sunken cargo of toilets and bathtubs

Jackfish Alley – Drift dive through sandy channels, eagle rays and reef sharks often spotted

Overnight cruise to Tiran Island

Tiran Island Reefs

Jackson Reef – Famous for colorful walls and the chance of pelagic sightings like hammerheads

Thomas Reef – Deep walls and soft coral fans with thrilling canyon formations

Gordon Reef – Reef plateaus and the iconic Loullia wreck

Overnight cruise to Dahab

Dahab – Blue Hole & Canyon

Blue Hole – Bells Entry – Drop through a vertical chimney to enter the famous Blue Hole

The Canyon – Unique topography in an enclosed cavern setting

Ras Abu Galum – A remote and peaceful reef with a rich variety of reef life

Overnight in Dahab

Dahab Exploration & Return to Ras Mohamed

Ras Abu Galum Drift – A relaxed drift past untouched coral gardens

Eel Garden – Sloping reef filled with hundreds of garden eels

Gabr El Bint – Towering coral pinnacles and abundant reef fish

Overnight cruise toward Ras Mohamed

Ras Mohamed National Park (Final Dive Sites)

Ras Ghozlani – A colorful dive with schools of fish and healthy soft corals

Small Crack – A channel dive with napoleons and morays

Afternoon cruise back to Hurghada

Hurghada Coast – Optional Bonus Dives

Sha’ab El Erg or Fanadir – Relaxed reef dive, excellent for photography

Gota Abu Ramada – Also known as the "Aquarium" for its fish-rich waters

Evening at leisure and overnight in the marina

Farewell dinner and overnight on board

Breakfast on board, followed by check-out and transfer to the airport or hotel for onward travel.

Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

alsuraya::north-hurghada-hurghada-7-nigh.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night liveaboard itinerary explores the best of Egypt’s northern Red Sea, combining vibrant coral reefs, dramatic underwater topography, and some of the region’s most iconic dive sites. The route includes Ras Mohamed National Park, known for its rich biodiversity and stunning reef formations, and the legendary dive sites around Tiran Island, where strong currents attract large schools of fish and occasional pelagics.

The journey continues to Dahab, offering a chance to explore the unique underwater landscapes of the Blue Hole and Canyon—both famous for their striking geological features and clear waters. Along the way, divers encounter a wide variety of marine life, from reef fish and turtles to rays and the occasional reef shark, all set against the backdrop of colorful soft and hard corals.

With a balance of reef dives, wall dives, and unique underwater formations, this itinerary offers a well-rounded and immersive Red Sea experience.

The Best of Hurghada itinerary, available as a 7-night or 3-night liveaboard adventure, provides easy access to the premier dive sites of Hurghada and Northern Hurghada. This itinerary is designed for a relaxed diving experience, allowing guests to avoid crowded reefs and dive at optimal times to maximize sightings of marine life. Expect a variety of dive sites, from beautiful coral reefs to interesting wrecks, with sites chosen according to the best conditions and duration of the trip.

days.description: Guests are welcomed at Marsa Alam or Hurghada Airport and transferred to Port Ghalib Marina for check-in, cabin allocation, dinner, and overnight onboard.
Following breakfast, the cruise begins with trip briefings, equipment setup, and check dives before sailing south toward the offshore reefs of the Egyptian Red Sea.

Daedalus Reef

Up to 3 dives are scheduled around the legendary Daedalus Reef, known for its steep walls, colorful coral formations, and opportunities to encounter hammerhead sharks and other pelagic species.

Rocky Island & Zabargad

The itinerary continues to Rocky Island and Zabargad, offering dramatic drop-offs, coral gardens, caves, and excellent marine biodiversity across multiple dive sites.

Elba Reefs

Guests explore the remote reefs of the Elba Nature Reserve, including wreck dives, offshore reef systems, and untouched coral formations rarely visited by liveaboards. Dive sites are selected according to weather conditions and marine traffic.

Abu Fendira

Three dives are typically scheduled around the Abu Fendira region near St. John’s, known for its reef systems, coral formations, and diverse marine life.

St. John’s

The itinerary continues across the famous St. John’s reef systems, offering tunnels, caverns, swim-throughs, and colorful coral gardens.

Fury Shoals & Sataya

Dives are scheduled around the Fury Shoals area, including possible encounters with dolphins at Sataya Dolphin Reef depending on conditions and dolphin behavior.

Elphinstone Reef

Two or three dives are typically offered at the legendary Elphinstone Reef, known for its dramatic walls, soft corals, and pelagic encounters.

Port Ghalib Area

Final dives are usually scheduled around the Port Ghalib and Marsa Alam region, including possible turtle encounters, before returning to the marina.

Check-out after breakfast and transfer to the airport or hotel according to guests’ travel arrangements.

Please note: This is a sample itinerary and dive sites, number of dives, and route may vary depending on weather conditions, marine park regulations, and local operational requirements.

dune-longara::daedalus-elphinstone-fury-.highlightsDescription:
The Ultra South Reef Elba itinerary explores some of the most remote and least-visited dive regions of the Egyptian Red Sea, combining legendary offshore reefs, pristine southern reef systems, and the protected Elba Nature Reserve into an adventurous extended safari. From Daedalus Reef and Rocky Island to the remote reefs of Elba, Abu Fendira, St. John’s, Fury Shoals, and Elphinstone Reef, this itinerary offers exceptional diversity and exploration opportunities for experienced divers.

Divers can explore dramatic drop-offs, colorful coral gardens, caves, wrecks, offshore reef systems, and untouched southern dive sites rich in marine biodiversity. Depending on conditions and season, encounters with hammerhead sharks, dolphins, turtles, pelagic fish, reef sharks, and large schools of reef fish are possible throughout the journey.

Ideal for experienced divers seeking a longer and more adventurous Red Sea expedition, this itinerary combines remote offshore diving, pristine southern reef systems, and some of Egypt’s most spectacular underwater landscapes.

Up to 26 dives on the 11-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

dune-longara::elba-port-ghalib-port-ghal.highlightsDescription:
The Ultra South Reef Elba itinerary explores some of the most remote and least-visited dive regions of the Egyptian Red Sea, combining legendary offshore reefs, pristine southern reef systems, and the protected Elba Nature Reserve into an adventurous extended safari. From Daedalus Reef and Rocky Island to the remote reefs of Elba, Abu Fendira, St. John’s, Fury Shoals, and Elphinstone Reef, this itinerary offers exceptional diversity and exploration opportunities for experienced divers.

Divers can explore dramatic drop-offs, colorful coral gardens, caves, wrecks, offshore reef systems, and untouched southern dive sites rich in marine biodiversity. Depending on conditions and season, encounters with hammerhead sharks, dolphins, turtles, pelagic fish, reef sharks, and large schools of reef fish are possible throughout the journey.

Ideal for experienced divers seeking a longer and more adventurous Red Sea expedition, this itinerary combines remote offshore diving, pristine southern reef systems, and some of Egypt’s most spectacular underwater landscapes.

Up to 23 dives on the 10-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

dune-longara::golden-triangle-port-ghali.highlightsDescription:
The Golden Triangle itinerary explores three of the Egyptian Red Sea’s most legendary offshore dive regions: Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, and Elphinstone Reef. Known for dramatic drop-offs, strong currents, vibrant coral formations, and excellent pelagic encounters, this safari is considered one of the Red Sea’s premier itineraries for experienced divers.

Divers can explore the steep walls and colorful soft corals of the Brothers Islands, the remote offshore reef systems of Daedalus, and the iconic drop-offs of Elphinstone Reef. Depending on conditions and season, encounters with hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetips, reef sharks, tuna, barracuda, and large schools of pelagic fish are possible throughout the trip.

Ideal for advanced divers seeking thrilling drift dives and offshore reef exploration, the Golden Triangle combines some of Egypt’s most famous dive sites into one exciting Red Sea safari adventure.

Up to 15 dives on the 7-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

SS Thistlegorm

Following breakfast, the cruise begins with trip briefings, equipment setup, and check dives before sailing north toward the northern Red Sea reef systems.

Abu Nuhas

The itinerary continues with dives around the famous Abu Nuhas wreck area, known for its historic shipwrecks, coral-covered structures, and abundant marine life. Up to 3 dives may be scheduled throughout the day, including wreck and reef dives depending on conditions.

SS Thistlegorm

Guests explore the legendary SS Thistlegorm wreck, one of the world’s most famous wreck dives. Divers can discover cargo holds filled with wartime equipment including motorcycles, trucks, and military supplies, now home to thriving marine ecosystems.

Ras Mohammed National Park

Up to 3 dives are offered within the renowned Ras Mohammed National Park, famous for its dramatic walls, coral gardens, strong currents, and dense schools of reef fish. Depending on conditions, dives may also include nearby wrecks or sheltered reef sites.

Brothers Islands

Three dives are typically scheduled around the Brothers Islands, known for their steep drop-offs, colorful soft corals, and excellent pelagic encounters. Depending on conditions, divers may encounter reef sharks, tuna, barracuda, and large schools of fish. Guests may also have the opportunity to visit the Brothers lighthouse.
The vessel returns overnight toward Safaga or the embarkation marina after the final dives at the Brothers Islands. Guests can relax onboard and prepare equipment for disembarkation.

Check-out after breakfast and transfer to the airport or hotel according to guests’ travel arrangements.

Please note: This is a sample itinerary and dive sites, number of dives, and route may vary depending on weather conditions, marine park regulations, and local operational requirements.

dune-longara::north-brothers-hurghada-hu.highlightsDescription:
The North Brothers itinerary combines some of the northern Red Sea’s most famous wrecks, coral reefs, and offshore islands into an exciting week of diverse diving. From the historic wrecks of Abu Nuhas and the legendary SS Thistlegorm to the dramatic walls of Ras Mohammed and the Brothers Islands, this safari offers a mix of wreck exploration, vibrant reef systems, and pelagic encounters.

Divers can explore iconic World War II wrecks covered in marine life, colorful coral gardens, steep drop-offs, and strong current dive sites frequented by tuna, barracuda, reef sharks, and other pelagic species. The Brothers Islands are particularly renowned for their dramatic underwater topography, soft corals, and excellent shark diving opportunities.

Ideal for experienced divers seeking a varied northern Red Sea safari, this itinerary combines historical wreck diving, marine park reefs, and thrilling offshore dives across some of Egypt’s most celebrated dive sites.

Up to 15 dives on the 7-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

Up to 3 dives are scheduled around the famous reefs of Tiran Island, including sites such as Thomas Reef, Jackson Reef, and Gordon Reef. These dives are known for their steep walls, coral-covered drop-offs, strong currents, and opportunities to encounter pelagic species.

Dahab & Nabq

Guests explore the renowned dive sites of Dahab and Nabq, including the famous Blue Hole and Canyon areas. The region offers dramatic underwater landscapes, coral formations, and diverse marine life in the waters of the Sinai Peninsula.

Ras Mohammed & SS Thistlegorm

The itinerary continues with dives in Ras Mohammed National Park, known for its colorful reefs, walls, and dense schools of reef fish, before exploring the legendary SS Thistlegorm wreck, one of the world’s most iconic wreck dives.

SS Thistlegorm & Abu Nuhas

Additional dives may take place around the SS Thistlegorm area before continuing toward the Abu Nuhas wreck sites, famous for their historic shipwrecks, coral-covered structures, and abundant marine life.

Hurghada or Safaga Area

The final dives of the trip are typically scheduled around the Hurghada or Safaga reef systems before the vessel returns to the marina in the afternoon.

dune-longara::north-dahab-tiran-hurghada.highlightsDescription:
The North Ras Mohamed itinerary explores some of the northern Red Sea’s most famous wrecks, reefs, and marine parks, combining colorful coral gardens, historic wreck diving, and scenic drift dives into one classic Egyptian Red Sea safari. From Abu Nuhas and the legendary SS Thistlegorm to the dramatic reefs of Ras Mohamed and the Sinai Peninsula, this itinerary offers a diverse mix of underwater landscapes and marine life encounters.

Divers can explore coral-covered wrecks, steep walls, vibrant reef systems, and drift dives frequented by barracuda, tuna, turtles, reef sharks, and large schools of reef fish. The itinerary also includes dives around Shaab Mahmud and the Sinai coastline, known for their rich coral formations and abundant marine biodiversity.

Ideal for divers seeking a classic northern Red Sea liveaboard experience, this route combines world-famous wrecks, marine park reefs, and relaxed cruising through some of Egypt’s most iconic dive regions.

Up to 15 dives on the 7-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

dune-longara::north-tiran-hurghada-hurgh.highlightsDescription:
The Best of Egypt itinerary is an extensive Red Sea safari combining many of Egypt’s most iconic northern and southern dive regions into one unforgettable liveaboard adventure. From the reefs of Tiran, Dahab, and Ras Mohamed to the legendary wrecks of Abu Nuhas and SS Thistlegorm, and further south to Brothers, Daedalus, Rocky Island, Zabargad, St. John’s, Fury Shoals, and Elphinstone, this itinerary showcases the incredible diversity of the Egyptian Red Sea.

Divers can explore dramatic offshore reefs, historic wrecks, colorful coral gardens, caves, tunnels, steep walls, and marine park systems rich in biodiversity. Depending on conditions and season, encounters with hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetips, dolphins, manta rays, turtles, barracuda, tuna, and large schools of reef fish are possible throughout the trip.

Ideal for experienced divers seeking the ultimate Red Sea experience, this itinerary combines world-famous wreck diving, exhilarating drift dives, pelagic encounters, and some of Egypt’s most celebrated offshore reefs into one comprehensive safari adventure.

Up to 36 dives on the 14-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

dune-longara::st-johns-reefs-port-ghalib.highlightsDescription:
The Fury Shoals Dolphin Trip itinerary offers a relaxed southern Red Sea safari focused on colorful reef diving, snorkeling, dolphin encounters, and comfortable cruising through the Fury Shoals region. Centered around Sataya Dolphin Reef and the surrounding reef systems, this itinerary combines scenic coral gardens, shallow lagoons, and abundant marine life with opportunities for both divers and snorkelers to enjoy the Egyptian Red Sea.

Guests can explore the protected reefs of Fury Shoals, snorkel alongside spinner dolphins at Sataya Reef depending on conditions and dolphin behavior, and enjoy a variety of activities including diving, snorkeling, and relaxing onboard. The itinerary also includes reef systems around Sheleneyat and the Marsa Alam region, known for their vibrant coral formations and calm conditions.

Ideal for divers, snorkelers, families, and guests seeking a more relaxed Red Sea experience, this itinerary combines marine life encounters, easy reef diving, and scenic southern Red Sea landscapes.

Snorkeling, dolphin encounters, and optional diving activities are offered throughout the itinerary depending on weather conditions and guest preferences.

Following breakfast, the cruise begins with trip briefings, equipment setup, and check dives before sailing south toward the offshore reefs of the Egyptian Red Sea.

Daedalus Reef

Up to 3 dives are scheduled around the legendary Daedalus Reef, known for its steep walls, colorful coral formations, and opportunities to encounter hammerhead sharks and other pelagic species.

Rocky Island & Zabargad

The itinerary continues to Rocky Island and Zabargad, offering dramatic drop-offs, coral gardens, caves, and excellent marine biodiversity across multiple dive sites.

Elba Reefs

Guests explore the remote reefs of the Elba Nature Reserve, including wreck dives, offshore reef systems, and untouched coral formations rarely visited by liveaboards. Dive sites are selected according to weather conditions and marine traffic.

Abu Fendira

Three dives are typically scheduled around the Abu Fendira region near St. John’s, known for its reef systems, coral formations, and diverse marine life.

St. John’s

The itinerary continues across the famous St. John’s reef systems, offering tunnels, caverns, swim-throughs, and colorful coral gardens.

Fury Shoals & Sataya

Dives are scheduled around the Fury Shoals area, including possible encounters with dolphins at Sataya Dolphin Reef depending on conditions and dolphin behavior.

Elphinstone Reef

Two or three dives are typically offered at the legendary Elphinstone Reef, known for its dramatic walls, soft corals, and pelagic encounters.

Check-out after breakfast followed by transfers to the airport or hotel according to guests’ travel arrangements.

Please note: This is a sample itinerary and dive sites, number of dives, and route may vary depending on weather conditions, marine park regulations, and local operational requirements.

dune-silky::elba-port-ghalib-port-ghalib.highlightsDescription:
The Ultra South Reef Elba itinerary explores some of the most remote and least-visited dive regions of the Egyptian Red Sea, combining legendary offshore reefs, pristine southern reef systems, and the protected Elba Nature Reserve into an adventurous extended safari. From Daedalus Reef and Rocky Island to the remote reefs of Elba, Abu Fendira, St. John’s, Fury Shoals, and Elphinstone Reef, this itinerary offers exceptional diversity and exploration opportunities for experienced divers.

Divers can explore dramatic drop-offs, colorful coral gardens, caves, wrecks, offshore reef systems, and untouched southern dive sites rich in marine biodiversity. Depending on conditions and season, encounters with hammerhead sharks, dolphins, turtles, pelagic fish, reef sharks, and large schools of reef fish are possible throughout the journey.

Ideal for experienced divers seeking a longer and more adventurous Red Sea expedition, this itinerary combines remote offshore diving, pristine southern reef systems, and some of Egypt’s most spectacular underwater landscapes.

Up to 23 dives on the 10-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

Following breakfast, the cruise begins with trip briefings, equipment setup, and check dives before sailing north toward the Sinai Peninsula and northern Red Sea reefs.

Tiran Reefs

Guests explore the famous reefs of Tiran Island, including sites such as Thomas Reef, Jackson Reef, and Gordon Reef, known for dramatic walls, strong currents, coral formations, and pelagic encounters.

Dahab & Nabq

Dives are scheduled around Dahab and Nabq, including the famous Blue Hole and Canyon areas, offering dramatic underwater landscapes, coral plateaus, and diverse marine life.

Ras Mohamed & SS Thistlegorm

The itinerary continues with dives in Ras Mohamed National Park before exploring the legendary SS Thistlegorm wreck, one of the world’s most iconic wreck dives.

SS Thistlegorm & Gubal

Additional dives are typically scheduled around the SS Thistlegorm before continuing toward the Gubal area for reef and wreck diving.

Abu Nuhas & Hurghada

Guests explore the famous Abu Nuhas wreck sites before continuing toward the reef systems surrounding Hurghada.

Safaga

The itinerary continues south toward Safaga, known for sites such as Panorama Reef and Abu Kafan, featuring colorful reefs, steep drop-offs, and diverse marine life.

Brothers Islands

Up to 3 dives are offered around the Brothers Islands, famous for their dramatic walls, soft corals, and excellent shark diving opportunities.

Daedalus Reef

Guests explore the legendary Daedalus Reef, known for its steep walls, coral formations, and opportunities to encounter hammerhead sharks and other pelagic species.

Rocky Island & Zabargad

Three dives are typically scheduled around Rocky Island and Zabargad, offering dramatic drop-offs, coral gardens, caves, and abundant marine biodiversity.

St. John’s

The itinerary continues to the famous St. John’s reef systems, known for tunnels, caverns, swim-throughs, and vibrant coral formations.

Fury Shoals & Wadi Gemal

Dives are scheduled around the Fury Shoals area, including the possibility of snorkeling with dolphins at Sataya Dolphin Reef before continuing north toward Wadi Gemal.

Elphinstone Reef

Two morning dives are typically scheduled at Elphinstone Reef, known for its dramatic walls, soft corals, and pelagic encounters, before returning to Port Ghalib Marina in the afternoon.

Check-out after breakfast and transfer to the airport or hotel according to guests’ travel arrangements.

dune-silky::golden-triangle-hurghada-por.highlightsDescription:
The Best of Egypt itinerary is an extensive Red Sea safari combining many of Egypt’s most iconic northern and southern dive regions into one unforgettable liveaboard adventure. From the reefs of Tiran, Dahab, and Ras Mohamed to the legendary wrecks of Abu Nuhas and SS Thistlegorm, and further south to Brothers, Daedalus, Rocky Island, Zabargad, St. John’s, Fury Shoals, and Elphinstone, this itinerary showcases the incredible diversity of the Egyptian Red Sea.

Divers can explore dramatic offshore reefs, historic wrecks, colorful coral gardens, caves, tunnels, steep walls, and marine park systems rich in biodiversity. Depending on conditions and season, encounters with hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetips, dolphins, manta rays, turtles, barracuda, tuna, and large schools of reef fish are possible throughout the trip.

Ideal for experienced divers seeking the ultimate Red Sea experience, this itinerary combines world-famous wreck diving, exhilarating drift dives, pelagic encounters, and some of Egypt’s most celebrated offshore reefs into one comprehensive safari adventure.

Up to 36 dives on the 14-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

The Mixed South itinerary explores some of the Egyptian Red Sea’s most iconic offshore reefs and southern dive regions, combining dramatic walls, vibrant coral gardens, and excellent pelagic diving opportunities. From the legendary Daedalus Reef and Elphinstone Reef to the remote islands of Rocky and Zabargad, this safari offers a varied and adventurous diving experience across the southern Red Sea.

Ideal for experienced divers seeking a classic southern Red Sea safari, this route combines remote offshore reefs, exciting drift dives, and some of Egypt’s most renowned dive sites.

Up to 15 dives on the 7-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

Elphinstone Reef

Port Ghalib Area

SS Thistlegorm

Ras Mohammed National Park

Up to 3 dives are offered within the renowned Ras Mohammed National Park, famous for its dramatic walls, coral gardens, strong currents, and dense schools of reef fish. Depending on conditions, dives may also include nearby wrecks or sheltered reef sites.

Brothers Islands

The vessel returns overnight toward Safaga or the embarkation marina after the final dives at the Brothers Islands. Guests can relax onboard and prepare equipment for disembarkation.

dune-silky::north-brothers-port-ghalib-h.highlightsDescription:
The North Brothers itinerary combines some of the northern Red Sea’s most famous wrecks, coral reefs, and offshore islands into an exciting week of diverse diving. From the historic wrecks of Abu Nuhas and the legendary SS Thistlegorm to the dramatic walls of Ras Mohammed and the Brothers Islands, this safari offers a mix of wreck exploration, vibrant reef systems, and pelagic encounters.

Divers can explore iconic World War II wrecks covered in marine life, colorful coral gardens, steep drop-offs, and strong current dive sites frequented by tuna, barracuda, reef sharks, and other pelagic species. The Brothers Islands are particularly renowned for their dramatic underwater topography, soft corals, and excellent shark diving opportunities.

Ideal for experienced divers seeking a varied northern Red Sea safari, this itinerary combines historical wreck diving, marine park reefs, and thrilling offshore dives across some of Egypt’s most celebrated dive sites.

Up to 15 dives on the 7-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

dune-titan::daedalus-elphinstone-fury-sh.highlightsDescription:
The Ultra South Reef Elba itinerary explores some of the most remote and least-visited dive regions of the Egyptian Red Sea, combining legendary offshore reefs, pristine southern reef systems, and the protected Elba Nature Reserve into an adventurous extended safari. From Daedalus Reef and Rocky Island to the remote reefs of Elba, Abu Fendira, St. John’s, Fury Shoals, and Elphinstone Reef, this itinerary offers exceptional diversity and exploration opportunities for experienced divers.

Divers can explore dramatic drop-offs, colorful coral gardens, caves, wrecks, offshore reef systems, and untouched southern dive sites rich in marine biodiversity. Depending on conditions and season, encounters with hammerhead sharks, dolphins, turtles, pelagic fish, reef sharks, and large schools of reef fish are possible throughout the journey.

Ideal for experienced divers seeking a longer and more adventurous Red Sea expedition, this itinerary combines remote offshore diving, pristine southern reef systems, and some of Egypt’s most spectacular underwater landscapes.

Up to 26 dives on the 11-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

Following breakfast, the cruise begins with trip briefings, equipment setup, and check dives before sailing offshore toward the Brothers Islands.

Brothers Islands

Up to 3 dives are scheduled around the famous Brothers Islands, known for their dramatic walls, soft corals, and excellent pelagic diving opportunities. Depending on conditions, divers may encounter reef sharks, tuna, barracuda, and large schools of fish.

Daedalus Reef

The itinerary continues to the legendary Daedalus Reef, where up to 3 dives per day may be offered around steep drop-offs and vibrant coral formations. Daedalus is particularly famous for encounters with hammerhead sharks and other pelagic species. Guests may also have the opportunity to visit the Daedalus lighthouse.

Elphinstone Reef

Two or three dives are typically scheduled at Elphinstone Reef, known for its dramatic walls, colorful soft corals, and frequent pelagic encounters. Depending on conditions, additional dives or night dives may also be offered in nearby protected areas.
One or two final dives are usually scheduled before the vessel returns to the marina in the afternoon.

Check-out after breakfast and transfer to the airport or hotel according to guests’ travel arrangements.

After breakfast, the cruise begins with safety and itinerary briefings. Diving certifications, logbooks, and insurance documents are checked before departure.

Check dives are completed at selected sites near Port Ghalib or Marsa Alam before the vessel begins sailing north.

Brothers Islands

Up to three dives are scheduled around Big Brother and Small Brother, known for their dramatic walls, strong currents, colorful soft corals, and potential pelagic encounters.

Depending on local authorization and operational conditions, a visit to the lighthouse on Big Brother may also be arranged.

Safaga

Diving continues around selected reefs or wrecks in the Safaga region. Sites are chosen according to weather, sea conditions, and marine traffic before the vessel continues north.

Ras Mohamed National Park

Two dives are usually scheduled around the spectacular walls and reef systems of Ras Mohamed National Park. A third dive may take place on a coral garden or wreck, with a possible night dive depending on the selected site and conditions.

SS Thistlegorm

The itinerary continues to the famous SS Thistlegorm, a World War II cargo ship containing motorcycles, trucks, railway equipment, and other wartime supplies.

Further dives may be scheduled in the surrounding area before the vessel continues toward the northern wreck sites.

Abu Nuhas & Hurghada

The final dives are usually scheduled around Abu Nuhas or selected reefs near Hurghada. Abu Nuhas is renowned for its historic shipwrecks and abundant marine life.

Following the final dives, the vessel continues to Hurghada and arrives at the marina in the afternoon.

Check-out after breakfast and transfer to the airport or hotel according to guests’ travel arrangements.

Please note: This is a sample itinerary. Dive sites, number of dives, and route may vary depending on weather and sea conditions, marine park regulations, diver experience, marine traffic, and local operational requirements.

dune-titan::north-brothers-hurghada-hurg.highlightsDescription:
The North Brothers itinerary combines some of the northern Red Sea’s most famous wrecks, coral reefs, and offshore islands into an exciting week of diverse diving. From the historic wrecks of Abu Nuhas and the legendary SS Thistlegorm to the dramatic walls of Ras Mohammed and the Brothers Islands, this safari offers a mix of wreck exploration, vibrant reef systems, and pelagic encounters.

Divers can explore iconic World War II wrecks covered in marine life, colorful coral gardens, steep drop-offs, and strong current dive sites frequented by tuna, barracuda, reef sharks, and other pelagic species. The Brothers Islands are particularly renowned for their dramatic underwater topography, soft corals, and excellent shark diving opportunities.

Ideal for experienced divers seeking a varied northern Red Sea safari, this itinerary combines historical wreck diving, marine park reefs, and thrilling offshore dives across some of Egypt’s most celebrated dive sites.

Up to 15 dives on the 7-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

Following breakfast, the cruise begins with trip briefings, equipment setup, and check dives before sailing north toward the northern Red Sea reef systems.

Abu Nuhas

The itinerary continues with dives around the famous Abu Nuhas wreck area, known for its historic shipwrecks, coral-covered structures, and abundant marine life. Up to 3 dives may be scheduled throughout the day, including wreck and reef dives depending on conditions.

SS Thistlegorm

Guests explore the legendary SS Thistlegorm wreck, one of the world’s most famous wreck dives. Divers can discover cargo holds filled with wartime equipment including motorcycles, trucks, and military supplies, now home to thriving marine ecosystems.

Ras Mohammed National Park

Up to 3 dives are offered within the renowned Ras Mohammed National Park, famous for its dramatic walls, coral gardens, strong currents, and dense schools of reef fish. Depending on conditions, dives may also include nearby wrecks or sheltered reef sites.

Brothers Islands

Three dives are typically scheduled around the Brothers Islands, known for their steep drop-offs, colorful soft corals, and excellent pelagic encounters. Depending on conditions, divers may encounter reef sharks, tuna, barracuda, and large schools of fish. Guests may also have the opportunity to visit the Brothers lighthouse.
The vessel returns overnight toward Safaga or the embarkation marina after the final dives at the Brothers Islands. Guests can relax onboard and prepare equipment for disembarkation.

Check-out after breakfast and transfer to the airport or hotel according to guests’ travel arrangements.

Please note: This is a sample itinerary and dive sites, number of dives, and route may vary depending on weather conditions, marine park regulations, and local operational requirements.

Tiran Reefs

Up to 3 dives are scheduled around the famous reefs of Tiran Island, including sites such as Thomas Reef, Jackson Reef, and Gordon Reef. These dives are known for their steep walls, coral-covered drop-offs, strong currents, and opportunities to encounter pelagic species.

Dahab & Nabq

Guests explore the renowned dive sites of Dahab and Nabq, including the famous Blue Hole and Canyon areas. The region offers dramatic underwater landscapes, coral formations, and diverse marine life in the waters of the Sinai Peninsula.

Ras Mohammed & SS Thistlegorm

The itinerary continues with dives in Ras Mohammed National Park, known for its colorful reefs, walls, and dense schools of reef fish, before exploring the legendary SS Thistlegorm wreck, one of the world’s most iconic wreck dives.

SS Thistlegorm & Abu Nuhas

Additional dives may take place around the SS Thistlegorm area before continuing toward the Abu Nuhas wreck sites, famous for their historic shipwrecks, coral-covered structures, and abundant marine life.

Hurghada or Safaga Area

dune-titan::north-ras-mohamed-hurghada-h.highlightsDescription:
The North Tiran itinerary combines some of the northern Red Sea’s most famous reefs, wrecks, and drift dives into a diverse week of underwater exploration. From the wrecks of Abu Nuhas and the legendary SS Thistlegorm to the dramatic walls of Tiran Island and the reefs of Ras Mohamed, this safari offers a varied mix of coral gardens, steep drop-offs, pelagic encounters, and historical wreck diving.

Divers can explore renowned sites such as Jackson Reef, Thomas Reef, Yolanda Reef, Giftun Island, and the Salem Express wreck near Safaga. Depending on conditions, encounters with reef sharks, barracuda, tuna, turtles, rays, and large schools of reef fish are possible throughout the trip.

Ideal for divers seeking a classic northern Red Sea liveaboard adventure, this itinerary combines iconic wreck dives, scenic drift diving, and vibrant reef systems across some of Egypt’s most celebrated dive regions.

Up to 15 dives on the 7-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

days.description: Guests are welcomed at the designated airport and transferred to the embarkation marina for check-in, cabin allocation, dinner, and overnight onboard.

Check Dive / Soma Bay

Check dive in sheltered conditions followed by a second reef dive. Overnight near Soma Bay.

Safaga Walls / Sha’ab Sheer

Morning wall dives in Safaga followed by an afternoon dive through Sha’ab Sheer coral gardens.

Salem Express / Sha’ab Sheer

Dives at the Salem Express wreck and Sha’ab Sheer, with chances to encounter spinner dolphins. Night dive.

Panorama Reef / Middle Reef

Exploration of Panorama Reef’s coral-covered walls and Middle Reef.

Coral Gardens / Tobia Arbaa

Morning reef dives with gorgonians and hard coral gardens followed by a night dive at Tobia Arbaa.

Gamul Soraya / Tobia Kebir

Final dives among schooling fish, garden eels, and possible eagle ray sightings before returning to Hurghada.

Check-out after breakfast and transfer to the airport or hotel according to guests’ travel arrangements.

dune-titan::north-tiran-hurghada-hurghad.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night Red Sea itinerary explores the legendary reefs and wrecks of the Safaga region, combining colorful coral gardens, dramatic drop-offs, exciting drift dives, and iconic wreck exploration. Diving around Soma Bay and Safaga offers excellent biodiversity, frequent encounters with dolphins, turtles, eagle rays, and schooling fish, together with some of Egypt’s most beautiful reef systems.

Highlights of the itinerary include the famous Salem Express wreck, the steep walls of Panorama Reef, the coral gardens of Sha’ab Sheer, and the thriving marine life around Tobia Arbaa and Tobia Kebir. Divers can expect a mix of reef dives, wall dives, drift dives, and night dives across a variety of underwater landscapes suitable for both underwater photography and marine life encounters.

Following breakfast, the cruise begins with trip briefings, equipment setup, and check dives before sailing north toward the northern Red Sea reef systems.

Abu Nuhas

The itinerary continues with dives around the famous Abu Nuhas wreck area, known for its historic shipwrecks, coral-covered structures, and abundant marine life. Up to 3 dives may be scheduled throughout the day, including wreck and reef dives depending on conditions.

SS Thistlegorm

Guests explore the legendary SS Thistlegorm wreck, one of the world’s most famous wreck dives. Divers can discover cargo holds filled with wartime equipment including motorcycles, trucks, and military supplies, now home to thriving marine ecosystems.

Ras Mohammed National Park

Up to 3 dives are offered within the renowned Ras Mohammed National Park, famous for its dramatic walls, coral gardens, strong currents, and dense schools of reef fish. Depending on conditions, dives may also include nearby wrecks or sheltered reef sites.

Brothers Islands

Three dives are typically scheduled around the Brothers Islands, known for their steep drop-offs, colorful soft corals, and excellent pelagic encounters. Depending on conditions, divers may encounter reef sharks, tuna, barracuda, and large schools of fish. Guests may also have the opportunity to visit the Brothers lighthouse.
The vessel returns overnight toward Safaga or the embarkation marina after the final dives at the Brothers Islands. Guests can relax onboard and prepare equipment for disembarkation.

Check-out after breakfast and transfer to the airport or hotel according to guests’ travel arrangements.

Please note: This is a sample itinerary and dive sites, number of dives, and route may vary depending on weather conditions, marine park regulations, and local operational requirements.

dune-titan::st-johns-reefs-port-ghalib-h.highlightsDescription:
The North Ras Mohamed itinerary explores some of the northern Red Sea’s most famous wrecks, reefs, and marine parks, combining colorful coral gardens, historic wreck diving, and scenic drift dives into one classic Egyptian Red Sea safari. From Abu Nuhas and the legendary SS Thistlegorm to the dramatic reefs of Ras Mohamed and the Sinai Peninsula, this itinerary offers a diverse mix of underwater landscapes and marine life encounters.

Divers can explore coral-covered wrecks, steep walls, vibrant reef systems, and drift dives frequented by barracuda, tuna, turtles, reef sharks, and large schools of reef fish. The itinerary also includes dives around Shaab Mahmud and the Sinai coastline, known for their rich coral formations and abundant marine biodiversity.

Ideal for divers seeking a classic northern Red Sea liveaboard experience, this route combines world-famous wrecks, marine park reefs, and relaxed cruising through some of Egypt’s most iconic dive regions.

Up to 15 dives on the 7-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

Following breakfast, the cruise begins with trip briefings, equipment setup, and check dives before sailing south toward the offshore reefs of the Egyptian Red Sea.

Daedalus Reef

Up to 3 dives per day are scheduled around the legendary Daedalus Reef, known for its steep walls, vibrant coral formations, and excellent pelagic diving opportunities. Divers may encounter hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetips, tuna, and large schools of reef fish while exploring different sections of the reef. Guests may also have the opportunity to visit the Daedalus lighthouse between dives.

Fury Shoals

The itinerary continues to the Fury Shoals region, home to colorful coral gardens, tunnels, caverns, and protected reef systems. Dives may include sites such as Sataya Dolphin Reef, Abu Galawa, and nearby coral formations rich in marine biodiversity. Snorkeling opportunities with spinner dolphins may also be possible depending on conditions and dolphin behavior.

Elphinstone Reef

Two morning dives are typically scheduled at the famous Elphinstone Reef, known for its dramatic walls, soft corals, and frequent pelagic encounters. After diving, the vessel returns to Port Ghalib Marina in the afternoon.

Check-out after breakfast and transfer to the airport or hotel according to guests’ travel arrangements.

Please note: This is a sample itinerary and dive sites, number of dives, and route may vary depending on weather conditions, marine park regulations, and local operational requirements.

dune-titan::st-johns-reefs-port-ghalib-h.highlightsDescription:
The Daedalus, Elphinstone & Fury Shoals itinerary combines three of the Egyptian Red Sea’s most iconic dive regions into an exciting week of offshore reefs, vibrant coral gardens, and pelagic encounters. From the dramatic walls of Daedalus Reef to the colorful reef systems of Fury Shoals and the legendary drop-offs of Elphinstone Reef, this safari offers a diverse and adventurous diving experience.

Daedalus Reef is famous for its steep walls, strong currents, and opportunities to encounter hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetips, manta rays, and other pelagic species. Fury Shoals offers a completely different atmosphere, with protected coral gardens, swim-throughs, caves, and the possibility to snorkel alongside spinner dolphins at Sataya Dolphin Reef. The itinerary concludes with dives at the world-renowned Elphinstone Reef, known for its soft corals, dramatic drop-offs, and frequent shark encounters.

Ideal for divers seeking a classic southern Red Sea safari, this route combines thrilling drift dives, vibrant reef systems, and some of Egypt’s most celebrated dive sites.

Up to 15 dives on the 7-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

dune-titan::st-johns-reefs-port-ghalib-h.highlightsDescription:
The St. John’s Reefs itinerary explores the remote southern reef systems of the Egyptian Red Sea, combining colorful coral gardens, tunnels, caverns, and pristine reef formations with the famous Fury Shoals region and the waters surrounding Marsa Alam. Known for its rich biodiversity and scenic underwater landscapes, this itinerary offers a relaxed yet adventurous southern Red Sea safari experience.

Divers can explore the renowned St. John’s reef systems, including dramatic walls, swim-throughs, caves, and coral plateaus rich in marine life. The itinerary also includes dives around Fury Shoals and Sataya Dolphin Reef, where encounters with dolphins may be possible depending on conditions and dolphin behavior.

Ideal for divers seeking scenic reef diving and vibrant southern Red Sea ecosystems, this itinerary combines remote reefs, colorful coral formations, and relaxed cruising through some of Egypt’s most beautiful dive regions.

Following breakfast, the cruise begins with trip briefings, equipment setup, and check dives before sailing south toward the offshore reefs of the Egyptian Red Sea.

Daedalus Reef

Up to 3 dives are scheduled around the famous Daedalus Reef, known for its steep walls, vibrant coral formations, and opportunities to encounter hammerhead sharks and other pelagic species. Guests may also have the opportunity to visit the Daedalus lighthouse.

Rocky Island & Zabargad

The itinerary continues to the remote islands of Rocky and Zabargad, offering dramatic walls, colorful coral gardens, caves, and excellent marine biodiversity. Up to 3 dives are planned, with dive sites selected according to sea conditions and marine traffic.

St. John’s Reefs

Guests explore the renowned St. John’s area, famous for its reef systems, swim-throughs, tunnels, coral formations, and diverse marine life. Up to 3 dives are typically offered throughout the day.

Fury Shoals & Wadi Gemal Area

The cruise gradually heads north with dives in the Fury Shoals region, including the possibility of encounters with dolphins in Sataya (Dolphin House). The final dive of the day may take place in the Wadi Gemal area during dusk or as a night dive where conditions permit.

Elphinstone Reef

Two morning dives are typically scheduled at the legendary Elphinstone Reef, known for its dramatic drop-offs, soft corals, and pelagic encounters. After diving, the vessel returns to Port Ghalib Marina in the afternoon.

Check-out after breakfast and transfer to the airport or hotel according to guests’ travel arrangements.

Please note: This is a sample itinerary and dive sites, number of dives, and route may vary depending on weather conditions, marine park regulations, and local operational requirements.

The Mixed South itinerary explores some of the Egyptian Red Sea’s most iconic offshore reefs and southern dive regions, combining dramatic walls, vibrant coral gardens, and excellent pelagic diving opportunities. From the legendary Daedalus Reef and Elphinstone Reef to the remote islands of Rocky and Zabargad, this safari offers a varied and adventurous diving experience across the southern Red Sea.

Divers may encounter hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetips, dolphins, tuna, barracuda, and large schools of reef fish while exploring steep drop-offs, colorful hard coral formations, caverns, and pristine reef systems. The itinerary also includes the famous St. John’s and Fury Shoals areas, known for their scenic reefs, swim-throughs, and diverse marine life.

Ideal for experienced divers seeking a classic southern Red Sea safari, this route combines remote offshore reefs, exciting drift dives, and some of Egypt’s most renowned dive sites.

Up to 15 dives on the 7-night itinerary, with additional dives possible depending on weather conditions and flight schedules.

After breakfast, the cruise begins with general and safety briefings. Diving certifications, logbooks, and insurance documents are checked before departure.

The first snorkeling or diving session is scheduled near the marina, followed by a second activity farther south. The vessel then continues overnight toward the Sataya area.

Sataya Dolphin Reef & Fury Shoals

Guests receive a briefing on how to interact responsibly with dolphins before the first snorkeling excursion inside the Sataya lagoon.

Certified divers may be offered a dive outside the lagoon, where scuba diving is permitted. Additional activities may include snorkeling along the reef, swimming, introductory dives, or further dolphin encounters, depending on conditions and guests’ preferences.

Fury Shoals

The vessel explores different sites around Fury Shoals, with a flexible program of diving, snorkeling, swimming, and possible further visits to the Sataya lagoon.

Certified divers can explore colorful coral gardens and reefs rich in Red Sea marine life. The exact activities and sites are selected according to weather conditions, guest preferences, and operational considerations.

Fury Shoals & Sheleneyat

A final dolphin excursion and a dive for certified divers may be organized in the morning. The vessel then sails north for approximately five to six hours toward Sheleneyat, where an additional snorkeling excursion may be offered.

Marsa Alam

One or two final diving or snorkeling sessions are usually scheduled in the Marsa Alam area. The vessel returns to Port Ghalib in the early afternoon.

Check-out after breakfast and transfer to the airport or hotel according to guests’ travel arrangements.

Please note: This is a sample itinerary. Dive and snorkeling sites, activities, number of sessions, and route may vary depending on weather conditions, dolphin behavior, guest preferences, flight schedules, and local operational requirements. Dolphin encounters cannot be guaranteed.

ghazala-adventure::brothers-daedalus-elp.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary takes divers to four of the Red Sea’s most iconic offshore sites: Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, Elphinstone, and Abu Dabab. Known for their dramatic drop-offs, vibrant coral formations, and high chance of shark sightings, these sites offer unforgettable diving for advanced divers.

The Brothers Islands feature steep walls, rich marine life, and two famous wrecks, Numidia and Aida, along with regular encounters with oceanic whitetips, threshers, and hammerheads. Daedalus Reef is a remote seamount where schooling hammerheads and manta rays are often spotted. Elphinstone impresses with vertical walls, soft coral gardens, and seasonal oceanic whitetip encounters. Abu Dabab offers a gentler finale, with calm reefs full of life.

Although wildlife sightings vary by season, the route offers strong year-round potential for shark encounters and consistently excellent diving. Divers must be Advanced Open Water certified or have a Deep Dive Specialty, both can be completed onboard.

ghazala-adventure::brothers-daedalus-elp.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary offers a balanced mix of Red Sea highlights, combining iconic wrecks with colorful reef systems. Divers explore the famous SS Thistlegorm, a WWII wreck rich in history and marine life, and Abu Nuhas Reef, home to wrecks like the Giannis D and Carnatic surrounded by healthy coral.

The Straits of Tiran provide dramatic drift dives at Jackson, Thomas, and Woodhouse Reefs, while Little Gubal Island offers a peaceful mix of wreck and reef with frequent sightings of turtles and dolphins. Ras Mohamed National Park delivers powerful dives at Shark Reef and Yolanda Reef, known for schooling fish and striking topography.

This route includes both popular and lesser-known sites, offering variety and consistent underwater excitement—ideal for divers who enjoy both wreck exploration and thriving reef life.

ghazala-adventure::brothers-daedalus-elp.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night liveaboard safari in the deep south of the Red Sea is designed for divers seeking adventure, biodiversity, and remote sites far from the crowds. Departing from and returning to Port Ghalib, the itinerary combines three of Egypt’s most spectacular areas: Daedalus Reef, Rocky Island, and the St Johns archipelago.

Daedalus Reef, a remote offshore pinnacle, is renowned for its steep coral-covered walls and the chance to encounter schooling hammerheads, grey reef sharks, and other pelagic species. Further south, Rocky Island offers thrilling dives along sheer drop-offs with pristine corals and an impressive variety of marine life.

The journey continues to St Johns, a maze of reefs, pinnacles, and caverns teeming with reef fish, napoleon wrasse, turtles, dolphins, and occasional manta rays. Its unique underwater landscapes, with passages and caverns illuminated by shafts of light, make these dives among the most atmospheric in the Red Sea.

Departing from and returning to Port Ghalib, the itinerary combines three of Egypt’s most spectacular areas: Daedalus Reef, Rocky Island, and the St Johns archipelago.

Daedalus Reef, a remote offshore pinnacle, is renowned for its steep coral-covered walls and the chance to encounter schooling hammerheads, grey reef sharks, and other pelagic species. Further south, Rocky Island offers thrilling dives along sheer drop-offs with pristine corals and an impressive variety of marine life.

The journey continues to St Johns, a maze of reefs, pinnacles, and caverns teeming with reef fish, napoleon wrasse, turtles, dolphins, and occasional manta rays. Its unique underwater landscapes, with passages and caverns illuminated by shafts of light, make these dives among the most atmospheric in the Red Sea.

With an average of 3–4 dives per day, including night dives where permitted, this trip combines big pelagic encounters with untouched reefs and stunning underwater scenery, making it ideal for experienced divers in search of excitement and natural beauty.

ghazala-adventure::north-safaga-area-hur.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary takes divers to four of the Red Sea’s most iconic offshore sites: Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, Elphinstone, and Abu Dabab. Known for their dramatic drop-offs, vibrant coral formations, and high chance of shark sightings, these sites offer unforgettable diving for advanced divers.

The Brothers Islands feature steep walls, rich marine life, and two famous wrecks, Numidia and Aida, along with regular encounters with oceanic whitetips, threshers, and hammerheads. Daedalus Reef is a remote seamount where schooling hammerheads and manta rays are often spotted. Elphinstone impresses with vertical walls, soft coral gardens, and seasonal oceanic whitetip encounters. Abu Dabab offers a gentler finale, with calm reefs full of life.

Although wildlife sightings vary by season, the route offers strong year-round potential for shark encounters and consistently excellent diving. Divers must be Advanced Open Water certified or have a Deep Dive Specialty, both can be completed onboard.

ghazala-adventure::north-tiran-dahab-hur.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night safari combines some of the Red Sea’s most iconic northern wrecks with the rich reefs of Safaga, offering a perfect balance of history, adventure, and marine biodiversity.

Departing from Hurghada, the route typically includes legendary wrecks such as the SS Thistlegorm, Giannis D, Carnatic, and Chrisoula K at Abu Nuhas, along with the Dunraven near Shaab Mahmoud. These wrecks, teeming with marine life, are a paradise for photographers and history enthusiasts alike.

The itinerary also features spectacular reef diving in Ras Mohamed National Park, known for its dramatic drop-offs, huge schools of fish, and pristine coral gardens. Continuing southwards, you will explore Safaga’s most celebrated sites, including Panorama Reef, Middle Reef, and the famous Salem Express wreck. Safaga is renowned for its healthy hard and soft corals, excellent visibility, and encounters with pelagics and macro life.

With an average of 3–4 dives per day, including night dives where permitted, this trip offers diverse diving opportunities for all certified levels, from vibrant reefs and dramatic walls to some of the Red Sea’s most iconic wrecks.
