ghazala-adventure::north-wrecks-reefs-hu.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary combines the dramatic reef walls of the Brothers Islands with the iconic wrecks and vibrant coral gardens of the northern Red Sea. The Brothers are renowned for steep drop-offs, colourful soft corals, and seasonal sightings of oceanic whitetips, hammerheads, threshers, and manta rays. The Numidia wreck, perched on the reef since 1901, adds historical interest and marine biodiversity.

In the north, divers explore the legendary SS Thistlegorm—one of the world’s most famous WWII wrecks—and the Abu Nuhas ship graveyard, home to Giannis D and Carnatic. Little Gubal Island offers a mix of easy reef and wreck dives, with sites like the Barge Wreck known for their marine life and photographic appeal.

Ras Mohamed National Park delivers high-energy dives at Shark Reef and Yolanda Reef, teeming with schooling fish and towering corals. This itinerary offers a rich mix of wrecks, reef exploration, and the potential for thrilling pelagic encounters throughout the year.

ghazala-adventure::north-wrecks-reefs-hu.highlightsDescription:
The Get Wrecked itinerary is designed for divers passionate about shipwreck exploration, offering access to some of the Red Sea’s most iconic and historically rich wrecks. Highlights include the world-famous SS Thistlegorm, the Rosalie Moller, and the four wrecks of Abu Nuhas—Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, and Kimon M—each with its own story and marine life.

Further south, the itinerary may include the Salem Express, one of the region’s most talked-about wrecks, and Yolanda Reef in Ras Mohamed National Park, where the scattered remains of the Yolanda still rest. Sites like the Ulysses and other lesser-known wrecks are also part of the route, offering a mix of shallow, deep, and advanced-level dives.

This trip blends history, exploration, and vibrant marine ecosystems, making it a top choice for divers eager to experience the best of the Red Sea’s underwater heritage.

ghazala-adventure::north-wrecks-reefs-hu.highlightsDescription:

The journey continues to the Strait of Tiran, where sites like Jackson, Thomas, and Gordon Reef offer colorful drift dives with the Sinai Mountains in the distance. In Dahab, divers can explore dramatic underwater features like the Canyon, a favorite for its structure and depth.

This itinerary is suitable for divers with Advanced Open Water certification or those completing the Deep Dive Specialty course onboard, allowing full access to the most rewarding sites on the route.

ghazala-explorer::brothers-daedalus-elph.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary takes divers to four of the Red Sea’s most iconic offshore sites: Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, Elphinstone, and Abu Dabab. Known for their dramatic drop-offs, vibrant coral formations, and high chance of shark sightings, these sites offer unforgettable diving for advanced divers.

The Brothers Islands feature steep walls, rich marine life, and two famous wrecks—Numidia and Aida—along with regular encounters with oceanic whitetips, threshers, and hammerheads. Daedalus Reef is a remote seamount where schooling hammerheads and manta rays are often spotted. Elphinstone impresses with vertical walls, soft coral gardens, and seasonal oceanic whitetip encounters. Abu Dabab offers a gentler finale, with calm reefs full of life.

Although wildlife sightings vary by season, the route offers strong year-round potential for shark encounters and consistently excellent diving. Divers must be Advanced Open Water certified or have a Deep Dive Specialty—both can be completed onboard.

Although wildlife sightings vary by season, the route offers strong year-round potential for shark encounters and consistently excellent diving. Divers must be Advanced Open Water certified or have a Deep Dive Specialty—both can be completed onboard.

Following breakfast, the cruise begins with safety briefings, equipment setup, and check dives before sailing south toward the Deep South reef systems.

St John’s Reefs

Up to 3–4 dives per day are scheduled around the St John’s reef system. The area offers coral gardens, walls, pinnacles, tunnels, caverns, and swim-throughs, including the distinctive formations of St John’s Caves.

Dive sites are selected according to weather conditions, marine traffic, and diver experience. Night dives may be offered where local regulations and conditions permit.

St John’s & Fury Shoals

The vessel gradually begins heading north, with further dives around St John’s before continuing toward Fury Shoals. Diving may include colorful coral gardens, sheltered reefs, and sites with the possibility of turtle or dolphin encounters.
One or two final dives are scheduled in the morning before the vessel returns to Port Ghalib.

Check-out after breakfast and disembarkation by 10:00.

Please note: This is a sample itinerary. The number of dives, dive sites, and route may change due to weather conditions, local regulations, marine traffic, and other unforeseen operational factors. Marine-life encounters cannot be guaranteed.

ghazala-explorer::brothers-daedalus-elph.highlightsDescription:
This Deep South itinerary explores the remote reefs of St John’s and Fury Shoals, among the most scenic diving areas in the southern Egyptian Red Sea.

The St John’s reef system is known for colorful coral gardens, dramatic reef formations, tunnels, caverns, and swim-throughs. Sites such as St John’s Caves offer unusual underwater landscapes, while the surrounding reefs attract turtles, reef fish, rays, and occasional pelagic species.

Farther north, Fury Shoals features sheltered lagoons, pinnacles, coral gardens, and shallow reefs rich in marine life. Depending on conditions and the final route, the itinerary may also include Sataya Dolphin Reef, where encounters with dolphins may be possible but cannot be guaranteed.

With a combination of caves, walls, coral gardens, and relaxed reef diving, this itinerary is ideal for divers wishing to explore the quieter and more remote regions of Egypt’s southern Red Sea.

Rocky Island and Zabargad offer lush reefs, dramatic drop-offs, and abundant marine life. The route continues through Fury Shoals, Marsa Shona, and Abu Dabab, known for calmer conditions, colourful reefs, and frequent turtle sightings. Elphinstone adds vertical reef walls, vibrant coral coverage, and potential encounters with pelagic species.

While marine life sightings vary by season and cannot be guaranteed, this itinerary offers consistently rewarding diving. Advanced Open Water certification or Deep Dive Speciality is required and can be completed onboard.

ghazala-explorer::daedalus-zabargad-rock.highlightsDescription:
This southern Red Sea itinerary connects several of Egypt’s most iconic offshore dive sites, including Daedalus Reef, Rocky Island, Zabargad, Fury Shoals, Marsa Shona, Abu Dabab, and Elphinstone.

Daedalus Reef features steep walls, thriving coral, and the chance to encounter hammerheads, oceanic whitetips, and manta rays. Rocky Island and Zabargad offer lush reefs, dramatic drop-offs, and abundant marine life. The route continues through Fury Shoals, Marsa Shona, and Abu Dabab, known for calmer conditions, colourful reefs, and frequent turtle sightings. Elphinstone adds vertical reef walls, vibrant coral coverage, and potential encounters with pelagic species.

While marine life sightings vary by season and cannot be guaranteed, this itinerary offers consistently rewarding diving. Advanced Open Water certification or Deep Dive Speciality is required and can be completed onboard.

ghazala-explorer::deep-south-hurghada-hu.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary takes divers to four of the Red Sea’s most iconic offshore sites: Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, Elphinstone, and Abu Dabab. Known for their dramatic drop-offs, vibrant coral formations, and high chance of shark sightings, these sites offer unforgettable diving for advanced divers.

The Brothers Islands feature steep walls, rich marine life, and two famous wrecks—Numidia and Aida—along with regular encounters with oceanic whitetips, threshers, and hammerheads. Daedalus Reef is a remote seamount where schooling hammerheads and manta rays are often spotted. Elphinstone impresses with vertical walls, soft coral gardens, and seasonal oceanic whitetip encounters. Abu Dabab offers a gentler finale, with calm reefs full of life.

Although wildlife sightings vary by season, the route offers strong year-round potential for shark encounters and consistently excellent diving. Divers must be Advanced Open Water certified or have a Deep Dive Specialty—both can be completed onboard.

ghazala-explorer::escorted-get-wrecked-h.highlightsDescription:
The Get Wrecked itinerary is designed for divers passionate about shipwreck exploration, offering access to some of the Red Sea’s most iconic and historically rich wrecks. Highlights include the world-famous SS Thistlegorm, the Rosalie Moller, and the four wrecks of Abu Nuhas—Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, and Kimon M—each with its own story and marine life.

Further south, the itinerary may include the Salem Express, one of the region’s most talked-about wrecks, and Yolanda Reef in Ras Mohamed National Park, where the scattered remains of the Yolanda still rest. Sites like the Ulysses and other lesser-known wrecks are also part of the route, offering a mix of shallow, deep, and advanced-level dives.

This trip blends history, exploration, and vibrant marine ecosystems, making it a top choice for divers eager to experience the best of the Red Sea’s underwater heritage.

ghazala-explorer::north-dahab-hurghada-h.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary combines the Red Sea’s most iconic northern dive sites with the unique beauty of Dahab, offering a well-rounded diving experience of reefs, wrecks, and striking underwater landscapes.

Wreck diving highlights include the SS Thistlegorm, a world-famous WWII wreck, and the Abu Nuhas reef, home to the Giannis D and Chrisoula K. Gubal Island adds variety with its blend of reef and wreck diving, known for healthy coral and a range of marine life.

The journey continues to the Strait of Tiran, where sites like Jackson, Thomas, and Gordon Reef offer colorful drift dives with the Sinai Mountains in the distance. In Dahab, divers can explore dramatic underwater features like the Canyon, a favorite for its structure and depth.

This itinerary is suitable for divers with Advanced Open Water certification or those completing the Deep Dive Specialty course onboard, allowing full access to the most rewarding sites on the route.

This route includes both popular and lesser-known sites, offering variety and consistent underwater excitement—ideal for divers who enjoy both wreck exploration and thriving reef life.

hammerhead-ii::brothers-light-marsa-alam.highlightsDescription:
Embark on a 7-night liveaboard adventure through the southern Egyptian Red Sea, combining some of the region’s most iconic offshore reefs with vibrant coral gardens and the famous dolphin encounters of Sataya Reef. This itinerary is designed for experienced divers seeking a mix of big-fish action, dramatic reef walls, and unforgettable marine life encounters.

The journey begins around the reefs of Marsa Alam before heading offshore to the legendary Daedalus Reef, one of the Red Sea’s most renowned dive sites. Its steep walls, pristine coral formations, and nutrient-rich waters attract large schools of fish, oceanic whitetip sharks, hammerheads, and other pelagic species.

Continuing northward, divers explore the spectacular reefs of Elphinstone and Shaab Maksour, known for their impressive drop-offs, colorful soft corals, and frequent shark sightings. The itinerary then reaches the expansive Sataya Reef (Dolphin Reef), famous for its resident pods of spinner dolphins and vast coral formations teeming with marine life.

Additional dives at Abu Galawa, Siyal Island, and surrounding reefs provide a wonderful contrast of coral gardens, pinnacles, caverns, and sheltered lagoons, making this route one of the most diverse Red Sea safaris available.

With opportunities to encounter dolphins, sharks, turtles, large schools of reef fish, and thriving coral ecosystems, Sharks & Dolphins offers an exceptional combination of pelagic encounters and classic Red Sea reef diving.

hammerhead-ii::daedalus-light-marsa-alam.highlightsDescription:
The Daedalus Light itinerary is a short Red Sea diving safari combining coastal reefs and legendary offshore sites, designed for divers seeking an intense big-animal experience in the southern Red Sea.

The program begins in the Marsa Alam area with relaxed check dives at local reefs, ideal for fine-tuning buoyancy and equipment while enjoying healthy coral gardens, pinnacles, and abundant reef life before heading offshore.

The highlight of the itinerary is Daedalus Reef, an isolated oceanic atoll rising from deep water and renowned for strong currents, dramatic walls, and consistent pelagic activity. Drift dives along the vertical drop-offs offer excellent opportunities to encounter schooling hammerheads, oceanic whitetip sharks, grey reef sharks, and large pelagic species, alongside dense schools of reef fish and pristine coral formations.

Depending on weather and schedule, the itinerary may also include Elphinstone Reef, one of the Red Sea’s most celebrated reefs, known for exhilarating current dives, vibrant coral growth, and frequent encounters with oceanic whitetips, barracudas, and other pelagic species. The combination of offshore and coastal diving delivers a compact yet thrilling safari focused on exposed reefs, big animals, and some of the most exciting diving in the southern Red Sea.

hammerhead-ii::daedalus-light-marsa-alam.highlightsDescription:
The Red Sea Charm itinerary is a classic 7-night Red Sea diving safari combining legendary wrecks, iconic offshore reefs, and vibrant coastal sites, offering a varied and well-balanced exploration of Egypt’s most famous dive areas.

The route includes Abu Nuhas, the renowned wreck graveyard of the northern Red Sea, where several historic shipwrecks rest on shallow reefs covered in corals and teeming with marine life. These atmospheric dives combine maritime history with colorful reef environments and large schools of fish.

A highlight of the itinerary is the SS Thistlegorm, one of the world’s most famous wreck dives. Penetration dives through holds filled with wartime cargo offer a unique experience, while the surrounding reef attracts batfish, jacks, barracudas, and hunting predators.

The journey continues south to the Brothers Islands, two isolated oceanic pinnacles rising from deep water and renowned for dramatic walls, strong currents, and consistent pelagic encounters. Divers can expect sightings of grey reef sharks, oceanic whitetips, thresher sharks, and occasionally hammerheads, alongside pristine coral walls and dense schools of reef fish.

The final part of the itinerary explores the Safaga area, known for its relaxed reefs, coral gardens, and sheltered sites offering a contrast to the exposed offshore diving. The combination of world-class wrecks, shark-rich offshore reefs, and colorful coastal diving makes the Red Sea Charm itinerary an ideal choice for experienced divers seeking variety, adventure, and some of the most iconic diving in the Red Sea.

hammerhead-ii::exploring-north-abu-nuhas.highlightsDescription:
The Southern Charm itinerary is a 7-night Red Sea diving safari exploring a selection of the most remote and spectacular reefs of the southern Red Sea, combining legendary offshore atolls, isolated islands, and pristine reef systems.

The route includes Daedalus Reef, an isolated oceanic atoll rising from deep water and famous for strong currents, dramatic walls, and consistent pelagic activity. Drift dives along the steep drop-offs offer excellent opportunities to encounter schooling hammerheads, oceanic whitetip sharks, grey reef sharks, and large pelagic fish, alongside dense schools of reef fish and vibrant coral growth.

The itinerary continues south to Zabargad Island and Rocky Island, two exposed offshore sites renowned for steep walls, deep drop-offs, and thrilling current dives. These sites are known for frequent encounters with grey reef sharks, silky sharks, hammerheads, and large schools of jacks and tuna, as well as pristine walls covered in gorgonians and soft corals.

The final part of the journey explores the reefs of Sataya and Fury Shoals, offering a contrasting environment with sheltered lagoons, coral gardens, pinnacles, and maze-like reef systems. These southern reefs are known for their crystal-clear water, colorful hard corals, and abundant reef life, with the chance to encounter dolphins, turtles, and large schools of reef fish.

The Southern Charm itinerary offers a perfect balance of exposed offshore diving, big-animal encounters, and pristine southern reefs, making it an ideal choice for experienced divers seeking variety, adventure, and some of the most exciting diving in the southern Red Sea.

hammerhead-ii::exploring-south-zabargad-.highlightsDescription:
Super Diversity takes divers on an exhilarating journey through some of the most varied and vibrant dive sites in the southern Red Sea, combining thrilling encounters, stunning coral reefs, and relaxed exploration.

Daedalus stands out with its dramatic walls and strong currents, offering adventurous diving opportunities and a high chance of spotting pelagic species like hammerhead sharks and oceanic whitetips. The pristine coral formations and vast marine life make this site a favorite for experienced divers.

Saint John's is a haven of biodiversity, featuring an array of colorful coral gardens, tunnels, and caverns teeming with marine creatures. From small critters hiding in crevices to schools of fish and pelagic visitors, the area promises exciting and diverse underwater scenes.

Sataya, known for its playful pods of spinner dolphins, provides a more serene yet captivating diving experience. The vibrant coral reefs here are ideal for exploring calm waters and soaking in the beauty of this remote and picturesque area.

This route blends adrenaline-pumping dives with tranquil moments, offering something for every diver while showcasing the incredible diversity of the southern Red Sea.

hammerhead-ii::red-sea-charm-abu-nuhas-s.highlightsDescription:
The Red Sea Charm itinerary is a classic 7-night Red Sea diving safari combining legendary wrecks, iconic offshore reefs, and vibrant coastal sites, offering a varied and well-balanced exploration of Egypt’s most famous dive areas.

The route includes Abu Nuhas, the renowned wreck graveyard of the northern Red Sea, where several historic shipwrecks rest on shallow reefs covered in corals and teeming with marine life. These atmospheric dives combine maritime history with colorful reef environments and large schools of fish.

A highlight of the itinerary is the SS Thistlegorm, one of the world’s most famous wreck dives. Penetration dives through holds filled with wartime cargo offer a unique experience, while the surrounding reef attracts batfish, jacks, barracudas, and hunting predators.

The journey continues south to the Brothers Islands, two isolated oceanic pinnacles rising from deep water and renowned for dramatic walls, strong currents, and consistent pelagic encounters. Divers can expect sightings of grey reef sharks, oceanic whitetips, thresher sharks, and occasionally hammerheads, alongside pristine coral walls and dense schools of reef fish.

The final part of the itinerary explores the Safaga area, known for its relaxed reefs, coral gardens, and sheltered sites offering a contrast to the exposed offshore diving. The combination of world-class wrecks, shark-rich offshore reefs, and colorful coastal diving makes the Red Sea Charm itinerary an ideal choice for experienced divers seeking variety, adventure, and some of the most iconic diving in the Red Sea.

hammerhead-ii::red-sea-charm-abu-nuhas-s.highlightsDescription:
The Exploring North itinerary offers a unique blend of world-class wreck dives and vibrant coral reef sites, making it an exceptional diving adventure. The route takes you to the iconic SS Thistlegorm, one of the most renowned wreck dives in the world, where history comes alive underwater. This site offers an incredible glimpse into the past, surrounded by thriving marine life.

The journey continues to the stunning Ras Mohamed National Park, a protected marine area famous for its dramatic underwater landscapes, colorful coral gardens, and abundant marine biodiversity. Divers can explore vertical walls, coral-encrusted drop-offs, and thriving reef systems that attract a wide array of marine species.

At Tiran Island, the adventure unfolds with a series of spectacular dive sites known for their crystal-clear waters and vibrant underwater ecosystems. These sites are home to an endless variety of coral species, schooling fish, and unique marine creatures, offering divers a chance to immerse themselves in one of the Red Sea's most remarkable marine environments.

The route also includes the wrecks of Abu Nuhas, providing additional opportunities to explore the rich history and marine life of this underwater graveyard. Together, these destinations create an unforgettable diving experience that caters to enthusiasts of both wrecks and reefs, showcasing the best of the northern Red Sea.

hammerhead-ii::red-sea-charm-abu-nuhas-s.highlightsDescription:
The Red Sea Charm itinerary is a classic 7-night Red Sea diving safari combining legendary wrecks, iconic offshore reefs, and vibrant coastal sites, offering a varied and well-balanced exploration of Egypt’s most famous dive areas.

The route includes Abu Nuhas, the renowned wreck graveyard of the northern Red Sea, where several historic shipwrecks rest on shallow reefs covered in corals and teeming with marine life. These atmospheric dives combine maritime history with colorful reef environments and large schools of fish.

A highlight of the itinerary is the SS Thistlegorm, one of the world’s most famous wreck dives. Penetration dives through holds filled with wartime cargo offer a unique experience, while the surrounding reef attracts batfish, jacks, barracudas, and hunting predators.

The journey continues south to the Brothers Islands, two isolated oceanic pinnacles rising from deep water and renowned for dramatic walls, strong currents, and consistent pelagic encounters. Divers can expect sightings of grey reef sharks, oceanic whitetips, thresher sharks, and occasionally hammerheads, alongside pristine coral walls and dense schools of reef fish.

The final part of the itinerary explores the Safaga area, known for its relaxed reefs, coral gardens, and sheltered sites offering a contrast to the exposed offshore diving. The combination of world-class wrecks, shark-rich offshore reefs, and colorful coastal diving makes the Red Sea Charm itinerary an ideal choice for experienced divers seeking variety, adventure, and some of the most iconic diving in the Red Sea.

2 dives at Abu Kafan Reef and Panorama Reef.

Explore dramatic walls and coral plateaus with opportunities to encounter pelagic fish and strong drift conditions.

3 dives at Big Brother Island.

Dive steep walls, coral-covered drop-offs, and famous wreck areas while searching for oceanic whitetips and other shark species.

3 dives at Little Brother Island.

Discover colorful soft coral gardens, dramatic reef formations, and exciting drift dives around this iconic offshore reef.

3 dives at SS Thistlegorm and nearby northern Red Sea reefs including a possible night dive.

Explore the legendary WWII wreck famous for its preserved cargo and abundant marine life.

3 dives at Carnatic Wreck, Giannis D Wreck, and Abu Nuhas area.

Dive some of the Red Sea’s most famous wrecks, now covered with corals and home to a wide variety of reef fish.

hammerhead-ii::red-sea-charm-abu-nuhas-s.highlightsDescription:
The Deepest South itinerary is a 7-night Red Sea diving safari exploring the remote southern reefs of Egypt, combining pristine coral systems, sheltered lagoons, dramatic walls, and some of the most unspoiled dive sites in the southern Red Sea.

The program begins in the Marsa Alam area with relaxed check dives at Shaab Marsa Alam and Shaab Sharm, allowing divers to fine-tune buoyancy and equipment while enjoying healthy coral gardens, pinnacles, and abundant reef life.

The route then heads south to Abu Fandira and the Saint John’s reef system, a maze of isolated pinnacles, caves, tunnels, and coral plateaus offering a rich variety of dive profiles. These remote reefs are known for their crystal-clear water, vibrant hard and soft corals, and large schools of reef fish, with regular encounters with grey reef sharks, silky sharks, and other pelagic species.

Sataya Reef, also known as Dolphin Reef, provides a different atmosphere with its vast lagoon, shallow coral formations, and frequent sightings of spinner dolphins. The sheltered environment allows for relaxed daytime dives and atmospheric night dives on colorful coral gardens.

The itinerary continues through Wadi El Gemal and back towards Marsa Alam, combining pristine reefs, gentle slopes, and current-swept corners rich in marine life. The final diving day at Elphinstone Reef adds an exhilarating finish, with dramatic drop-offs, vibrant coral walls, and frequent encounters with oceanic whitetip sharks, barracudas, and other pelagic species.

The Deepest South itinerary offers a perfect balance of remote exploration, varied reef landscapes, and big-animal encounters, making it an ideal choice for experienced divers seeking pristine reefs and adventurous routes in the far south of the Red Sea.

hammerhead-ii::sharks-dolphins-marsa-ala.highlightsDescription:
Embark on a 7-night liveaboard adventure through the southern Egyptian Red Sea, combining some of the region’s most iconic offshore reefs with vibrant coral gardens and the famous dolphin encounters of Sataya Reef. This itinerary is designed for experienced divers seeking a mix of big-fish action, dramatic reef walls, and unforgettable marine life encounters.

The journey begins around the reefs of Marsa Alam before heading offshore to the legendary Daedalus Reef, one of the Red Sea’s most renowned dive sites. Its steep walls, pristine coral formations, and nutrient-rich waters attract large schools of fish, oceanic whitetip sharks, hammerheads, and other pelagic species.

Continuing northward, divers explore the spectacular reefs of Elphinstone and Shaab Maksour, known for their impressive drop-offs, colorful soft corals, and frequent shark sightings. The itinerary then reaches the expansive Sataya Reef (Dolphin Reef), famous for its resident pods of spinner dolphins and vast coral formations teeming with marine life.

Additional dives at Abu Galawa, Siyal Island, and surrounding reefs provide a wonderful contrast of coral gardens, pinnacles, caverns, and sheltered lagoons, making this route one of the most diverse Red Sea safaris available.

With opportunities to encounter dolphins, sharks, turtles, large schools of reef fish, and thriving coral ecosystems, Sharks & Dolphins offers an exceptional combination of pelagic encounters and classic Red Sea reef diving.

hammerhead-ii::sharks-obsession-brothers.highlightsDescription:
Sharks Obsession is an exhilarating route that takes divers to the Red Sea’s most daring and iconic dive sites, offering extraordinary underwater adventures and unforgettable encounters with diverse marine life. This journey is designed for thrill-seekers and marine enthusiasts who aim to explore some of the most remarkable underwater environments.

Daedalus, an isolated offshore reef, is a standout destination known for its frequent shark sightings, including hammerheads, grey reef sharks, and occasionally silky sharks. The reef’s dramatic drop-offs and strong currents create the perfect setting for close encounters with these magnificent creatures while exploring its vibrant coral gardens.

The Brothers Islands are equally captivating, with steep walls teeming with colorful soft corals, large schools of fish, and pelagic visitors. These twin reefs are famous for their exhilarating drift dives and encounters with oceanic whitetips, thresher sharks, and even manta rays. The marine diversity here, coupled with the islands' underwater topography, makes for an unforgettable experience.

Elphinstone completes the adventure with its steep walls adorned with soft corals and colorful marine life. Divers can expect encounters with reef sharks, barracudas, and other pelagic species. Known for its currents and spectacular views, Elphinstone is a thrilling addition to this route, ideal for seasoned divers.

This route combines excitement, exploration, and breathtaking natural beauty, offering an exceptional dive experience in the Red Sea’s most iconic locations. Whether captivated by the beauty of the coral reefs or seeking adrenaline-filled shark encounters, this journey promises unforgettable memories beneath the waves.

hammerhead-ii::south-parks-zabargad-rock.highlightsDescription:
Sharks Obsession is an exhilarating route that takes divers to the Red Sea’s most daring and iconic dive sites, offering extraordinary underwater adventures and unforgettable encounters with diverse marine life. This journey is designed for thrill-seekers and marine enthusiasts who aim to explore some of the most remarkable underwater environments.

Daedalus, an isolated offshore reef, is a standout destination known for its frequent shark sightings, including hammerheads, grey reef sharks, and occasionally silky sharks. The reef’s dramatic drop-offs and strong currents create the perfect setting for close encounters with these magnificent creatures while exploring its vibrant coral gardens.

The Brothers Islands are equally captivating, with steep walls teeming with colorful soft corals, large schools of fish, and pelagic visitors. These twin reefs are famous for their exhilarating drift dives and encounters with oceanic whitetips, thresher sharks, and even manta rays. The marine diversity here, coupled with the islands' underwater topography, makes for an unforgettable experience.

Elphinstone completes the adventure with its steep walls adorned with soft corals and colorful marine life. Divers can expect encounters with reef sharks, barracudas, and other pelagic species. Known for its currents and spectacular views, Elphinstone is a thrilling addition to this route, ideal for seasoned divers.

This route combines excitement, exploration, and breathtaking natural beauty, offering an exceptional dive experience in the Red Sea’s most iconic locations. Whether captivated by the beauty of the coral reefs or seeking adrenaline-filled shark encounters, this journey promises unforgettable memories beneath the waves.

days.description: Check-in in Port Ghalib, welcome briefing, cabin allocation, and overnight onboard.

2 dives at Shaab Marsa Alam and Shaab Sharm.

Check dives on colorful reefs with abundant reef fish, coral gardens, and relaxed conditions before heading offshore.

3 dives at Daedalus Reef.

Explore spectacular walls, steep drop-offs, and pristine coral formations with chances to encounter hammerheads and other pelagic species.

3 dives at Daedalus Reef.

Continue diving this iconic offshore reef known for excellent visibility, strong currents, and exciting shark encounters.

2 dives at Rocky Island and 1 dive plus night dive at Zabargad Island.

Discover dramatic underwater landscapes, caves, coral-covered walls, and vibrant marine life around these remote southern islands.

3 dives in Sataya and Fury Shoals area including a possible night dive.

Enjoy relaxed reef dives, swim-throughs, coral gardens, and opportunities to encounter spinner dolphins in Sataya Lagoon.
2 dives at Wadi El Gemal and Marsa Alam area before returning to Port Ghalib.

Breakfast onboard followed by check-out

hammerhead-ii::super-diversity-daedalus-.highlightsDescription:
The South Parks itinerary is a 7-night Red Sea diving safari exploring the remote southern marine parks of Egypt, combining pristine offshore islands, dramatic walls, and some of the most unspoiled reefs in the southern Red Sea.

The route focuses on Zabargad Island and Rocky Island, two isolated oceanic sites rising from deep water and renowned for steep drop-offs, strong currents, and exceptional pelagic activity. Divers can expect encounters with grey reef sharks, silky sharks, hammerheads, and large schools of jacks and tuna, along with spectacular walls covered in gorgonians and colorful soft corals.

The journey then continues to the Saint John’s reef system, a vast and intricate maze of pinnacles, caves, tunnels, and coral plateaus offering a wide variety of dive profiles. These remote reefs are known for crystal-clear visibility, vibrant hard and soft corals, and dense schools of reef fish, with regular sightings of reef sharks and other pelagic species.

Throughout the itinerary, dives take place on exposed offshore reefs and sheltered southern reef systems, creating a perfect balance between exhilarating current dives and relaxed reef exploration. The South Parks itinerary is an ideal choice for experienced divers seeking remote locations, pristine coral systems, and adventurous diving in the far south of the Red Sea.

hammerhead-ii::wrecks-reefs-abu-nuhas-ss.highlightsDescription:
Sharks Obsession is an exhilarating route that takes divers to the Red Sea’s most daring and iconic dive sites, offering extraordinary underwater adventures and unforgettable encounters with diverse marine life. This journey is designed for thrill-seekers and marine enthusiasts who aim to explore some of the most remarkable underwater environments.

Daedalus, an isolated offshore reef, is a standout destination known for its frequent shark sightings, including hammerheads, grey reef sharks, and occasionally silky sharks. The reef’s dramatic drop-offs and strong currents create the perfect setting for close encounters with these magnificent creatures while exploring its vibrant coral gardens.

The Brothers Islands are equally captivating, with steep walls teeming with colorful soft corals, large schools of fish, and pelagic visitors. These twin reefs are famous for their exhilarating drift dives and encounters with oceanic whitetips, thresher sharks, and even manta rays. The marine diversity here, coupled with the islands' underwater topography, makes for an unforgettable experience.

Elphinstone completes the adventure with its steep walls adorned with soft corals and colorful marine life. Divers can expect encounters with reef sharks, barracudas, and other pelagic species. Known for its currents and spectacular views, Elphinstone is a thrilling addition to this route, ideal for seasoned divers.

This route combines excitement, exploration, and breathtaking natural beauty, offering an exceptional dive experience in the Red Sea’s most iconic locations. Whether captivated by the beauty of the coral reefs or seeking adrenaline-filled shark encounters, this journey promises unforgettable memories beneath the waves.

hammerhead-ii::wrecks-reefs-abu-nuhas-ss.highlightsDescription:
The Mini Safari is a compact yet exhilarating 4-night adventure that showcases some of the Red Sea's most iconic diving sites. This route blends the allure of historic wrecks with the vibrant beauty of coral reefs, offering an unforgettable experience for divers of all levels.

Highlights include the legendary SS Thistlegorm, a sunken World War II vessel rich in marine life and history, the stunning Ras Mohammed National Park with its colorful reefs and abundant biodiversity, and the Abu Nuhas area, home to an array of wrecks surrounded by thriving underwater ecosystems.

This short but impactful itinerary provides the perfect escape for those seeking an intensive diving experience packed with unforgettable sights and marine encounters.

ms-royal-evolution::borthers-deadalus-ro.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary offers an unforgettable diving adventure through some of the Red Sea’s most legendary sites, combining dramatic seascapes, vibrant coral reefs, and thrilling big fish encounters. Departing from Port Ghalib, the journey begins with the Brothers Islands, two remote outcrops rising from the depths, surrounded by steep walls covered in colorful soft and hard corals. The Brothers are renowned for their exceptional biodiversity, home to large schools of fish, swirling barracudas, and regular sightings of oceanic whitetip sharks, hammerheads, and the elusive thresher sharks. The wrecks of the Numidia and Aida add a fascinating historical touch to the dives.

Daedalus Reef, a massive offshore reef crowned by a picturesque lighthouse, offers spectacular drift dives along sheer walls adorned with vibrant corals. The strong currents attract pelagic species, making this one of the best places in the Red Sea to encounter large schools of scalloped hammerheads, grey reef sharks, and even the occasional manta ray. The pristine coral gardens on the sheltered sides of the reef provide a stunning contrast to the adrenaline-pumping pelagic action.

The itinerary concludes with Elphinstone Reef, a slender, elongated reef famous for its towering walls, dense coral cover, and abundant marine life. Here, divers often encounter oceanic whitetip sharks cruising near the surface, along with grey reef sharks and colorful reef fish. The southern plateau is particularly known for thrilling shark sightings, while the northern tip offers dynamic drift dives.

Throughout the trip, up to three dives per day are scheduled, with a focus on safety and maximizing underwater experiences. Due to marine park regulations, night dives are not permitted in these protected areas. This itinerary is perfect for experienced divers seeking close encounters with sharks, vibrant coral ecosystems, and the remote beauty of Egypt’s offshore reefs.

ms-royal-evolution::brothers-deadalus-ro.highlightsDescription:
This 10-night Red Sea expedition departs round trip from Port Ghalib and is designed for experienced divers seeking the most iconic and remote dive sites in southern Egypt. The itinerary combines legendary offshore reefs with rarely visited southern marine parks, creating a demanding yet exceptionally rewarding diving safari.

The route begins with a warm-up at Abu Dabab and Elphinstone before heading offshore to the world-famous Brothers Islands, renowned for dramatic walls, strong currents, and frequent encounters with pelagic species such as oceanic whitetips, hammerheads, threshers, and grey reef sharks. From here, the cruise continues to the isolated lighthouse reef of Daedalus Reef, a magnet for schooling hammerheads and large pelagics, offering classic blue-water diving and breathtaking drop-offs.

Further south, the itinerary explores the wild and rarely dived reefs of Rocky Island and Elba Reef. These remote areas are known for pristine coral cover, dramatic underwater topography, and a strong sense of exploration, with multiple full dive days and night dives in near-untouched environments. The journey then continues to the vast reef systems of St. John's Reefs, featuring labyrinths of pinnacles, caves, swim-throughs, and coral gardens teeming with reef fish and macro life.

The safari concludes at the iconic Elphinstone Reef, famous for its sheer walls, currents, and consistent shark action, before returning to Port Ghalib. With a high dive count, extended crossings, and exposure to open-sea conditions, this itinerary delivers a true expedition feel and showcases the very best of Egypt’s southern Red Sea, from big-animal encounters to untouched reefs and dramatic underwater landscapes.

Special permissions granted by the Egyptian Navy make access to these untouched reefs possible, turning this itinerary into a true expedition-style experience for confident, well-prepared divers.

ms-royal-evolution::deadalus-sudan-borde.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night expedition-style itinerary departs round trip from Port Ghalib and focuses on the remote offshore reefs of the southern Red Sea, reaching as far as the Egyptian–Sudanese border. Designed for experienced divers, it combines iconic deep-water sites with some of the least-dived reefs in the region, offering a strong sense of exploration and minimal diving traffic.

After initial dives along the mainland coast and at Elphinstone Reef, the route heads offshore to Daedalus Reef, a legendary lighthouse reef known for strong currents, dramatic walls, and frequent encounters with schooling hammerheads and other pelagic species. From there, the itinerary continues south to Rocky Island and Zabargad Island before reaching the remote and rarely visited Elba Reef, located near the Sudanese border.

Elba Reef offers pristine coral formations, large sea fans, excellent visibility, and the possibility of encounters with grey reef sharks and hammerheads, all in an environment largely untouched by mass tourism. The itinerary concludes with dives in the St. John’s Reefs area, known for its maze of pinnacles, caves, and coral gardens, before returning to Port Ghalib. This is a demanding but highly rewarding safari, ideal for divers seeking remote reefs, big-animal potential, and a true southern Red Sea adventure.

Up to 3–4 dives per day over 6 diving days

ms-royal-evolution::deep-south-elba-reef.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night expedition-style itinerary departs round trip from Port Ghalib and focuses on the extreme southern reaches of the Egyptian Red Sea, close to the Sudanese border. Created specifically for experienced divers, it offers access to remote reefs that remain largely untouched by mass tourism, recreating the atmosphere of early Red Sea exploration.

After initial coastal dives and a check dive near the mainland, the route heads south to the expansive reef systems of St. John’s Reefs, known for their maze-like topography of pinnacles, caverns, and coral gardens. From there, the itinerary continues to the rarely visited Elba Reef, a pristine and isolated reef complex located at the Egyptian–Sudanese maritime border.

Elba Reef is characterized by dramatic plateaus, large sea fans, excellent visibility, and frequent encounters with pelagic species such as grey reef sharks and hammerheads. The area also hosts the historic Levanzo Wreck, an Italian cargo vessel resting between 22 and 75 meters, adding a technical and historical dimension to the diving. Long offshore crossings, minimal diver traffic, and special permissions granted by the Egyptian Navy make this a true expedition safari, best suited for confident, well-experienced divers.

Up to 3–4 dives per day over 6 diving days

ms-royal-evolution::egypt-elba-reef-elba.highlightsDescription:
This 10-night expedition explores one of the most remote and least-dived regions of the Egyptian Red Sea, reaching the pristine reefs of Elba near the Sudanese border. Designed for experienced divers seeking true exploration, the itinerary combines famous southern Red Sea sites with untouched reefs rarely visited by dive boats.

After a check dive at Shouna and dives at the iconic Elphinstone Reef, the safari heads south to St. John's before continuing to the isolated Elba Reef region. Located near the Egyptian-Sudanese border and accessible only with special permits, Elba offers spectacular coral gardens, enormous sea fans, excellent visibility, and opportunities to encounter grey reef sharks, hammerheads, and other pelagic species in an environment virtually untouched by mass tourism.

One of the highlights is the Levanzo, a 113-meter Italian cargo ship that sank in 1923. Resting between approximately 22 and 65 meters, the wreck offers an exciting technical-profile dive for suitably qualified divers.

After several days exploring Elba's remote reefs, the itinerary returns north via St. John's before sailing back to Port Ghalib.

Up to 3-4 dives per day over 9 diving days.

ms-royal-evolution::special-wreck-hurgha.highlightsDescription:
A Special Wreck itinerary in the Red Sea delivers a distinctive and immersive diving experience focused on some of the region’s most iconic historic shipwrecks. Departing round trip from Hurghada, this route is designed for divers fascinated by maritime history, dramatic underwater scenery, and the unique atmosphere that only wreck diving can offer.

The Red Sea is world-renowned for the quality, preservation, and variety of its wrecks. Sunken cargo ships, wartime vessels, and steamers lie scattered across sandy bottoms and coral slopes, each telling its own story beneath the surface. These sites range in depth and complexity, allowing divers to explore exterior structures, towering hulls, and encrusted superstructures, with penetration opportunities assessed by the dive guides based on conditions and experience levels.

Over time, many of these wrecks have transformed into thriving artificial reefs. Dense coral growth, clouds of reef fish, schooling predators, and occasional larger pelagics surround the steel frames, creating a compelling blend of history and marine life. Between wreck dives, nearby reefs often provide additional variety, adding color, biodiversity, and contrast to the itinerary.

For suitably qualified divers, some sites may offer deeper or more technical profiles, while night dives introduce a completely different perspective, with nocturnal species emerging from the shadows of the wrecks. Throughout the trip, experienced dive guides ensure safe operations, thoughtful briefings, and valuable insight into both the historical significance of the wrecks and the marine ecosystems that now inhabit them.

This itinerary is ideal for divers seeking a focused wreck safari that combines exploration, history, and classic Red Sea marine life into a single, rewarding liveaboard experience.

Up to 3 dives per day over 6 diving days

This route is ideal for divers drawn to maritime history, dramatic underwater landscapes, and the unique sense of exploration that wreck diving provides.

The northern and central Red Sea are home to an exceptional collection of well-preserved wrecks, ranging from iconic wartime cargo ships to lesser-known vessels resting along reefs and sandy slopes. These sites vary in depth and structure, allowing for a mix of exterior exploration, swim-throughs, and close-up inspection of hulls now covered in corals and sponges. Dive profiles are planned according to conditions and diver experience, with briefings led by experienced guides.

Many of these wrecks have evolved into vibrant artificial reefs, attracting dense fish life, schooling species, and predators that patrol the surrounding blue. Between wreck dives, nearby reefs often complement the itinerary, adding color, biodiversity, and a softer contrast to the steel silhouettes below.

For qualified divers, some dives may involve deeper profiles, while night dives reveal a different side of the wrecks, with nocturnal marine life emerging from the shadows. Throughout the cruise, professional dive guides ensure safe operations and provide insight into both the historical background of the wrecks and the marine ecosystems that now inhabit them.

This one-way wreck safari is well suited to experienced divers seeking a dedicated Red Sea wreck adventure combined with classic reef diving, all framed by the convenience of embarking in Hurghada and disembarking in Port Ghalib.

mv-blue-horizon::project-shark-daedalus-.highlightsDescription:
Project Shark' itineraries aim to get you up close and personal with the oceans' apex predators. When not diving, you will have opportunities to learn about the history, ecology and global issues facing these ancient, intriguing creatures. Through structured and engaging sessions you will also learn about the biology and behaviour of sharks. As part of the Project Shark itinerary, you will also have a chance to learn about globally endangered marine species and what we as divers can do to help protect them.

Brother Islands

Brother Islands in the northernmost part of Egypt's offshore marine park is made up of two islands 60km away from the coast and 140km south from Hurghada. The larger island (complete with a lighthouse from 1883) is 400 metres long with a spectacular plateau on the south east corner which is dotted with coral mountains and famous for thresher and grey reef shark sightings. The western side of the island has two impressive wrecks which both lie almost vertical on the side of the reef. The most spectacular is the Numidia, a large cargo steamer which sank in 1901 and now lies on the tip of the island between 10 and 80 metres covered in soft corals and frequented by large pelagic predators. The smaller wreck of the Aida (sitting between 30 and 65 metres) was a lighthouse authority supply vessel which sank in bad weather in 1957.

The smaller island, whilst only a little over 200 metres long, hosts an incredible concentration and variety of marine life. There is a pristine fan coral forest, a massive collection of hard and soft corals and compelling overhangs to explore. The highlight is the fish life; with regular seasonal sightings of hammerhead, thresher, grey reef and oceanic whitetip sharks.

Daedalus

Daedalus is a huge tear-drop shaped reef rises from the sea bed in the middle of the Red Sea, 80km offshore and more than 300km south of Hurghada. Easily recognised by its zebra-striped lighthouse, this reef offers some of the most amazing dives in the Red Sea. The sheer walls are covered in over-grown hard coral formations and a variety of reef fish. Napoleon wrasses and turtles are often cruising by, but make sure you keep your eyes open on the blue! Daedalus is one of those places where anything can happen... oceanic white tip, grey reef and thresher sharks are often sighted, but Daedalus is most famous for its scalloped hammerhead sharks which can often be seen in large schools out in the blue during the summer months. The sheer size of this reef means that you can do several dives here and never get bored!

Elphinstone Reef

Elphinstone Reef is a Red Sea legend; a finger shaped reef, with north and south plateaus covered in hard and soft corals, unpredictable and exciting this truly is an awesome reef where hammerhead sharks are regularly spotted in the summer and oceanic whitetip sharks often congregate in large numbers during late autumn.

mv-blue-horizon::project-shark-simply-th.highlightsDescription: Simply the best shark itinerary the Red Sea has to offer. Explore the untouched wonders of Egypt's remote offshore reefs on this thrilling diving liveaboard adventure. Dive into the renowned marine havens of Brothers and Daedalus, and uncover their majestic drop-offs. And don't forget the chance to explore the captivating Elphinstone reef on this unforgettable journey. With plenty of opportunity to see hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetip sharks, and even the elusive thresher, this is a hard trip to beat.

mv-blue-horizon::simply-the-best-7-night.highlightsDescription: Simply the best shark itinerary the Red Sea has to offer. Explore the untouched wonders of Egypt's remote offshore reefs on this thrilling diving liveaboard adventure. Dive into the renowned marine havens of Brothers and Daedalus, and uncover their majestic drop-offs. And don't forget the chance to explore the captivating Elphinstone reef on this unforgettable journey. With plenty of opportunity to see hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetip sharks, and even the elusive thresher, this is a hard trip to beat.
mv-blue-horizon::simply-the-best-7-night.logistics:
Before the trip 

  • Transfers from the airport
  • You will find advice about the transfer timings for your particular trip on your booking Confirmation.
  • The following should be used as a guide:- Hurghada Airport - Hurghada Marina (vessel departing from Hurghada) = 15mins - Hurghada Airport - Port Ghalib (vessel departing from Port Ghalib) = 4 hours - Hurghada Airport - Marsa Alam (vessel departing from Marsa Alam) = 4.5 hours
  • On longer transfers, snacks and water will be provided.
  • You will be transferred from the airport to your vessel upon arrival and from your vessel back to the airport on your departure.
  • A blue o two representative will accompany you.
  • Please note that if you are making your own travel arrangements you will be able to check in on the vessel after 6pm.
  • We will always try our best to welcome your beforehand whenever possible, but the vessels need time to be properly stocked and cleaned before your arrival.
  • Please note that ports are subject to change.
  • Departure next morning

 

After the trip

  • Upon your return into the marina, our representatives will advise you of your precise departure arrangements for the following day.
  • Normally you will be expected to vacate the vessel between 9am and 10am on the following morning.
  • On leaving the liveaboard and depending on your return flight times, you will be provided with local day use facilities.
  • Please note this does not include the use of a hotel room although these may be available to book with an additional cost.
  • Please note that after breakfast no meals are provided so for late flights a lunch provision may be necessary.
  • If you decide to upgrade to a hotel room on the final night of your trip, check in will be available from 2pm and check out will be at 12pm.

Dive into the renowned marine havens of Brothers and Daedalus, and uncover their majestic drop-offs. And don't forget the chance to explore the captivating Elphinstone reef on this unforgettable journey. With plenty of opportunity to see hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetip sharks, and even the elusive thresher, this is a hard trip to beat.
mv-blue-horizon::simply-the-best-7-night.logistics:
Before the trip 

  • Transfers from the airport
  • You will find advice about the transfer timings for your particular trip on your booking Confirmation.
  • The following should be used as a guide:- Hurghada Airport - Hurghada Marina (vessel departing from Hurghada) = 15mins - Hurghada Airport - Port Ghalib (vessel departing from Port Ghalib) = 4 hours 
  • On longer transfers, snacks and water will be provided.
  • You will be transferred from the airport to your vessel upon arrival and from your vessel back to the airport on your departure.
  • A blue o two representative will accompany you.
  • Please note that if you are making your own travel arrangements you will be able to check in on the vessel after 6pm.
  • We will always try our best to welcome your beforehand whenever possible, but the vessels need time to be properly stocked and cleaned before your arrival.
  • Please note that ports are subject to change.
  • Departure next morning

 

After the trip

 

  • Upon your return into the marina, our representatives will advise you of your precise departure arrangements for the following day.
  • Normally you will be expected to vacate the vessel between 9am and 10am on the following morning.
  • On leaving the liveaboard and depending on your return flight times, you will be provided with local day use facilities.
  • Please note this does not include the use of a hotel room although these may be available to book with an additional cost.
  • Please note that after breakfast no meals are provided so for late flights a lunch provision may be necessary.
  • If you decide to upgrade to a hotel room on the final night of your trip, check in will be available from 2pm and check out will be at 12pm.

mv-blue-horizon::strait-of-tiran-north-7.highlightsDescription: The Strait of Tiran and North cruise allows you to take in some of the most iconic wrecks and reefs the northern Red Sea has to offer, such as Thistlegorm and Ras Mohammed, as well as the pristine coral reefs of Tiran. The Tiran dive area is found in the entrance to the Gulf of Aqaba and is made up of four main reefs that form the top of an underwater bridge. These reefs, named after British cartographers (Jackson, Woodhouse, Thomas, Gordon), are world famous for their extraordinary diversity of corals and strong south westerly currents make them home to many large pelagic fish.

days.description:
Once onboard there will be a safety briefing, crew introduction, complete and check dive paperwork, cabin allocation and boat orientation. Our boats moor in port on arrival day departing early next morning.

There is no diving on the first and last day.

Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforseeable factors.

3-4 dives per day, including night dive (if possible)

Discover Elphinstone's vibrant soft corals, encounter oceanic white tips; explore Daedalus' pristine hard coral formations with hammerheads; and dive into Fury Shoals' diverse reef system, home to spinner dolphins, swim-throughs, and stunning coral gardens.

On the last diving day, 2 dives are available in the morning whilst observing the rule of no diving within 24 hours of reaching altitude. We return to port at approximately 1pm and moor here overnight. Evening-time pack up diving equipment, visit the marina and settle any outstanding bills ready to depart for the airport or hotel the following morning.

Disembark after breakfast, transfer to the airport or your local hotel.

Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

mv-emperor-asmaa::daedalus-elphinstone-p.highlightsDescription:
This trip offers you some of the best diving in the Red Sea and includes Daedalus, Fury Shoals and Elphinstone. With less distance to travel than some routes, you have more time to dive these iconic sites and there is less chance of seasickness with shorter sailings and secure moorings. Depending on prevailing weather conditions your guides will pick sites suitable for night dives outside the Marine Park.

Heading first to Fury Shoals, we may dive around the Marsa Alam area or perhaps dive Sha’ab Sharm with its wall dives and white tip reef sharks. Oceanic white tips and silky sharks can sometimes be found in the blue and turtles often visit the south side before heading further south. At Fury Shoals, we have more time to explore the vast reef system than other itineraries afford. Of course we will dive the classics such as Sha’ab Claude (a.k.a. Claudio) with its famous swim-throughs and huge porite corals, Malahi with its mazes and friendly turtles and Abu Galawa Soraya with its fantastic coral garden and a wreck of a private sailing boat smothered with glass fish. Sataya with its resident spinner dolphin population is a must for snorkelling between dives, as well as having some good underwater offerings, and on top of that we can spend time exploring less dived sites such as Sha’ab Hamam (Stairway to Heaven), Abu Galawa Kebir with the Tien Hsing wreck, Gota Sataya and if the weather is kind there are some submerged reefs that can be moored on such as Habili Sameh that will blow you away!

Daedalus Reef, part of the Red Sea offshore Marine Park, is a large, oval reef with a lighthouse and is the furthest offshore reef in the Egyptian Red Sea. Its deep walls and drop-offs offer some of the most spectacular diving. Daedalus has mountainous, pristine, hard coral formations. There is also a strong chance of spotting schooling hammerheads, especially from May to November, and grey reef sharks.

Of course no trip to the South would be complete without stopping at world famous Elphinstone, with its sheer walls covered in soft corals, and likely encounters with oceanic white tip sharks. Depending on the experience of the group and the weather, you may even get the chance to dive it at the beginning and end of your amazing trip!

days.description:
Once onboard there will be a safety briefing, crew introduction, complete and check dive paperwork, cabin allocation and boat orientation. Our boats moor in port on arrival day departing early next morning.

There is no diving on the first and last day.

Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforseeable factors.

3-4 dives per day, including night dive (if possible).

Explore the wreck graveyard at Abu Nuhas, visit the infamous SS Thistlegorm and sister Rosalie Moller, Salem Express and more.

Breath-taking reefs and fishes at Shark & Yolanda at Ras Mohamed National Park, magnificent anemones and huge coral formations at Panorama Reef, Safaga

Deep walls draped in soft corals and gorgonian forests take centre stage to diverse marine life and large pelagics at the Brothers.

Look out for big tuna, barracudas, jacks and snappers. Occasional hammerheads, silky and oceanic white tips and mantas and the rare chance to spot the thresher shark.

On the last diving day, 2 dives are available in the morning whilst observing the rule of no diving within 24 hours of reaching altitude. We return to port at approximately 1pm and moor here overnight. Evening-time pack up diving equipment, visit the marina and settle any outstanding bills ready to depart for the airport or hotel the following morning.

Disembark after breakfast, transfer to the airport or your local hotel.

Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

mv-emperor-asmaa::famous-five-hurghada-h.highlightsDescription:
Starting from Hurghada, we sail north towards Gubal Island and on to Abu Nuhas and its four well-known wrecks: Giannis D, Carnatic, the ‘Lentil Wreck’ and the ‘Tile Wreck’, all offering spectacular dives and plenty of fish life. Explore the Rosalie Moller (the sister ship of the slightly more famous Thistlegorm), which lies from 30 to 50 metres deep and is in excellent condition. Although the visibility is not always good, the wreck is covered in glassfish from bow to stern and hunting them are masses of lionfish. Around the wreck are the usual pelagics such as tuna, trevallies, Emperor fish and many more.

A short ride across the Straits of Gubal and you visit the most famous wreck of the Red Sea, the SS Thistlegorm! An awe-inspiring World War II British vessel with a cargo full of armaments, Bedford trucks and BSA motorbikes, which were all destined for the British troops in North Africa. She was sunk by the German Luftwaffe and now lies in 30 metres of water. Depending on divers’ experience, along with weather and current conditions, we try to offer a night dive here. Nearby is the Ras Mohamed National Park, offering a morning dive at the renowned ‘Shark and Yolanda’ reefs. Ras Mohamed National Park is the furthest Sinai destination before heading south towards the Brothers.

The Brother Islands are the pinnacles of two undersea mountains rising from the depths of the abyss and are located about 60 miles offshore from El Quseir. Part of the Marine Park Islands National Park, these islands offer stunning wall diving, with the walls covered in soft corals and forests of gorgonians, creating a kaleidoscope of ever-changing colours. They attract a diverse array of marine species and large pelagics. Big tuna, barracudas, jacks and snappers cruise in the blue, accompanied by occasional hammerheads, silky and oceanic white tip sharks and mantas. Even the rare thresher shark can sometimes be found there. Sightings of the grey reef shark are almost guaranteed on the North and South Plateaux of Small Brother.

For the wreck diver, the Aida II, an Egyptian supply vessel, and the Numidia, a cargo ship, lie on the walls of the Big Brother. Both are covered in a rich growth of soft and hard corals. Marine life includes a family of Napoleon wrasse and grey reef sharks.

The boat will then sail back to Hurghada via Safaga where you can dive at Panorama Reef or the famous wreck of Salem Express for a memorable finale!

Explore the majestic Red Sea during the warm summer months of May to August with our much anticipated Red Sea Sharks itinerary offering flexibility and focus for ‘action’ dives. Our guides select the best possible action sites to visit based on their immense local knowledge and on insider-data on recent activity including a variety of Red Sea sharks, dolphins and anything else that chooses to join the party.

mv-emperor-asmaa::fury-and-st-johns-tues.highlightsDescription:
Starting from Hurghada, we sail north towards Gubal Island and on to Abu Nuhas and its four well-known wrecks: Giannis D, Carnatic, the ‘Lentil Wreck’ and the ‘Tile Wreck’, all offering spectacular dives and plenty of fish life. Explore the Rosalie Moller (the sister ship of the slightly more famous Thistlegorm), which lies from 30 to 50 metres deep and is in excellent condition. Although the visibility is not always good, the wreck is covered in glassfish from bow to stern and hunting them are masses of lionfish. Around the wreck are the usual pelagics such as tuna, trevallies, Emperor fish and many more.

A short ride across the Straits of Gubal and you visit the most famous wreck of the Red Sea, the SS Thistlegorm! An awe-inspiring World War II British vessel with a cargo full of armaments, Bedford trucks and BSA motorbikes, which were all destined for the British troops in North Africa. She was sunk by the German Luftwaffe and now lies in 30 metres of water. Depending on divers’ experience, along with weather and current conditions, we try to offer a night dive here. Nearby is the Ras Mohamed National Park, offering a morning dive at the renowned ‘Shark and Yolanda’ reefs. Ras Mohamed National Park is the furthest Sinai destination before heading south towards the Brothers.

The Brother Islands are the pinnacles of two undersea mountains rising from the depths of the abyss and are located about 60 miles offshore from El Quseir. Part of the Marine Park Islands National Park, these islands offer stunning wall diving, with the walls covered in soft corals and forests of gorgonians, creating a kaleidoscope of ever-changing colours. They attract a diverse array of marine species and large pelagics. Big tuna, barracudas, jacks and snappers cruise in the blue, accompanied by occasional hammerheads, silky and oceanic white tip sharks and mantas. Even the rare thresher shark can sometimes be found there. Sightings of the grey reef shark are almost guaranteed on the North and South Plateaux of Small Brother.

For the wreck diver, the Aida II, an Egyptian supply vessel, and the Numidia, a cargo ship, lie on the walls of the Big Brother. Both are covered in a rich growth of soft and hard corals. Marine life includes a family of Napoleon wrasse and grey reef sharks.

The boat will then sail back to Hurghada via Safaga where you can dive at Panorama Reef or the famous wreck of Salem Express for a memorable finale!

mv-emperor-asmaa::fury-and-st-johns-wedn.highlightsDescription:
Designed to showcase some of the highlights of the Northern Red Sea at a relaxed pace whether diving or snorkelling, it’s ideal for both divers and non-divers. It’s also the best time of year for dolphin spotting and the world class fish schooling event at Ras Mohamed.

We spend more time moored at each location and less time travelling from dive site to dive site; perfectly designed for the divers who like to take things easy, the photo enthusiasts looking for more dive time to capture that perfect photo opportunity or for non-divers looking to soak up the scenery, both below and above the water. Our open deck policy at certain dive sites on these trips mean you can simply relax and sunbathe or grab your snorkel or dive gear whenever you want to hit the water.

Enjoy the breath-taking scenery as we start from Hurghada, sail across to well-known areas such as Sha’ab El Erg, two of the world’s best dive sites including Ras Mohamed National Park (Shark and Yolanda reefs) and the wreck of the Thistlegorm, breath-taking schools of glass fish on the wreck of the Dunraven and the colourful coral gardens on the islands of Tiran.

This itinerary allows up to 4 dives per day for qualified divers whilst non-divers have the chance to experience an ‘introductory dive’. Our experienced guides will select the best spots to dive, snorkel and swim in each location and to suit local conditions, marine life opportunities and your skill.

mv-emperor-asmaa::reefs-wrecks-7-nights.highlightsDescription:
This itinerary presents the best of both worlds, where you visit famous wrecks in the northern Red Sea along with some stunning reef diving. As a 21+ DIVES cruise, there’s a good chance to enjoy 21 or more dives on a 7-day safari if you choose to.

The famous horseshoe shaped reef of Shaab El Erg is a perfect example of the reefs on offer on this cruise with its beautiful hard coral garden and the chance to see dolphins.

Abu Nuhas has four well-known wrecks: Giannis D, Carnatic, the Chrisoula K (’tile wreck’) and the Kimon M (‘lentil wreck’), all offering spectacular dives and plenty of fish life.

In between wreck dives you will also visit the reefs of the Straits of Gubal, Gulf of Suez and those to the north of Hurghada. A variety of deep walls and hard coral gardens with an abundance of reef fish make them well worth a visit.

Night dives can be superb as Gubal Island offers protected anchoring for the night. A small wreck at 8-10 metres makes for a spectacular night dive with lionfish, scorpion fish and its resident giant moray eel as well as the wreck of the Ulysses. Next onto the Kingston lying at Shag Rock, the Carina lying close to Sha’ab Ali and the Dunraven at Beacon Rock.

Ras Mohamed lies on the southernmost tip of the Sinai and is one of the best kept National Parks in Egypt with waters full of nutrients, steep walls going down to a depth of 1000 metres attracting a large amount of big fish and earning itself a reputation as one of the top diving areas in the world. Whilst here, you may have the chance to dive at Shark Reef, a sheer wall falling into the blue, as well as the wreck of the Yolanda.

Jackson Reef, locally named the ‘Aquarium’, is Tiran‘s most popular dive with the ‘Jackson Drift’ being Sharm’s fastest and most exhilarating drift dive past a stunning wall bursting with prolific coral growth. Occasionally, in the summer months, a school of scalloped hammerheads can be seen. Thomas Reef gives you plunging walls covered with soft coral, gorgonians and colourful fish life. The west wall is darker with overhangs and caves full of glassfish and sweepers. A night dive at Gordon Reef promises various species of coral, small nudibranchs hidden in the crevices and the soft corals and a chance to see white tip reef sharks, eagle rays, octopus and different types of eel such as moray, peppered and gold edged morays.

Finally the most famous wreck in the Red Sea, the SS Thistlegorm, at Shaab Ali including a night dive on Thistle. The Thistlegorm was sunk in 1941 after being bombed by the German Luftwaffe while on a mission to deliver a cargo of ammunition and other war materials to the British troops in North Africa.

From here the boat heads back towards Hurghada.

All dive sites are subject to divers’ experience and weather conditions.

mv-emperor-asmaa::safaga-brothers-and-el.highlightsDescription:
The area around Safaga has some great diving, the best being the offshore reefs of Panorama Reef, Middle Reef and Abu Kafan. Some divers say this area equals the great sites of Ras Mohamed. The diving offers a combination of shallow reef dives and drop-offs, as well as the famous wreck of the Salem Express.

The Salem Express is a dramatic wreck dive. It is now home to a thriving underwater life, including a famous resident frogfish, blue-spotted stingrays, angel and butterfly fish. The ship itself is covered in a large quantity of hard and soft corals. It is one of the largest wrecks in the Egyptian Red Sea, roughly the same size as the Thistlegorm.

There is superb wall diving at Panorama: on the south-east side of the plateau is a gorgonian and glassfish corner with the whole plateau covered in soft corals and on the south side is an anemone city.

Hal Hal (Middle Reef) is a rarely chosen dive site due to its distance from the coast, which makes it a virgin spot. The north side is a drop off going down to 80 metres and is a perfect location to spot tunas, barracudas, turtles and sharks. The southern side has colourful coral gardens along with some caves and canyons.

Abu Kafan is a 300-metre long, narrow reef offering a plateau at both north and south tips. We normally jump in the water on the north plateau and glide with the frequent strong current southwards along the impressive walls covered with soft and black coral, giant fans and gorgonians.

Abu Dabab is six reefs commonly known as “Fathers Steps” or “Fathers Stepping Stones” and as the name suggests a set of fairly shallow reefs ranging from depths of 25 metres to the seafloor. In between Abu Dabab II and III at approximately 15 metres is the wreckage of a small ship sunk after a fire in 2004.

Once onboard there will be a safety briefing, crew introduction, complete and check dive paperwork, cabin allocation and boat orientation. Our boats moor in port on arrival day departing early next morning.

There is no diving on the first and last day.

3-4 dives per day, including night dive (if possible)

Discover vibrant underwater wonders in the Red Sea with colorful soft coral walls and gorgonian forests at the Brothers and Elphinstone sites. Safaga offers magnificent anemones, glass fish, and expansive coral formations at Panorama Reef, as well as the thriving artificial reef of the Salem Express. Encounter a diverse array of marine life, including tuna, barracudas, jacks, groupers, snappers, reef sharks, and occasional sightings of hammerheads, silky and oceanic white tip sharks, dolphins, and mantas, with rare opportunities to spot threshers.

On the last diving day, 2 dives are available in the morning whilst observing the rule of no diving within 24 hours of reaching altitude. We return to port at approximately 1pm and moor here overnight. Evening-time pack up diving equipment, visit the marina and settle any outstanding bills ready to depart for the airport or hotel the following morning.

Disembark after breakfast, transfer to the airport or your local hotel.

Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

mv-emperor-asmaa::safaga-brothers-elphin.highlightsDescription:
The area around Safaga has some great diving, the best being the offshore reefs of Panorama Reef, Middle Reef and Abu Kafan. Some divers say this area equals the great sites of Ras Mohamed. The diving offers a combination of shallow reef dives and drop-offs, as well as the famous wreck of the Salem Express.

The Salem Express is a dramatic wreck dive. It is now home to a thriving underwater life, including a famous resident frogfish, blue-spotted stingrays, angel and butterfly fish. The ship itself is covered in a large quantity of hard and soft corals. It is one of the largest wrecks in the Egyptian Red Sea, roughly the same size as the Thistlegorm.

There is superb wall diving at Panorama: on the south-east side of the plateau is a gorgonian and glassfish corner with the whole plateau covered in soft corals and on the south side is an anemone city.

Hal Hal (Middle Reef) is a rarely chosen dive site due to its distance from the coast, which makes it a virgin spot. The north side is a drop off going down to 80 metres and is a perfect location to spot tunas, barracudas, turtles and sharks. The southern side has colourful coral gardens along with some caves and canyons.

Abu Kafan is a 300-metre long, narrow reef offering a plateau at both north and south tips. We normally jump in the water on the north plateau and glide with the frequent strong current southwards along the impressive walls covered with soft and black coral, giant fans and gorgonians.

The Brother Islands are the pinnacles of two undersea mountains rising from the depths of the abyss and are located about 60 miles offshore. Part of the Marine Park Islands National Park, these islands offer stunning wall diving, with the walls covered in soft corals and forests of gorgonians, creating a kaleidoscope of ever-changing colours. They attract a diverse array of marine species and large pelagics. Large tuna, jacks and snappers cruise in the blue, accompanied by occasional hammerheads, silvertips, silky and oceanic white tip sharks and mantas. Even the rare thresher shark can be found here. Sightings of the grey reef shark are almost guaranteed on the North and South Plateaux of Small Brother.

Abu Dabab is six reefs commonly known as “Fathers Steps” or “Fathers Stepping Stones” and as the name suggests a set of fairly shallow reefs ranging from depths of 25 metres to the seafloor. In between Abu Dabab II and III at approximately 15 metres is the wreckage of a small ship sunk after a fire in 2004.

Elphinstone is approximately 30km from Port Ghalib; Elphinstone reef is 300 metres long with sheer walls richly covered in colourful pink and red soft corals and elegant red gorgonians descending to around 40 metres. Other areas of the reef have near vertical cliffs, overhangs, small caves and drop offs of up to 100 metres. Elphinstone is known to experience some strong currents attracting many diverse species such as barracuda, angel fish, groupers, Napoleons, morays, reef sharks and great shoals of dogtooth tuna and jacks. Occasional sightings include dolphins, turtles, oceanic white tip and hammerhead sharks.

mv-emperor-asmaa::southern-sharks.highlightsDescription:
The Brother Islands are the pinnacles of two undersea mountains rising from the depths of the abyss and are located about 60 miles offshore. Part of the Marine Park Islands National Park, these islands offer stunning wall diving, with the walls covered in soft corals and forests of gorgonians, creating a kaleidoscope of ever-changing colours. They attract a diverse array of marine species and large pelagics. Large tuna, jacks and snappers cruise in the blue, accompanied by occasional hammerheads, silvertips, silky and oceanic white tip sharks and mantas. Even the rare thresher shark can be found here. Sightings of the grey reef shark are almost guaranteed on the North and South Plateaux of Small Brother.

For the wreck diver, the Aida II, an Egyptian supply vessel, and the Numidia, a cargo ship, lie on the walls of the Big Brother. Both are covered in a rich growth of soft and hard corals. Marine life includes a family of Napoleon wrasse and grey reef sharks.

Daedalus Reef, also part of the Marine Park, is a large, oval reef with a lighthouse and is the furthest offshore reef in the Egyptian Red Sea. Its deep walls and drop-offs offer some of the most spectacular diving to be found. Daedalus has mountainous, pristine, hard coral formations. There is also a strong chance of spotting schooling hammerheads and grey reef sharks.

Elphinstone is approximately 30km from Port Ghalib; Elphinstone reef is 300 metres long with sheer walls richly covered in colourful pink and red soft corals and elegant red gorgonians descending to around 40 metres. Other areas of the reef have near vertical cliffs, overhangs, small caves and drop offs of up to 100 metres. Elphinstone is known to experience some strong currents attracting many diverse species such as barracuda, angel fish, groupers, Napoleons, morays, reef sharks and great shoals of dogtooth tuna and jacks. Occasional sightings include dolphins, turtles, oceanic white tip and hammerhead sharks.
