my-blue-melody::strait-of-tiran-and-nort.highlightsDescription:
The Strait of Tiran and North cruise allows you to take in some of the most iconic wrecks and reefs the northern Red Sea has to offer as well as the pristine coral reefs of Tiran.

The Tiran dive area is found in the entrance to the Gulf of Aqaba and is made up of four main reefs that form the top of an underwater bridge. These reefs, named after British cartographers (Jackson, Woodhouse, Thomas, Gordon), are world famous for their extraordinary diversity of corals and strong south westerly currents make them home to many large pelagic fish.

Strait of Tiran

Only accessible by boat, this dive area is found in the entrance to the Gulf of Aqaba and is made up of four main reefs that form the top of an underwater bridge. These reefs, named after British cartographers (Jackson, Woodhouse, Thomas, Gordon), are world-famous for their extraordinary diversity of corals and strong south westerly currents make them home to many large pelagic fish.

Jackson Reef is the most northerly reef and on its northern edge lays the wreck of a freighter serving as a stark warning to ships in the narrow straights. Dives are usually conducted from the moorings on the south side which is sheltered from the main swell and currents. Moving northwards you will come across a forest of spectacular gorgonian fan coral at about 20 to 30 metres as well as many different kinds of reef fish. This site can also be done as a drift dive heading from the mooring towards the East with the reef on the left where it is mostly wall diving with excellent corals. Diving the back of Jackson in late summer can give you the chance to see the resident hammerhead sharks.

Woodhouse Reef is the longest reef of the four in the Strait of Tiran. Home to reef sharks and eagle rays, it is dived as a drift dive usually from south to north. Jumping at the southern part of the reef is a wall to about 30m covered with coral from the surface all the way down. There is a canyon going along the reef at about 25m which spreads out into a coral garden with sand alleys.

Thomas Reef is the smallest reef in the strait and diving here is governed by conditions as there are potential strong currents. The ends are vertical walls with a large plateau at about 25m on the south eastern side. This plateau is covered in colourful coral has a fence of gorgonian fans where you can find longnose hawkfish.

Gordon Reef is the most southerly reef of the four and has a different topography from the others offering both a shallow plateau area and drop offs. There is a huge variety of reef fish and the chance to see sleeping whitetip reef sharks on sand patches. At 4 to 5 metres there is an eel garden area along with coral encrusted drums. The top of the reef, with its lighthouse, is also home to the wreck Louilla which sits almost parallel to the wreck on Jackson Reef.

SS. Thistlegorm

Probably the most famous of the Red Sea wrecks. The 126.5m English Freighter was bombed by German aviation on 6th October 1941. Today she creates an artificial reef on a sandy bottom at 32m max depth. She is home to an enormous variety of marine life and is especially popular with large schooling fish.

Please note: Due to CDWS regulations, you must have a minimum of 20 logged dives in order to dive on this wreck. Other dives on the itinerary are not affected.

Ras Mohamed - Shark & Yolanda Reefs

This is a world renowned dive site, situated at the tip of the Sinai. Two small ergs are joined by a vertical wall dropping into the abyss. At Shark Reef the current allows you to drift along the wall, rich with colourful corals. Moving towards Yolanda Reef you reach a plateau scattered with small ergs and coral outcrops. Continuing around the reef you will come upon the scattered remains of the wreck 'Yolanda' complete with its cargo of toilets and baths. The whole of this area is big fish territory so keep an eye on the blue!

Gubal Island

At the gate of the Straits of Gubal is 'Bluff Point', which gets its name from the turbulence created by strong currents that beat the eastern wall of the island. The wreck of the 'Ulysses' lies on the reef 300m north of the lighthouse, starting at 5m and sloping to 25m. 'The Barge' wreck, south of the lighthouse, provides divers with a fun and unusual night dive. The wrecks skeleton creates protection for all types of night creatures.

my-blue-seas::brothers-daedalus-elphinst.highlightsDescription: This classic 7-night itinerary links three of the most iconic dive sites in the Egyptian Red Sea: the Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef, and Elphinstone. Designed for experienced divers, the route features dramatic drop-offs, lush coral walls, historic wrecks, and thrilling encounters with pelagic species. Big Brother is home to the famous wrecks Numidia and Aida II, now vibrant artificial reefs. Small Brother offers dense coral formations and frequent sightings of hammerheads, threshers, and silky sharks. Daedalus Reef is known for schooling hammerheads and vast hard coral formations, while Elphinstone adds the chance to see oceanic whitetip sharks and enjoy exhilarating drift dives along steep, current-swept walls.

days.description:
• Safety briefing, crew introduction, necessary dive paperwork, cabin allocation and ship orientation will take place before departing the harbor.
  • Journey to the first dive site for a check dive. Please take this opportunity to familiarize yourself with the vessel and make yourself comfortable. 
  • Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforeseeable factors.

• Explore three of the finest dive sites in the Red Sea. A great all-round tour for divers with slightly more experience.
  • There is so much to see that you’re spoilt for choice, but don’t forget to keep an eye out in the blue.
  • This safari offers challenging dives, big drop offs, beautiful coral walls and plenty of large fish. Brother Islands, Daedalus & Elphinstone is a must for all die-hard Red Sea divers!
  • Night dives in Marine Park are generally not allowed.

Brother Islands

  • Big Brother: A 400 meter long island offering fabulous wreck diving and wall diving. The wreck of the Numidia lies on the northern tip between 10 and 80 meter.
  • The north-west side of the island houses the wreck of the Aida. On every section of this reef the wall is covered with corals and life.
  • Little Brother: Boasts a very high concentration of life within a very small area.
  • Fan coral forests, overhangs, hard and soft corals in a variety of astonishing colors… and of course there are plenty of fish! With regular sightings of hammerheads, thresher sharks, grey sharks and white tip reef sharks, at the right time of year.

Daedalus

  • About 180 km south of the Brother Islands, this huge reef is surrounded by a sheer wall and strong currents allowing for fantastic drift diving. The hard corals grow to huge sizes but make sure you also keep an eye on the blue!

Elphinstone Reef

  • A Red Sea legend. One of the most beautiful reefs, with its north and south plateau’s covered in hard and soft corals and visiting pelagic, this truly is an awesome reef.
  • All dives sites are subject to weather conditions and the final route taken is at the absolute discretion of the captain and dive guides.

• 2 dives in the morning depending on guest flight schedules and the 24 hour requirement before flying.

  • In the afternoon the boat will enter the harbour
  • Dinner on board
  • Take advantage of an evening onshore to purchase souvenirs and enjoy Egypt's famous hospitality before your journey home the next day.

• Breakfast and check out 
  • Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

Safety briefing, crew introduction, necessary dive paperwork, cabin allocation and ship orientation will take place before departing the harbor.

Journey to the first dive site for a check dive. Please take this opportunity to familiarize yourself with the vessel and make yourself comfortable. 

Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforeseeable factors.

3 dives each day

Explore three of the Red Sea’s premier dive sites on this thrilling safari, perfect for experienced divers. With dramatic drop-offs, vibrant coral walls, and abundant marine life, it's a must for dedicated Red Sea enthusiasts.

Brother Islands

Big Brother features spectacular wall diving and two legendary wrecks: Numidia and Aida. Its coral-covered walls teem with marine life. Little Brother, though smaller, offers rich biodiversity, with fan corals, colorful overhangs, and regular sightings of hammerheads, threshers, and grey reef sharks.

Daedalus

Located 180 km south of the Brothers, this vast reef offers drift diving along sheer walls adorned with massive hard corals. Keep an eye out for pelagic species in the blue.

Elphinstone Reef

A true Red Sea icon, famous for its stunning north and south plateaus draped in hard and soft corals. Pelagic encounters are frequent at this awe-inspiring site.

Night dives in Marine Park areas are generally not permitted. Routes depend on weather conditions and the captain’s discretion.

Two morning dives are planned, considering flight schedules and the 24-hour no-fly rule.

In the afternoon, the boat arrives in Hurghada. Guests can enjoy dinner on board and spend the evening ashore for souvenirs and local hospitality.

Breakfast and check out

Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

my-blue-seas::daedalus-fury-shoal.highlightsDescription:
The Daedalus & Fury Shoals itinerary offers a thrilling 7-night adventure for experienced divers, featuring challenging dives, dramatic drop-offs, and vibrant coral walls. Explore Sha’ab Claudio’s shallow swim-throughs with sunlight filtering through caverns, and encounter a variety of marine life including rays, Napoleon wrasse, and possibly even a white tip reef shark or turtle.

Sha’ab Sataya, known as the ‘Dolphin House,’ is famous for its steep drop-offs and large pods of spinner dolphins, while Elphinstone Reef delivers an unforgettable dive with its rich coral coverage and pelagic visitors. Daedalus Reef, located 180 km south of the Brother Islands, presents exhilarating drift dives along its sheer walls. This tour offers a mix of challenging dives and marine wildlife encounters, all guided by weather conditions and the captain's discretion. The safari starts and ends in Port Ghalib.

my-blue-seas::daedalus-zabargad-rockys.highlightsDescription:
Daedalus, Rocky, and Zabargad offer the ultimate Red Sea diving adventure, combining world-renowned sites like Elphinstone, Daedalus Reef, and the unique islands of Zabargad and Rocky. This itinerary features breathtaking walls, vibrant coral gardens, and encounters with pelagic marine life.

Elphinstone's legendary plateaus are teeming with hard and soft corals, while Daedalus Reef promises thrilling drift dives along its towering walls. Zabargad enchants with its lagoon, circling reef, and hidden wrecks, while Rocky Island captivates with steep drop-offs and diverse marine life near the surface.

As night diving and snorkeling are restricted in marine parks, this itinerary focuses on exceptional day dives, ensuring unforgettable underwater experiences. Routes depend on weather and are guided by the captain and dive leaders for optimal diving conditions.

my-blue-seas::north-brothers-hurghada-hu.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary explores Egypt's remote southern Red Sea, combining the spectacular reefs of Zabargad Island with some of the region's most pristine offshore dive sites. Crystal-clear waters, colourful coral gardens and dramatic walls create an unforgettable diving experience far from the busier northern routes.

Zabargad is renowned for its impressive reef systems, vibrant hard and soft corals, turtles, eagle rays and occasional reef sharks. Depending on conditions, divers may also explore nearby reefs featuring steep drop-offs, coral pinnacles and excellent opportunities to encounter pelagic species.

With fewer boats operating in this remote region, divers can enjoy healthy reefs, exceptional visibility and a wide variety of marine life in one of Egypt's most rewarding diving destinations.

All dive sites are subject to weather conditions, and the captain and dive guides will determine the final route to ensure the best possible diving experience for everyone onboard.

my-blue-seas::north-tiran-dahab-hurghada.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary offers an unforgettable diving adventure in the northern Red Sea, showcasing some of the most famous dive sites in the region. The journey begins with the SS Thistlegorm wreck, one of the most iconic dives in the world, offering a fascinating glimpse into history and an abundance of marine life.

Next, explore the diverse reefs of Tiran, where crystal-clear waters reveal stunning coral gardens and schools of vibrant fish. Ras Mohamed National Park, a true highlight, offers dramatic drop-offs, vibrant coral walls, and the chance to encounter pelagic species, including reef sharks, barracudas, and eagle rays.

The itinerary also includes the remarkable wrecks of Abu Nuhas, with its shallow and deep dive sites offering thrilling exploration for divers of all levels. Routes are carefully planned by the captain and dive guides to ensure optimal diving conditions, making this trip a perfect blend of history, adventure, and spectacular underwater landscapes.

my-blue-seas::rocky-elba-stjohns-elphins.highlightsDescription: This 10-night safari explores some of the southern Red Sea’s most remote and spectacular dive sites. Departing from Port Ghalib, the itinerary includes the legendary walls of Elphinstone, the pristine coral gardens and tunnels of St. John’s, and the dramatic underwater landscapes around Rocky and Elba reefs. These areas are rarely visited, offering the chance to dive untouched reefs rich in hard corals, steep drop-offs, and vibrant marine life. Highlights include encounters with oceanic whitetip sharks, hammerheads, schools of barracuda, and possibly manta rays and dolphins. Expect a mix of drift dives, caverns, and pelagic action across some of Egypt’s most beautiful and biodiverse sites.
my-blue-seas::rocky-elba-stjohns-elphins.logistics:
Before the trip 

  • Arrival at the airport, The tour leader of Blue Planet Liveaboards will welcome you with a sign of Blue Planet Liveaboards. He can take care of your visa (stamp) that will be pasted in your passport.
  • After the check of the entry authority, you will go to the luggage claim.
  • It is possible a pick up from local hotel upon request
  • Transfer to the boat
  • Time for Transfer Airport Hurghada – Port Ghalib around 3 hrs. Airport Marsa Alam – Port Ghalib around 10 min.
  • Check in and check out on the boat. It goes without saying that we need time to load the boats, to clean and do small maintenance.
  • We ask for your cooperation on arrival day that check in can not be before 05:00 p.m. and the check out 10:00 a.m. at the latest.
  • If you check in before 05:00 p.m., please have consideration for the crew if they are still cleaning or loading the boat.
  • Because of organizational or technical reasons, perhaps you will have to stay in a hotel for the last night as our guest.
  • Meet the crew, assign cabins, something to eat ( depending time of arrival), and welcome briefing

After the trip

  • In the afternoon one day before departure, the boat will enter the harbour.
  • The luggage will be brought from the storage to prepare all your personal things.
  • The details for the return journey will be given to you from the staff of Blue Planet Liveaboards.

my-blue-seas::rocky-zabargad-stjohns-por.highlightsDescription: This 7-night itinerary combines the best of the northern Red Sea with vibrant reefs, famous wrecks, and the relaxed charm of Dahab. Departing and returning to Hurghada, the route typically includes Ras Mohamed National Park, the iconic wrecks of the Thistlegorm and Dunraven, and the rich coral gardens of Sha’ab El Erg and Abu Nuhas. In the Strait of Tiran, divers explore the reefs of Jackson, Thomas, Woodhouse, and Gordon—renowned for their strong currents, soft corals, and pelagic life. The tour also reaches Dahab, offering unique dives such as the Canyon and Blue Hole. Ideal for all levels, this safari delivers variety, color, and history in one of Egypt’s most beloved diving regions.

my-blue-seas::saint-john-3.highlightsDescription:
The St. Johns itinerary offers a more challenging dive experience, taking divers to stunning sites with dramatic drop-offs, massive gorgonians, and vibrant soft corals. Explore unique dive sites like Cave Reef, where tunnels and pinnacles await, and St. John’s Reef, featuring a variety of underwater landscapes such as drop-offs, tunnels, and hard-coral formations.

St. John’s Reef North invites you to explore more pinnacles and tunnels, while Fury Shoal provides a network of reefs with exciting caves, coral gardens, and plateaus, including the wreck of the 'Tug Boat' at Abu Galawa. This safari promises an unforgettable adventure, with the route adjusted based on weather conditions and the captain’s discretion for the best possible experience.

my-blue-seas::tiran-special-hurghada-hur.highlightsDescription:

Offering a diverse mix of reef, drift and wreck diving, it is suitable for divers looking to experience some of Egypt's most iconic underwater landscapes in a single trip.

The northern Red Sea features famous wrecks, thriving coral reefs and abundant marine life, while Safaga is known for its spectacular coral formations, healthy hard and soft corals, pinnacles and impressive drop-offs. Divers can expect encounters with turtles, reef sharks, moray eels, napoleon wrasse, eagle rays and large schools of reef fish.

With generally calm conditions and a wide variety of dive sites, this itinerary offers an excellent balance between scenic reef dives, fascinating wrecks and exciting marine life encounters.

All dive sites are subject to weather conditions, and the captain and dive guides will determine the final route to ensure the best possible diving experience for everyone onboard.

my-blue-seas::zabargad-special-port-ghal.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary explores the remote southern Red Sea, combining the dramatic reefs of Rocky Island, the colourful coral gardens of Zabargad and the extensive reef system of St. John's. It is designed for experienced divers seeking pristine dive sites, spectacular underwater landscapes and excellent opportunities to encounter pelagic marine life.

Rocky Island is renowned for its steep walls, strong currents and frequent shark encounters, while Zabargad offers vibrant coral reefs, turtles and abundant reef fish. St. John's completes the itinerary with its maze of pinnacles, caverns, tunnels and coral gardens, providing exceptional diversity throughout the week.

With minimal surface traffic and some of Egypt's healthiest coral reefs, this itinerary delivers an unforgettable southern Red Sea diving experience.

All dive sites are subject to weather conditions, and the captain and dive guides will determine the final route to ensure the best possible diving experience for everyone onboard.

my-blue-storm::brothers-daedalus-elphins.highlightsDescription:
This classic Red Sea route combines the most iconic wrecks of the north with the dramatic offshore walls of the Brother Islands. The trip begins and ends in Hurghada, giving easy access to historic sites such as the SS Thistlegorm, one of the world’s most famous wreck dives, as well as the fascinating wreck graveyard of Abu Nuhas with its multiple ships lying in shallow, turquoise waters.

As the itinerary moves south toward the offshore marine park, the focus shifts from wrecks to walls. Big Brother and Small Brother rise sharply from deep water and are known for their vibrant soft corals, powerful currents, and regular sightings of pelagic species. Encounters with oceanic whitetip sharks, threshers, and schooling fish are possible, along with beautifully decorated coral plateaus alive with anthias and fusiliers.

Depending on conditions, dives may also include Ras Mohamed National Park with its steep drop-offs and dense marine life, as well as colorful fringing reefs along the way. The exact routing is always adjusted based on weather and the experience of the group to ensure safe and enjoyable dives.

Ideal for advanced divers who enjoy a mix of wrecks, reefs, deep walls, and big-fish encounters, this itinerary offers some of the very best that the Egyptian Red Sea has to offer over the course of a full week at sea.

my-blue-storm::brothers-daedalus-elphins.highlightsDescription:
Embark on a 7-night journey through some of the Red Sea’s most celebrated dive sites—Brothers, Daedalus, and Elphinstone. This itinerary is ideal for experienced divers seeking thrilling adventures and unforgettable underwater encounters. With dramatic drop-offs, vibrant coral walls, and the chance to spot a variety of large pelagic species, every dive promises to be an extraordinary experience.

Big Brother offers a unique combination of wall diving and wreck exploration. The Numidia and Aida wrecks, both encrusted with marine life, lie at varying depths and provide a fascinating glimpse into the past. Little Brother, though smaller in size, is teeming with marine biodiversity. Fan coral forests, colorful soft corals, and frequent sightings of sharks, including hammerheads, threshers, and white tips, make this dive site truly spectacular.

Daedalus Reef, located about 180 km south of the Brother Islands, offers sheer walls, immense hard corals, and exhilarating drift dives. Keep a watchful eye on the blue for manta rays, sharks, and schools of fish passing by.

Finally, Elphinstone Reef, a legend of the Red Sea, captivates divers with its north and south plateaus blanketed in hard and soft corals. The reef is a hotspot for pelagic species and a photographer’s dream with its dazzling underwater scenery.

All dive sites are subject to weather conditions, and the captain and dive guides will determine the final route to ensure the best experience for everyone onboard.

my-blue-storm::north-brothers-hurghada-h.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night liveaboard safari begins and ends in Hurghada and explores two of the Red Sea’s most iconic regions: the northern reefs and the legendary Strait of Tiran. The route combines drift dives, vibrant coral gardens, dramatic walls and the chance to explore historic wrecks, making it ideal for divers who want variety and strong marine life encounters.

The trip typically includes dives around the northern reefs near Hurghada, where you can expect healthy hard-coral plateaus, sheltered bays and impressive drop-offs. Conditions often allow for relaxed dives with abundant reef fish, moray eels, blue-spotted rays and occasional turtles or dolphins.

Further north, the itinerary continues toward the Strait of Tiran, a world-class diving area situated between the Sinai Peninsula and Tiran Island. Here you will explore famous sites such as Thomas Reef, Gordon Reef, Woodhouse Reef and Laguna Reef. These reefs are known for their steep walls covered with soft corals, towering gorgonians, schools of snappers and fusiliers, and the possibility of spotting reef sharks or large pelagics cruising in the blue.

Depending on weather and current, the itinerary may also include wreck dives such as the Lovilla or Kormoran, adding a historical and adventurous element to the safari. Most days offer three to four dives, including early-morning dives when the reefs are at their most active, and night dives when conditions permit.

The exact selection of sites and the sequence of visits depend on wind, sea state and the experience level of the group. This route provides an engaging mix of landscapes and conditions, making it suitable for divers who enjoy diverse environments from shallow coral gardens to deep vertical walls.

Daedalus, Rocky, and Zabargad offer the ultimate Red Sea diving adventure, combining world-renowned sites like Elphinstone, Daedalus Reef, and the unique islands of Zabargad and Rocky. This itinerary features breathtaking walls, vibrant coral gardens, and encounters with pelagic marine life.

As night diving and snorkeling are restricted in marine parks, this itinerary focuses on exceptional day dives, ensuring unforgettable underwater experiences. Routes depend on weather and are guided by the captain and dive leaders for optimal diving conditions.

my-blue-storm::north-safaga-hurghada-hur.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary explores some of the northern Red Sea's most celebrated reefs while extending into the Gulf of Aqaba to visit the spectacular reefs of Tiran and Dahab. Combining colourful coral gardens, dramatic walls and historic wrecks, it offers an exciting variety of dive experiences suitable for experienced recreational divers.

The vibrant reefs of Tiran are famous for their crystal-clear waters, thriving coral formations and frequent encounters with turtles, eagle rays, barracuda and reef sharks. Around Dahab, dramatic underwater landscapes, steep drop-offs and healthy coral reefs create unforgettable dives rich in marine biodiversity. Together with the classic northern Red Sea sites, the itinerary provides an excellent mix of reef, drift and wreck diving.

Changing currents, excellent visibility and abundant marine life make this one of the most varied Red Sea itineraries, with every day offering new underwater scenery and exciting encounters.

All dive sites are subject to weather conditions, and the captain and dive guides will determine the final route to ensure the best possible diving experience for everyone onboard.

my-blue-storm::north-tiran-dahab-hurghad.highlightsDescription:
This classic 7-night itinerary explores the northern Red Sea's most famous wrecks and reefs, combining fascinating maritime history with vibrant coral reefs and diverse marine life. Ideal for divers with some experience, it offers an excellent mix of wreck penetration opportunities, scenic reef dives and relaxed cruising with short sailing distances between dive sites.

Highlights include the legendary SS Thistlegorm, widely regarded as one of the world's finest wreck dives, the beautifully preserved Rosalie Moller, and the famous Abu Nuhas reef, home to the wrecks of Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K and Kimon M. The itinerary also visits scenic reefs around Gubal Island, where colourful soft corals, gorgonians and abundant reef life attract barracuda, reef sharks and numerous macro species.

This itinerary offers the perfect balance between history and marine life, with opportunities to explore some of the Red Sea's most iconic wrecks alongside healthy coral reefs teeming with tropical fish.

All dive sites are subject to weather conditions, and the captain and dive guides will determine the final route to ensure the best possible diving experience for everyone onboard.

The Daedalus & Fury Shoals itinerary offers a thrilling 7-night adventure for experienced divers, featuring challenging dives, dramatic drop-offs, and vibrant coral walls. Explore Sha’ab Claudio’s shallow swim-throughs with sunlight filtering through caverns, and encounter a variety of marine life including rays, Napoleon wrasse, and possibly even a white tip reef shark or turtle.

Sha’ab Sataya, known as the ‘Dolphin House,’ is famous for its steep drop-offs and large pods of spinner dolphins, while Elphinstone Reef delivers an unforgettable dive with its rich coral coverage and pelagic visitors. Daedalus Reef, located 180 km south of the Brother Islands, presents exhilarating drift dives along its sheer walls. This tour offers a mix of challenging dives and marine wildlife encounters, all guided by weather conditions and the captain's discretion. The safari starts and ends in Port Ghalib.

my-carlton::northeren-route-wrecks-7-nig.highlightsDescription:
This 4-night Red Sea liveaboard combines the world-famous reefs of Ras Mohamed National Park with the spectacular coral formations of the Tiran Strait. Designed for certified divers looking for a short but action-packed safari, the itinerary offers a mix of colorful reef walls, thriving marine life, drift dives, and iconic wrecks.

Ras Mohamed is renowned for its dramatic drop-offs, nutrient-rich currents, and dense schools of reef fish, while Tiran's reefs are famous for their vibrant coral gardens, steep walls, and frequent encounters with pelagic species. Depending on conditions, divers may encounter barracuda, giant trevallies, tuna, turtles, eagle rays, and reef sharks.

The route also often includes visits to some of the northern Red Sea's most celebrated wrecks, offering a fascinating blend of natural reefs and maritime history. With up to three dives per day, optional night dives where permitted, and comfortable onboard accommodation, this itinerary is ideal for both first-time liveaboard guests and experienced Red Sea enthusiasts.

Thistlegorm & Dolphins

Wrecks & Shark Reef

Southern & Tiran Reefs

Dives at Ras Um Sid, Jackson Reef, and Gordon Reef. Night dive.

Straits of Tiran

Diving at Thomas Reef, Woodhouse Reef, and Jackson Reef. Night dive.

Local Reefs & Return

Morning dives at Ras Um Sid and Ras Katy, followed by return cruise to Travco Jetty. Last night onboard.

my-carlton::tiran-ras-mohamed-minisafari.highlightsDescription:
This 2-night mini safari is a compact yet action-packed Red Sea escape, combining some of the region’s most iconic wrecks with the vibrant reefs of Ras Mohamed. Departing from Sharm El Sheikh, the itinerary is designed to maximise underwater time in a short window, with a balanced mix of wreck diving, reef exploration, and optional sunset or night dives depending on conditions.

Highlights include multiple dives on the legendary SS Thistlegorm, widely regarded as one of the world’s top wreck dives, as well as famous sites such as Shark & Yolanda Reef, Temple, Small Crack, and Ras Ghozlani. Divers can expect colourful coral gardens, abundant marine life, schooling fish, and dramatic underwater landscapes throughout the trip.

Ideal for divers with limited time who still want a true liveaboard experience, this mini safari offers excellent value, efficient routing, and a high concentration of signature Red Sea dive sites, all while enjoying the comfort and convenience of a short liveaboard cruise.

Between dives, relax on board and enjoy the hospitality of your liveaboard while cruising through the crystal-clear waters of the Red Sea. This short but unforgettable safari offers a perfect mix of wreck and reef diving in one of Egypt’s most renowned diving destinations.

my-discovery-i::brothers-daedalus-and-el.highlightsDescription:
The Brother Islands (El Akhawein) are the pinnacles of two undersea mountains rising from the depths of the abyss 300m deep and are located about 60 miles offshore. Big Brother, which is easily identified with it’s lighthouse, is about 100 metres across and 400 metres in length, with two extremities to the east and west. Little Brother lies about 800 metres east of Big Brother.

As part of the Marine Park Islands National Park, these islands offer stunning wall diving and a breath-taking display of colour with their rich variety of soft corals and gorgonians which cover the walls. You will find large and small fish here in abundance; tuna, barracuda, shoals of snappers and jack fish, as well a hammerheads, silky and oceanic white tip sharks, even the occasional thresher shark and manta ray. Sightings of the Grey Reef Shark are almost guaranteed on the North and South Plateaux of Small Brother.

For the wreck diver, the wrecks of the Aida II, an 82 m long Egyptian supply vessel that sank in 1957, and the Numidia, a cargo ship carrying locomotive spare parts to India, lie on the walls of the Big Brother. Both are covered in a rich growth of soft and hard corals. Marine life includes a family of Napoleon Wrasse and Grey Reef Sharks.

Daedalus Reef, also part of the Marine Park, is a large, oval reef with a lighthouse and is the furthest offshore reef in the Egyptian Red Sea. Its deep walls and drop-offs offer some of the most spectacular diving to be found. Daedalus has mountainous, pristine, hard coral formations. There is also a strong chance of spotting schooling Hammerheads, and grey reef sharks.

Elphinstone, with its shear walls covered in soft corals, offers a likely encounter with Grey Reef Sharks circling on the plateaux and even Oceanic White Tip Sharks can be seen here for most of the year.

my-discovery-i::brothers-daedalus-and-el.highlightsDescription:
The Brother Islands (El Akhawein) are the pinnacles of two undersea mountains rising from the depths of the abyss 300m deep and are located about 60 miles offshore. Big Brother, which is easily identified with it’s lighthouse, is about 100 metres across and 400 metres in length, with two extremities to the east and west. Little Brother lies about 800 metres east of Big Brother.

As part of the Marine Park Islands National Park, these islands offer stunning wall diving and a breath-taking display of colour with their rich variety of soft corals and gorgonians which cover the walls. You will find large and small fish here in abundance; tuna, barracuda, shoals of snappers and jack fish, as well a hammerheads, silky and oceanic white tip sharks, even the occasional thresher shark and manta ray. Sightings of the Grey Reef Shark are almost guaranteed on the North and South Plateaux of Small Brother.

For the wreck diver, the wrecks of the Aida II, an 82 m long Egyptian supply vessel that sank in 1957, and the Numidia, a cargo ship carrying locomotive spare parts to India, lie on the walls of the Big Brother. Both are covered in a rich growth of soft and hard corals. Marine life includes a family of Napoleon Wrasse and Grey Reef Sharks.

Daedalus Reef, also part of the Marine Park, is a large, oval reef with a lighthouse and is the furthest offshore reef in the Egyptian Red Sea. Its deep walls and drop-offs offer some of the most spectacular diving to be found. Daedalus has mountainous, pristine, hard coral formations. There is also a strong chance of spotting schooling Hammerheads, and grey reef sharks.

Elphinstone, with its shear walls covered in soft corals, offers a likely encounter with Grey Reef Sharks circling on the plateaux and even Oceanic White Tip Sharks can be seen here for most of the year.

my-discovery-i::brothers-mghrg-7-nights.highlightsDescription:
This Red Sea diving safari offers a mixed itinerary of wreck diving and reef diving. You will visit the most impressive wrecks in the Northern Red Sea, as well as stunning reef diving.

This cruise has something for everyone. Starting from Hurghada and sailing north gives a perfect combination of reef diving and wreck diving. The famous horseshoe shaped reef of Shaab El Erg is a perfect example of the reefs with its beautiful hard coral garden and the chance to see dolphins. Abu Nuhas has four well-known wrecks: Giannis D, Carnatic, the lentil wreck and the tile wreck, all offering spectacular dives and plenty of fish life.

The Northern Red Sea's impressive array of wrecks won't disappoint. You'll visit the Dunraven and the world-famous Thistlegorm, a World War II shipwreck. Gubal Island, with at least four intriguing wreck sites, teems with big fish like barracuda, turtles, and eagle rays.

Night dives can be superb in this area Gubal Island offers protected anchoring for the night. A small wreck at 8-10 metres makes for a spectacular night dive with lionfish, scorpion fish and its resident giant moray eel.

To the south, you'll find Ras Mohammed, Egypt's first marine protected area and national park, renowned for its vibrant soft coral walls and bustling marine life.

The Brother Islands are the pinnacles of two undersea mountains rising from the depths of the abyss and are located about 60 miles offshore from El Quesir. Part of the Marine Park Islands National Park, these islands offer stunning wall diving, with the walls being covered in soft corals and forests of gorgonians, creating a kaleidoscope of ever-changing colours. They attract a diverse array of marine species and large pelagics. Large tuna, Baracudas, Jacks and Snappers cruise in the blue, accompanied by occasional Hammerheads, Silky and Oceanic White Tip Sharks and Mantas. Even the rare Thresher Shark can sometimes be found there. Sightings of the Grey Reef Shark are almost guaranteed on the North and South Plateau of Small Brother.

For the wreck diver, the wrecks of the Aida II, an Egyptian supply vessel, and the Numidia, a cargo ship, lie on the walls of the Big Brother. Both are covered in a rich growth of soft and hard corals. Marine life includes a family of Napoleon Wrasse and Grey Reef Sharks.The boat will then sail back to Hurghada via Safaga where you can dive at Panorama Reef or the famous wreck of Salem Express for a memorable finale !

my-discovery-i::daedalus-rocky-and-zabar.highlightsDescription:
Further south are the spectacular overhangs and deep walls of Rocky Island and the abundance of soft coral and spectacular coral pinnacles at Zabargad.

Zabargad Island is a wonderful dive site offering wall diving, a wreck and shallow areas with dozens of slender coral towers. Here live a great many tropical groupers, which are easily approached and photographed during a dive without equals in its category. When diving here at night you will find octopus, crustaceans and nudibranchs emerge to crowd through the coral grottos.

Rocky Island is a small fossil-coral island that emerges from the surface, elliptical in shape, surrounded by a surface level reef. The island sinks it walls down to more that 1000 metres of water. The walls are covered in soft corals and huge gorgonians which float and wave in the current. It is possible to sight many species of shark here as well as sailfish, dolphins and manta rays.

St John’s is a beautiful reef system which lies approx. 40km north of the Sudanese border and 20km South of Zabargad. It is a vast collection of small reefs offering some of the most remote and rewarding diving in the Red Sea. Habili Ali offers giant gorgonians and black corals whilst Grey Reef, Silvertip and schools of Hammerhead sharks might be found on the west side. Habili Gafaar is a mass of soft corals teaming with shoals of Snappers, Butterfly Fish and Barracudas. Mantas, Oceanic White Tip, Grey Reef and Silvertip Sharks can be seen in the blue. Gota Kebir is a massive reef, famous for its tunnels and south plateau where Jacks and Barracudas can be seen and the occasional Manta. The tunnels are ideal for novice cave divers.

Gota Soraya is rated as possibly one of the best wall dives in the Red Sea, with overhangs and cracks in the reef wall full of Glass Fish and Sweepers and an abundance of corals, Grey Reef, Silvertip, Oceanic White Tip and Hammerheads.

Elphinstone, with its shear walls covered in soft corals, offers a likely encounter with Grey Reef Sharks circling on the plateaux and even Oceanic White Tip Sharks can be seen here for most of the year.

my-discovery-i::deep-south-and-elphinsto.highlightsDescription:
At Fury Shoals, dive Shaab Claude with its famous swim-throughs and huge porite corals. White Tip Reef sharks and an anemone and clownfish settlement can be seen a little off the reef to the South. Abu Galawa Soraya has a fantastic coral garden and a wreck of a private sailing boat packed with glass fish.

Dive Shab Sharm, with its wall dives and White Tip Reef sharks. Oceanic White Tips and Silky sharks can sometimes be found in the blue and turtles often visit the South side before heading further south to Wadi Gamal, with its flowing banks of hard yellow and green soft coral, resident angel and butterfly fish, and in the right season huge schools of placid jack and tuna visit the area.

St John’s is a vast collection of small reefs offering some of the most remote and rewarding diving in the Red Sea. Habili Ali offers giant gorgonians and black corals whilst Grey Reef, Silvertip and schools of Hammerhead sharks might be found on the west side. Gota Soraya is rated as possibly one of the best wall dives in the Red Sea, with overhangs and cracks in the reef wall full of glass fish and sweepers and an abundance of corals, Grey Reef, Silvertips and Hammerhead sharks.

my-discovery-i::north-wrecks-and-ras-moh.highlightsDescription:
This Red Sea diving safari offers a mixed itinerary of wreck diving and reef diving. You will visit the most impressive wrecks in the Northern Red Sea, as well as stunning reef diving.

This cruise has something for everyone. Starting from Hurghada and sailing north gives a perfect combination of reef diving and wreck diving. The famous horseshoe shaped reef of Shaab El Erg is a perfect example of the reefs on offer on this cruise with its beautiful hard coral garden and the chance to see dolphins. Abu Nuhas has four well-known wrecks: Giannis D, Carnatic, the lentil wreck and the tile wreck, all offering spectacular dives and plenty of fish life.

The Northern Red Sea's impressive array of wrecks won't disappoint. You'll visit the Dunraven and the world-famous Thistlegorm, a World War II shipwreck. Gubal Island, with at least four intriguing wreck sites, teems with big fish like barracuda, turtles, and eagle rays.

Night dives can be superb in this area Gubal Island offers protected anchoring for the night. A small wreck at 8-10 metres makes for a spectacular night dive with lionfish, scorpion fish and its resident giant moray eel.

To the south, you'll find Ras Mohammed, Egypt's first marine protected area and national park, renowned for its vibrant soft coral walls and bustling marine life.

Expect to make between three and four dives per day, including night dives.

my-discovery-ii::brothers-daedalus-elphi.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary showcases some of the most thrilling dive sites in the Egyptian Red Sea, renowned for their dramatic walls, rich marine life, and legendary shipwrecks.

The Brothers Islands rise from the depths of a 300-meter abyss, forming pinnacles teeming with life. Big Brother, marked by its iconic lighthouse, and Little Brother offer stunning wall dives adorned with soft corals and gorgonians. Divers can expect encounters with schools of tuna, barracuda, snappers, and jacks, alongside hammerheads, silky sharks, and oceanic white tips. Thresher sharks and manta rays make occasional appearances, while Grey Reef Sharks are almost guaranteed at Small Brother's plateaux. Wreck enthusiasts can explore the coral-encrusted Aida II and Numidia wrecks on Big Brother, home to Napoleon wrasse and vibrant marine life.

Daedalus Reef, an oval-shaped marine park site with a lighthouse, is known for its pristine hard coral formations and dramatic drop-offs. It’s a prime spot for schooling hammerheads and grey reef sharks.

Elphinstone, famous for its sheer walls blanketed in soft corals, offers close encounters with grey reef sharks and oceanic white tips, which frequent the site most of the year.

This route combines awe-inspiring underwater landscapes, diverse marine life, and unforgettable wreck dives, making it a must for adventure-seeking divers.

my-discovery-ii::brothers-daedalus-elphi.highlightsDescription:
Explore the wild and remote southern Red Sea on this 7-night itinerary combining the legendary reefs of St. Johns, the vibrant Fury Shoals, and the iconic Elphinstone Reef. Departing from Port Ghalib, this route offers a perfect balance of pristine coral gardens, dramatic walls, and thrilling pelagic encounters.

Fury Shoals welcomes divers with colorful reefs, swim-throughs, and abundant marine life, including reef sharks, turtles, and large schools of reef fish. Moving further south, St. Johns reveals some of the most untouched and rewarding dive sites in Egypt, with labyrinths of pinnacles, caves, and drop-offs where hammerheads, grey reef sharks, and oceanic whitetips may appear.

The itinerary also includes Elphinstone, one of the Red Sea’s most famous dive sites, known for its steep walls, soft corals, and frequent sightings of oceanic whitetip sharks and schooling pelagics. Throughout the week, expect a mix of relaxed reef dives and more challenging drift dives, all set against spectacular underwater scenery.

This itinerary is ideal for experienced divers seeking variety, big fish encounters, and access to some of the Red Sea’s most celebrated and remote dive locations.

my-discovery-ii::brothers-hurghada-hurgh.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary showcases some of the most thrilling dive sites in the Egyptian Red Sea, renowned for their dramatic walls, rich marine life, and legendary shipwrecks.

The Brothers Islands rise from the depths of a 300-meter abyss, forming pinnacles teeming with life. Big Brother, marked by its iconic lighthouse, and Little Brother offer stunning wall dives adorned with soft corals and gorgonians. Divers can expect encounters with schools of tuna, barracuda, snappers, and jacks, alongside hammerheads, silky sharks, and oceanic white tips. Thresher sharks and manta rays make occasional appearances, while Grey Reef Sharks are almost guaranteed at Small Brother's plateaux. Wreck enthusiasts can explore the coral-encrusted Aida II and Numidia wrecks on Big Brother, home to Napoleon wrasse and vibrant marine life.

Daedalus Reef, an oval-shaped marine park site with a lighthouse, is known for its pristine hard coral formations and dramatic drop-offs. It’s a prime spot for schooling hammerheads and grey reef sharks.

Elphinstone, famous for its sheer walls blanketed in soft corals, offers close encounters with grey reef sharks and oceanic white tips, which frequent the site most of the year.

This route combines awe-inspiring underwater landscapes, diverse marine life, and unforgettable wreck dives, making it a must for adventure-seeking divers.

my-discovery-ii::north-and-brothers-4.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night Red Sea safari is a diverse journey through wrecks, reefs, and marine parks, offering something for every diver. Departing from Hurghada, it combines the iconic wrecks of the north, vibrant reefs, and deeper adventures in the Brothers and Safaga regions.

Explore the legendary wrecks of Abu Nuhas, including the Giannis D and Carnatic, Ras Mohamed National Park offers dramatic drop-offs teeming with soft corals and vibrant marine life, while the reefs of Tiran, such as Jackson and Thomas, showcase thriving biodiversity and the chance to encounter pelagics like sharks and barracudas.

Heading south, the Brothers Islands promise thrilling wall dives and encounters with hammerheads, oceanic whitetips, and grey reef sharks. Safaga’s highlights, like Panorama Reef and the wreck of the Salem Express, feature colorful coral gardens and abundant marine life, perfect for both beginners and experienced divers.

This itinerary offers a balanced mix of wreck diving, reef exploration, and big pelagic encounters, ensuring a dynamic and unforgettable Red Sea experience.

my-discovery-ii::north-wrecks-ras-mohame.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night Red Sea safari combines thrilling wreck dives, stunning reef explorations, and iconic marine parks, offering an unforgettable diving adventure. Departing from Hurghada, the route takes you to the Northern Red Sea's most famous underwater treasures.

Explore the captivating wrecks of Abu Nuhas, including the Giannis D, Carnatic, the lentil wreck, and the tile wreck, each brimming with marine life. The reefs are equally stunning, with highlights like Shaab El Erg, a horseshoe-shaped reef renowned for its vibrant coral gardens and frequent dolphin sightings.

Ras Mohamed, a protected marine reserve, offers dramatic drop-offs adorned with colorful soft corals and an incredible variety of fish. Tiran’s vibrant reefs, such as Jackson and Thomas, showcase rich biodiversity, from schooling fish to larger pelagics like barracudas and sharks.

Gubal Island provides a sheltered spot for night dives, featuring a shallow wreck at 8-10 meters where lionfish, scorpionfish, and a resident giant moray eel create a memorable scene.

This itinerary offers the perfect mix of history, marine biodiversity, and scenic underwater landscapes, making it ideal for all divers.

my-discovery-ii::rocky-zabargad-st-johns.highlightsDescription:
Experience the ultimate southern Red Sea adventure on this 7-night itinerary combining the legendary Daedalus Reef with the remote islands of Rocky and Zabargad, and the iconic Elphinstone Reef. Departing from Port Ghalib, this route is designed for experienced divers seeking strong currents, dramatic drop-offs, and unforgettable big fish encounters.

Daedalus Reef, one of the most famous offshore sites in Egypt, offers breathtaking walls covered in hard corals and a high likelihood of encounters with schooling hammerheads, grey reef sharks, and other pelagics. Its remote location ensures pristine conditions and thrilling drift dives.

Further south, Rocky Island and Zabargad showcase some of the Red Sea’s most untouched reefs. Expect steep walls, vibrant soft corals, and excellent visibility, with frequent sightings of oceanic whitetip sharks, silvertips, manta rays, and large schools of fish. These sites are renowned for their raw beauty and consistent action in the blue.

The itinerary also includes Elphinstone Reef, famous for its sheer walls and coral-covered plateaus. Here, divers often encounter oceanic whitetip sharks and schooling pelagics, providing an exciting and memorable highlight to the trip.

This itinerary offers a perfect blend of remote offshore reefs, pristine coral ecosystems, and exhilarating shark diving, making it ideal for advanced divers looking to explore the Red Sea at its most spectacular.

my-discovery-ii::st-johns-fury-shoal-elp.highlightsDescription:
Discover the wildest corners of Egypt’s southern Red Sea on this 7-night itinerary combining Rocky Island, Zabargad, St. John’s, and Elphinstone. Departing from Port Ghalib, this route is designed for experienced divers seeking dramatic underwater landscapes and consistent encounters with pelagic marine life.

The journey begins in the far south at Rocky Island and Zabargad, where steep walls, coral pinnacles, and crystal-clear waters create ideal conditions for spotting grey reef sharks, silvertips, oceanic whitetips, and even manta rays. These remote sites are known for their pristine reefs, soft coral coverage, and strong currents that attract large predators.

Further north, St. John’s offers an incredible variety of dive sites, from labyrinthine reef systems and caves to drop-offs rich in marine life. Expect vibrant coral gardens, schools of barracuda and snapper, and frequent shark sightings, making this area one of the most rewarding in the Red Sea.

The itinerary concludes with Elphinstone Reef, one of Egypt’s most iconic dive sites. Its sheer walls and coral-covered plateaus are famous for encounters with oceanic whitetip sharks and schooling pelagics, providing a thrilling finale to the trip.

This itinerary delivers a perfect mix of remote exploration, big fish action, and world-class reef diving, ideal for divers looking to experience the Red Sea at its most untamed.

my-grand-discovery::bde-hurghada-hurghad.highlightsDescription:
This itinerary brings divers to three of the most renowned Marine Park sites in the Egyptian Red Sea: the Brother Islands, Daedalus Reef and Elphinstone Reef. Together, they offer a combination of dramatic topography, exceptional coral growth, thrilling pelagic encounters and historic wrecks.

The Brother Islands rise sharply from depths of around 300 meters and are known for their spectacular walls, which are densely covered in soft corals, gorgonians and vibrant marine life. Large schools of tuna, barracuda, snappers and jacks are frequently seen, as well as hammerheads, silky sharks, oceanic white tips and the occasional thresher shark or manta ray. Grey reef sharks are commonly spotted around the North and South plateaux of Small Brother. Big Brother is also home to two celebrated wrecks: the Aida II and the Numidia, both adorned with healthy coral growth and sheltering resident marine life, including Napoleon wrasse and grey reef sharks.

Daedalus Reef, the most remote offshore reef in Egypt, offers dramatic drop-offs and vast hard coral formations. Its isolation attracts larger pelagics, and divers have very good chances of encountering schooling hammerheads and grey reef sharks along the reef’s steep edges. The lighthouse above the reef adds a distinctive landmark to this iconic site.

Elphinstone Reef completes the route with its steep, coral-covered walls and narrow plateaux, where grey reef sharks are often seen circling. Oceanic white tip sharks are frequent visitors for most of the year, adding to the excitement of diving this long, slender reef. Soft corals are abundant, providing a colourful backdrop to every dive.

Overall, the BDE itinerary is suited to experienced divers seeking action-packed dives, pristine coral ecosystems and some of the Red Sea’s best opportunities for shark encounters.

my-grand-discovery::north-wrecks-ras-moh.highlightsDescription:
This extended northern itinerary combines some of the Red Sea’s most iconic wrecks, reefs and offshore marine-park sites into one comprehensive program. It offers a diverse mix of topography, history and pelagic encounters, suitable for experienced divers seeking variety and high-quality diving.

The northern section includes Abu Nuhas with well-known wrecks such as the Giannis D, along with colourful reef dives around Shaab Mahmoud and the Giftun area. The Strait of Tiran features the famous Jackson, Thomas, Gordon and Woodhouse reefs, known for their clear water, dramatic walls and the possibility of spotting pelagics along the drop-offs.

Ras Mohamed National Park delivers rich coral gardens, large fish schools and some of the most scenic diving in the region. The route also includes multiple dives on the legendary SS Thistlegorm, one of the world’s most iconic wrecks, allowing time to explore its holds, artifacts and resident marine life.

The itinerary then heads offshore to the Brother Islands, part of the Marine Park. Big Brother and Small Brother offer spectacular wall dives, dense soft corals, gorgonians and a high chance of encounters with grey reef sharks, hammerheads and other pelagic species. Big Brother also features historic wrecks such as the Numidia and Aida.

On the return south, Safaga provides further highlights including the Salem Express wreck and colourful reefs such as Panorama and Ras Abu Soma. Additional dives at Tubia Arbaa, Abu Ramada or the Giftun area offer relaxed coral gardens and sheltered conditions, often ideal for night dives.

This route blends diverse reef structures, offshore pinnacles, deep walls, and major wrecks, creating one of the most varied week-long itineraries available in the northern Red Sea. All dive sites remain subject to weather and marine-park conditions.

days.description:
Hurghada (Check-in & briefing)

Check-in on board in the late afternoon (between 17:00 and 23:30), cabin allocation, equipment setup and safety briefing. Dinner served on board. Overnight in Hurghada.

Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforseeable factors

Northern Hurghada

Two daytime dives on northern reefs and islands, followed by a night dive. Typical sites may include shallow lagoons, coral gardens and easy wrecks, ideal for a relaxed start.

Shaab Abu Nuhas area

Three daytime dives exploring the famous wrecks of Shaab Abu Nuhas (such as Giannis D, Carnatic or Chrisoula K, conditions permitting), plus a night dive. A highlight day for wreck lovers.

Islands & reefs north of Hurghada

Three daytime dives and a final night dive, with sites selected according to conditions. Possible areas include Siyul Islands, Umm Gamar, Shaab El Erg (Dolphin House) or nearby reefs.

Final dives & disembarkation

Two morning dives, then return to the marina in the afternoon. Check-out takes place between 15:00 and 19:00, respecting the 24-hour no-fly rule after the last dive.

Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

my-iceberg::hurghada-north-4-nights-5-da.highlightsDescription:
This 4-night liveaboard itinerary explores the northern Red Sea, combining relaxed reef diving with some of the area’s most famous wrecks. Departing from Hurghada, the route focuses on the sheltered northern reefs and island systems, making it suitable for a wide range of certified divers.

Highlights typically include the wrecks of Shaab Abu Nuhas, colourful coral gardens, shallow lagoons and the chance to encounter dolphins at sites such as Shaab El Erg. The itinerary offers a balanced pace with multiple dives per day, including night dives, and finishes with easy final dives to ensure a comfortable end to the trip.

The trip is ideal for beginners and experienced divers of all levels, as well as wreck enthusiasts and underwater photographers. It offers breathtaking diving in a relaxed safari atmosphere, with an emphasis on avoiding crowded sites whenever possible. By keeping distance from other boats, guests can enjoy unspoiled reefs, abundant marine life, and a peaceful diving experience with more fish than divers.

my-iceberg::hurghada-north-hurghada-hurg.highlightsDescription:
Special Wrecks – Hurghada North is a 4-night liveaboard safari dedicated to the most famous wrecks and northern dive sites of the Red Sea, combined with relaxed reef diving and night dives.

This itinerary focuses on the legendary wrecks of the Abu Nuhas area, offering the opportunity to explore historic ships covered in coral and teeming with marine life, alongside colorful northern reefs rich in fish activity. With a balanced pace and up to four dives per day including night dives, it is ideal for divers who want to maximize underwater time without long crossings.

The trip is perfect for beginners and experienced divers of all levels, wreck lovers, and underwater photographers. Careful planning allows the boat to avoid crowded sites whenever possible, creating a calm and enjoyable diving experience with more fish than divers. A classic Red Sea safari combining spectacular wrecks, vibrant reefs, and a relaxed onboard atmosphere.

days.description:
• Safety Briefing, Crew Introduction, Necessary Dive Paperwork, Cabin allocation and ship orientation will take place before departing the Harbour.
  • During the journey to our first dive site for a check dive, please take this opportunity to familiarize yourselves with the vessel and make yourself comfortable. 
  • Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforseeable factors
• The morning after your arrival, we will go to our first reef for our “put in fins“ dive. Explore the reef at leisure before you take off toward Brother islands in the late afternoon.

• You will wake up next to Small Brother where you will have an early morning dive.
  • After exploring the stunning drops off, cross the channel to dive around the big brother. Take the time to visit 2 stunning shipwrecks on the north, the south plateau and the fall.
  • You could also go on the island to visit the 31m high military lighthouse built in 1883 by the English. 
  • Reach the top after climbing 140 steps and 2 metallic scales. Enjoy the beautiful sunset.
  • Numidia Wreck is a 130 meters long and 6 400 tons wreck which has been on the northern tip of Big Brother since it sank in July 1901. The ship was making her first journey from Glasgow to India with railway material. Today it sits on the skew, al- most vertically, between 10 and 80 meters deep. Do not forget to look “in the blue“ so you can see gray sharks or hammerheads.
  • Then drift with the current on one or both sides of the reef.
  • Descend to admire this wreck covered with a large number of multicolored alcyonaires and teeming with life, especially in the hold. In the early morning, do not forget to look in the water to see gray sharks or hammerheads. This is their spot!
  • Aida II is a wreck of 1426 tons, sunk in 1957 northwest of Big Brother. The zodiac will drop you along the reef, before the wreck, in the direction of the current. You will descend along the wall down to 30 meters. You will see the wreck of Aida.
  • Discover a gaping hole from which hang ropes covered with multicolored alcyonnaires. If you look inside, you will be able to admire clouds of “glassfish“. You can continue your exploration and, coming by the back of the wreck, you will admire an explosion of colors. The railings covered with multicolored alcyonnaires transform the wreck into a beautiful garden.
  • Small Brother's North Plateau. Here you will have th ebest chance of spot gray sharks and hammerheads. It is even possible to cross a Manta ray and / or a moonfish (Mola-mola).
  • Leave the plateau and the deep zone to reach the western slope, which is full of life with alcyonarians of all colors, magnificent sea fans and an extremely varied fauna : groupers, barracudas ...
  • On this island, you have the chance to see an incredible number of shark species : gray reefs, white tips, silky, hammerhead, thresher, and of course, often near the surface, the one you all expect : the oceanic white tip.
• Begin the cruise after dinner to reach Deadalus 8 hours later.

• Take the chance to see hammerhead sharks early in the morning.
  • Possible visit to another english lighthouse from 1931.
  • To achieve the triangle, cruise to North/East and navigate towardsthe mythical reef of Elphinstone.
  • Daedalus's North Face is on the northern slope of Daedalus, which is the most exposed to the dominant current, here the most chances to make beautiful encounters with the pelagics.
  • Indeed it is very common here to encounter a school of hammerhead sharks composed of about twenty individuals. Trevallies and tunas are also very often seen..
  • Leave the deep zone to explore the falling area which requires great attention as
    it is full of overhangs. Observe many branches of black corals which colonized the reef. During your ascent,look at the surfaceand you will be able to see schools of barracudas.

• Elphinstone's North Plateau, jump in the water early in the morning. Descend along the reef to reach the plateau twenty meters deeper. You will see an impressive life. Follow the plateau down to 40 meters. There, around the fault and in the current hammerhead sharks and gray reefs can be spotted  very frequently.Observe them then start ascending along the plateau to go towards the east or west, depending on the current.
  • Multicolored alcyonnaires, the sea fans whips, and do not forget to look regularly “in the blue“ : it is frequent to see passing the silhouette of a shark
  • Above your head you have a great chance to see barracudas.At the end of the dive, in the landing zone, take the time to stroll while looking at the top of the reef: a large number of fish are there as refugees among a wide variety of multicolored hard corals.

• 2 dives in the morning depending on guest flight schedules and the 24 hour requirement before flying.
  • Take advantage of an evening onshore to purchase souvenirs and enjoy Egypt's famous hospitality before your journey home the next day.
• Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

my-odyssey::bde-hurghada-2.highlightsDescription:
Brothers, Deadalus, Elphinstone ...

This tour takes you to the heart of the Red Sea to sites that made the reputation of Egypt with divers, who nicknamed it "the golden triangle" for the quality of its dives.

BROTHERS: Only accessible by cruising, the two Brothers islands are rooted at more than 500m of depth but only surmount the surface by a few meters. Often exposed to the currents, pelagic life abounds, making it one of the best sites of the Red Sea.

DEADALUS: Located 80km off Marsa Alam, this reef offers a multitude of opportunities to dive. Gray sharks, longimane and hammers can be seen here, under the keen eye of an army of clown fishes in an anemone field.

ELPHINSTONE: Two plateaus follow each other at 25m and 45m to form a majestic arch around which you can see schools of jacks, tuna and even hammerhead sharks.

On board one of our exceptional boats, lovers of sharks and wrecks will be delighted. You will discover vertiginous vertical drop offs which, often influenced by the currents coming from the wide, offer a pelagic fauna, gorgonians and alcyonnaires in abundance.

days.description:
• Safety Briefing, Crew Introduction, Necessary Dive Paperwork, Cabin allocation and ship orientation will take place before departing the Harbour.
  • During the journey to our first dive site for a check dive, please take this opportunity to familiarize yourselves with the vessel and make yourself comfortable. 
  • Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforseeable factors
• The morning after your arrival, we will go to our first reef for our “put in fins“ dive. Explore the reef at leisure before you take off toward Brother islands in the late afternoon.

• You will wake up next to Small Brother where you will have an early morning dive.
  • After exploring the stunning drops off, cross the channel to dive around the big brother. Take the time to visit 2 stunning shipwrecks on the north, the south plateau and the fall.
  • You could also go on the island to visit the 31m high military lighthouse built in 1883 by the English. 
  • Reach the top after climbing 140 steps and 2 metallic scales. Enjoy the beautiful sunset.
  • Numidia Wreck is a 130 meters long and 6 400 tons wreck which has been on the northern tip of Big Brother since it sank in July 1901. The ship was making her first journey from Glasgow to India with railway material. Today it sits on the skew, al- most vertically, between 10 and 80 meters deep. Do not forget to look “in the blue“ so you can see gray sharks or hammerheads.
  • Then drift with the current on one or both sides of the reef.
  • Descend to admire this wreck covered with a large number of multicolored alcyonaires and teeming with life, especially in the hold. In the early morning, do not forget to look in the water to see gray sharks or hammerheads. This is their spot!
  • Aida II is a wreck of 1426 tons, sunk in 1957 northwest of Big Brother. The zodiac will drop you along the reef, before the wreck, in the direction of the current. You will descend along the wall down to 30 meters. You will see the wreck of Aida.
  • Discover a gaping hole from which hang ropes covered with multicolored alcyonnaires. If you look inside, you will be able to admire clouds of “glassfish“. You can continue your exploration and, coming by the back of the wreck, you will admire an explosion of colors. The railings covered with multicolored alcyonnaires transform the wreck into a beautiful garden.
  • Small Brother's North Plateau. Here you will have th ebest chance of spot gray sharks and hammerheads. It is even possible to cross a Manta ray and / or a moonfish (Mola-mola).
  • Leave the plateau and the deep zone to reach the western slope, which is full of life with alcyonarians of all colors, magnificent sea fans and an extremely varied fauna : groupers, barracudas ...
  • On this island, you have the chance to see an incredible number of shark species : gray reefs, white tips, silky, hammerhead, thresher, and of course, often near the surface, the one you all expect : the oceanic white tip.

• Begin the cruise after dinner to reach Deadalus
    8 hours later.

• Take the chance to see hammerhead sharks early in the morning.
  • Possible visit to another english lighthouse from 1931.
  • To achieve the triangle, cruise to North/East and navigate towardsthe mythical reef of Elphinstone.
  • Daedalus's North Face is on the northern slope of Daedalus, which is the most exposed to the dominant current, here the most chances to make beautiful encounters with the pelagics.
  • Indeed it is very common here to encounter a school of hammerhead sharks composed of about twenty individuals. Trevallies and tunas are also very often seen..
  • Leave the deep zone to explore the falling area which requires great attention as
    it is full of overhangs. Observe many branches of black corals which colonized the reef. During your ascent,look at the surfaceand you will be able to see schools of barracudas.

• Elphinstone's North Plateau, jump in the water early in the morning. Descend along the reef to reach the plateau twenty meters deeper. You will see an impressive life. Follow the plateau down to 40 meters. There, around the fault and in the current hammerhead sharks and gray reefs can be spotted  very frequently.Observe them then start ascending along the plateau to go towards the east or west, depending on the current.
  • Multicolored alcyonnaires, the sea fans whips, and do not forget to look regularly “in the blue“ : it is frequent to see passing the silhouette of a shark
  • Above your head you have a great chance to see barracudas.At the end of the dive, in the landing zone, take the time to stroll while looking at the top of the reef: a large number of fish are there as refugees among a wide variety of multicolored hard corals.

• 2 dives in the morning depending on guest flight schedules and the 24 hour requirement before flying.
  • Take advantage of an evening onshore to purchase souvenirs and enjoy Egypt's famous hospitality before your journey home the next day.
• Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

my-odyssey::best-of-tiran-hurghada-hurgh.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night Northern Red Sea safari is designed to showcase the very best of Egypt’s classic dive routes, combining legendary wrecks, protected marine parks and vibrant offshore reefs. The itinerary focuses on the historic wrecks of the Abu Nuhas reef system, including some of the most photographed shipwrecks in the Red Sea, as well as the world-famous SS Thistlegorm, where trucks, motorcycles and military artefacts still rest on the seabed.

In addition to wreck diving, the route includes spectacular reef and drift dives in Ras Mohamed National Park, where strong nutrient-rich currents attract dense schools of fish and occasional pelagic encounters. Dramatic drop-offs, coral-covered walls and large gorgonians dominate these dives, offering outstanding wide-angle photography opportunities.

Further south, the itinerary explores offshore reefs in the Safaga area, such as Panorama Reef and Abu Kifan, known for their vertical walls, coral plateaus and chances to encounter sharks, barracudas and other large pelagic species. Calmer reefs closer to Hurghada provide a relaxed end to the safari, with colourful coral gardens, pinnacles and excellent visibility.

This itinerary offers a well-balanced mix of wreck, reef and drift diving, suitable for certified and experienced divers looking for variety, iconic dive sites and a classic Red Sea liveaboard experience in a relaxed yet adventure-focused setting.

• Safety Briefing, Crew Introduction, Necessary Dive Paperwork, Cabin allocation and ship orientation will take place before departing the Harbour.
  • During the journey to our first dive site for a check dive, please take this opportunity to familiarize yourselves with the vessel and make yourself comfortable. 
  • Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforseeable factors

• Abu Galawa, famous for its Tienstin wreck that goes from the surface to -17m at the stern. A wreck of about thirty meters colonized by so much corals that in some places, it is impossible to discern the end of the wreck and the begin of the reef (often in night dive).
  • Sha’ab Claudio, a site with a particular topography with large, magnificent cathedral-shaped caves that offer superb light. In the morning, it is not uncommon to meet small white tip sharks laying on the sand, and most of the time a huge napoleon wrasse hangs around at the safety stop.
  • Malahi,  is a site consisting of a maze of canyons where a magical atmosphere occurs with a magnificent light. It’s also a photographer’s paradise! Very often, schools of yellowfin mullet colonize the canyons. It is not uncommon to see a turtle during the dive.
  • Sataya's Reef, a huge reef more than 1.5 kilometers long. In summer, the water exceeds 33 ° in the lagoon. This site is home to a colony of more than 100 spinner dolphins (Stenella longirostris), often divided into several groups. days.description:
Arrival in Marsa Alam / Port Ghalib, meet & greet and transfer to the vessel. Check-in, cabin allocation, briefing, and overnight onboard in the marina.

Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforseeable factors
Early morning departure. Navigation south with 2–3 dives en route (Elphinstone or coastal reefs depending on conditions).

Full diving days in the deep South. Explore Rocky Island and Zabargad with steep walls, caves, and strong currents attracting pelagics. Continue to St John’s reef system for a variety of sites including coral gardens, tunnels, and pinnacles. Up to 3–4 dives per day, including night dives where permitted.
Start heading north with dives in the Fury Shoals / Sataya area, known for colorful reefs and easier conditions.
Final dives near Elphinstone or coastal reefs. Maximum 2 dives before heading back to port.

Disembarkation after breakfast and transfer to the airport.

days.description:
• Safety Briefing, Crew Introduction, Necessary Dive Paperwork, Cabin allocation and ship orientation will take place before departing the Harbour.
  • During the journey to our first dive site for a check dive, please take this opportunity to familiarize yourselves with the vessel and make yourself comfortable. 
  • Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforseeable factors

Sha'ab el Erg 

  • We will do our first dive on beautiful horseshoe shaped reef. Dolphins regularly swim on the outside of the reef or in the lagoon. We can observe them either by diving or snorkelling.
  • Thistlegorm, an English cargo ship dates from October 6, 1941. He was bombed by the German aviation while carrying ammunition and war material (trucks, cars, motorcycles, ...). You will see all these remains that are still present in the wreck. It is one of the most famous wrecks in the world.

Ras Mohamed 

  • Marine park located at the southern tip of Sinaï, ultimate separation between the Gulf of Aqaba and Suez. The water masses of the two straits meet and generate strong currents. Many pelagics evolve on these vertiginous drop offs (schools of barracudas, snappers ...) Drift on the extreme southern tip: “Shark Reef“ and “Yolanda Reef“, the most extraordinary sites of the park. We will immerse ourselves on “Shark Reef“ and its steep wall that goes down to -800m! We will follow this vertiginous drop and then go up on the plateau towards “Yolanda Reef“.
  • Chance to observe many coral formations covered with alcyonarians and gorgonians. Cross this beautiful territory inhabited by giant moray eels, napoleons, turtles, groupers, and a huge shoal of batfish, before finishing our dive on the remains of a Cypriot wreck sunk in 1980 which gave its name to the site (the Yolanda). There is only a small part of the debris remaining that slid much lower on the drop. The Yolanda was carrying sanitaries !! We can see a series of bathtubs and toilets where many fishes found shelter.

Small Brother's North Plateau 

  • We will go down to 35/40 m, above the northern plateau. This is where you will have the best chance of seeing gray sharks and hammerheads. It is even possible to cross a Manta ray and / or a moonfish (Mola-mola). We will then leave the plateau and the deep zone to reach the western slope, which is full of lifewith alcyonarians of all colors, magnificent sea fans and an extremely varied fauna :
    groupers, barracudas ... On this island, you have the chance to see an incredible number of shark species : gray reefs, white tips, silky, hammerhead, thresher,
    and of course, often near the surface, the one you all expect : the oceanic white tip.

Aida II Wreck 

  • A wreck of 1 426 tons, sunk in 1957 northwest of Big Brother. The zodiac will drop you along the reef, before the wreck, in the direction of the current. You will descend along the wall down to 30 meters. You will see the wreck of Aida. You will first discover a gaping hole from which hang ropes covered with multicolored alcyonnaires. If you look inside, you will be able to admire clouds of “glassfish“. You can continue your exploration and, coming by the back of the wreck, you will admire an explosion of colors. The railings covered with multicolored alcyonnaires transform the wreck into a beautiful garden.

Numidia Wreck 

  • A 130 meters long and 6 400 tons wreck which has been on the northern tip of Big Brother since it sank in July 1901. The ship was making her first journey from Glasgow to India with railway material. Today it sits on the skew, almost vertically, between 10 and 80 meters deep. Do not forget to look in the blue so you can see gray sharks or hammerheads. We will then drift with the current on one or both sides of the reef. 
  • Descend to admire this wreck covered with a large number of multicolored alcyonaires and teeming with life, especially in the hold. In the early morning, do not forget to look in the water to see gray sharks or hammerheads. This is their spot!

• 2 dives in the morning depending on guest flight schedules and the 24 hour requirement before flying.
  • Take advantage of an evening onshore to purchase souvenirs and enjoy Egypt's famous hospitality before your journey home the next day.
• Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

    Loop.
  • Dive some fantastic wreck, simply breathtaking! The ships are fully preseved, amazing stuff to see, great visibility 
  • Wreck diving, coral reefs, wall dives and pelagic.
  • The underwater scenery is ever changing and guaranteed to leave you breathless. 
  • Barracudas, giant trevallies, shoals of tuna and sometimes a manta ray along with loads of colourful corals and reef fish.
