my-odyssey::premium-expedition-hurghada-.highlightsDescription:
This exclusive 10-night liveaboard showcases the very best of the Egyptian Red Sea, combining legendary wrecks, world-famous reefs, dramatic walls, and exhilarating pelagic encounters in one unforgettable expedition.

Designed for experienced divers seeking maximum variety, the itinerary explores iconic sites including the northern wrecks, Ras Mohamed, the famous Blue Hole and reefs of the Sinai Peninsula, before continuing south to the offshore reefs of Brothers, Daedalus, and Elphinstone. Along the way, divers can expect colourful coral gardens, breathtaking drop-offs, thriving reef life, and the chance to encounter hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetips, grey reef sharks, manta rays, turtles, schooling jacks, and barracuda.

With up to 28 dives over nine diving days, this itinerary offers one of the most comprehensive explorations of the Red Sea, combining historic wrecks, spectacular reef systems, and world-class shark diving aboard the Odyssey's comfortable liveaboard experience.

days.description:
• Safety Briefing, Crew Introduction, Necessary Dive Paperwork, Cabin allocation and ship orientation will take place before departing the Harbour.
  • During the journey to our first dive site for a check dive, please take this opportunity to familiarize yourselves with the vessel and make yourself comfortable. 
  • Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforseeable factors

Deadalus 

  • Deadalus North Face, a dive on the northern
    slope of Daedalus, which is the most exposed to the dominant current, that we have the most chances to make beautiful encounters with the pelagics. Indeed it is very common here to evolve with a school of hammerhead sharks composed of about twenty individuals. Trevallies and tunas are also very often seen.

Zabargad

 

  • Zabargad is an island of about 5km2. It is next to Rocky. On the south side where the boat will be moored is a turquoise lagoon with a coral reef reminiscent of a Polynesian lagoon. Diving on the plateau sud discover abundant wildlife and coral towers covered with multicolored alcyonnaires. It is not uncommon to encounter turtles during the dive.

Rocky

  • 5km south of Zabargad is Rocky Island, close to the Sudanese border. This is without a doubt the wildest site in Egypt. As the dive goes on, the shallow plateau that is home to all kinds of species changes to a drop off covered with giant sea fans, corals and sponges. The south of the island is the pelagic point with white tip sharks, grays, hammerheads and even manta rays.

Elphinstone

  • Elphinstone's North Plateau, jump in the water early in the morning. Descend along the reef to reach the plateau twenty meters deeper. You will see an impressive life. Follow the plateau down to 40 meters. There, around the fault and in the current hammerhead sharks and gray reefs can be spotted  very frequently. Observe them then start ascending along the plateau to go towards the east or west, depending on the current.
  • Multicolored alcyonnaires, the sea fans whips, and do not forget to look regularly “in the blue“ : it is frequent to see passing the silhouette of a shark. Above your head you have a great chance to see barracudas.At the end of the dive, in the landing zone, take the time to stroll while looking at the top of the reef: a large number of fish are there as refugees among a wide variety of multicolored hard corals.

• 2 dives in the morning depending on guest flight schedules and the 24 hour requirement before flying.
  • Take advantage of an evening onshore to purchase souvenirs and enjoy Egypt's famous hospitality before your journey home the next day.
• Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

days.description:
• Safety Briefing, Crew Introduction, Necessary Dive Paperwork, Cabin allocation and ship orientation will take place before departing the Harbour.
  • During the journey to our first dive site for a check dive, please take this opportunity to familiarize yourselves with the vessel and make yourself comfortable. 
  • Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforseeable factors

Sha'ab el Erg 

  • We will do our first dive on beautiful horseshoe shaped reef. Dolphins regularly swim on the outside of the reef or in the lagoon. We can observe them either by diving or snorkelling.

Sha'ab Abu Nuhas 

  • More known as Cemetery of ships, this  reef is very close to the shipping route that connects Europe to the East. Indeed, some ships coming out of the Gubal Strait after crossing the Suez Canal came up against this reef fringing the surface. On its north face, five wrecks are aligned:
  • Carnatic a 90m long and 1800 barrels steamer came to finish his days on this reef one night of 1869. It rests between 18 and 24m. The cargo was recovered: 32,000 pounds sterling in gold bars. 8 000 are still missing... The hull is covered with hard corals, colorful alcyonarians and sponges. Inside, countless “glass fish“ mingle with beautiful lion fish.
  • Ghiannis  D a 100m. long and 2900 barrels cargo ship sunk in 1983. He was traveling between Croatia and Yemen and was transporting wood.
  • Chrisoula K a Greek cargo ship of 100m. long and 3700 barrels sunk on October 30, 1981. He carried a transport of tiles from Italy towards Jiddah. Its stern rests on a bottom of -26 m. and is lying on his starboard side.
  • Kimon M a cargo ship of 3715 tons sunk on December 1978. He carried a cargo of 4,500 tonnes of lenses! Hence his nickname The wreck with lentils. The holds house a multitude of hatchet fish.
  • Rosalie Moeller a 108m. long cargo sunk in 1941, the same week as the Thistlegorm. A magnificent wreck, laid straight on a 50m bottom. The descent along the rear mast starts at -17m. The view on the wreck while descending and the trevallies hunt in the clouds of smelts leaves an unforgettable memory.
  • Thistlegorm, this English cargo ship dates from October 6, 1941. He was bombed by the German aviation while carrying ammunition and war material (trucks, cars, motorcycles, ...). You will see all these remains that are still present in the wreck. It is one of the most famous wrecks in the world.

Tiran Strait 

  • Four beautiful coral reefs fringing the surface are located in the middle of this strait. Its narrowness usually brings a strong current which allows the observation of many pelagic fish, jacks, rays eagles, barracudas, gray sharks, hammers ... You will also discover two remains of shipwrecks stranded on these reefs. They are “posed“ straight like two guardians of the place. These are the cargos Louilla (Gordon) and Lara (Jackson). You will be able to observe many cargo debris from the boats, all covered with coral.
  • Thomas reef, the smallest of the four but the richest! It of-ten happens to see gray sharks and hammerheads on the north face where you can admire many gorgonians and alcyonarians. The east face is also exceptional. On the north/east corner, at a thirty meters depth, starts a beautiful narrow canyon with several arches. The dive ends on a large plateau that  overlooks this vertical drop. It is very commonto come across turtles. You will end your dive on the beautiful coral garden around ten meters, among gaterini, emperors, butterfly fish, trevallies ...
  • Gordon Reef, along the eastern slope, looking in the “blue“, you will see gray sharks that do not seem to be disturbed by the current. Then, if you head south, going up on the plateau, you should see a pretty little sandbank occupied by a colony of garden eels, standing upright... Further away, a very large school of banner fish is waiting for you.
  • Jackson Reef and Woodhouse. After walking along the reef towards the west plateau, you will see large gorgonians. You will surely meet a turtle on the plateau (20m.)m that separates Jackson from Woodhouse. The current can be strong enough to bring pelagic fish to the drop off or over the plateau. 
  • Ras Mohamed, a marine park located at the southern tip of Sinaï, ultimate separation between the Gulf of Aqaba and Suez. The water masses of the
    two straits meet and generate strong currents. Many pelagics evolve on these vertiginous drop offs (schools of barracudas, snappers ...) We will drift on the extreme southern tip: Shark Reef and Yolanda Reef, the most extraordinary sites of the park. We will immerse ourselves on Shark Reef and its steep wall that goes down to -800m! We will follow this vertiginous drop and then go up on the plateau towards Yolanda Reef. 
  • Chance to observe many coral formations covered with alcyonarians and gorgonians. We will cross this beautiful territory inhabited by giant moray eels, napoleons, turtles, groupers, and a huge shoal of batfish, before finishing our dive on the remains of a Cypriot wreck sunk in 1980 which gave its name to the site (the Yolanda). There is only a small part of the debris remaining that slid much lower on the drop. The Yolanda was carrying sanitaries !! We can see a series of bathtubs and toilets where many fishes found shelter.
• 2 dives in the morning depending on guest flight schedules and the 24 hour requirement before flying.
• Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

my-odyssey::souakin-et-legends-2.highlightsDescription:
Embark on our comfortable yachts and discover the best sites in the region of Hurghada, Sharm El Sheikh, the Gubal Strait and the Strait of Tiran in the Gulf of Aqba.

As an extension of the North Cruise, this route takes you to the Strait of Tiran in the Gulf of Aqaba, passing by the famous Ras Mohamed Reserve and the mystical wrecks of Thistlegorm and Rosalie Moeller.

Dolphins will accompany you for part of the trip, while you dive on vertiginous and preserved drop-offs where pelagic life thrives: trevallies, eagle rays, and sharks. 

The pulsating splendor of the coral reefs, the abundant fish life, and the numerous wrecks shrouded in the mysteries of war, tragedy, and heroism make the Red Sea a unique underwater adventure. Dive some fantastic wrecks, including the Thistlegorm, currently ranked as the second best wreck dive in the world. Enjoy both day and night dives at the same site, experiencing different creatures that emerge once the sun goes down.

Highlights:

• The Ras Mohamed reserve

• Mythical wrecks: Thistlegorm, Rosalie Moeller ...

• Meeting with dolphins

my-odyssey::the-golden-loop-brothers-nor.highlightsDescription:
This exclusive 10-night liveaboard showcases the very best of the Egyptian Red Sea, combining legendary wrecks, world-famous reefs, dramatic walls, and exhilarating pelagic encounters in one unforgettable expedition.

Designed for experienced divers seeking maximum variety, the itinerary explores iconic sites including the northern wrecks, Ras Mohamed, the famous Blue Hole and reefs of the Sinai Peninsula, before continuing south to the offshore reefs of Brothers, Daedalus, and Elphinstone. Along the way, divers can expect colourful coral gardens, breathtaking drop-offs, thriving reef life, and the chance to encounter hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetips, grey reef sharks, manta rays, turtles, schooling jacks, and barracuda.

With up to 28 dives over nine diving days, this itinerary offers one of the most comprehensive explorations of the Red Sea, combining historic wrecks, spectacular reef systems, and world-class shark diving aboard the Odyssey's comfortable liveaboard experience.

days.description:
• Safety Briefing, Crew Introduction, Necessary Dive Paperwork, Cabin allocation and ship orientation will take place before departing the Harbour.
  • During the journey to our first dive site for a check dive, please take this opportunity to familiarize yourselves with the vessel and make yourself comfortable. 
  • Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforseeable factors

Sha'ab el Erg 

  • We will do our first dive on beautiful horseshoe shaped reef. Dolphins regularly swim on the outside of the reef or in the lagoon. We can observe them either by diving or snorkelling.
  • Thistlegorm, an English cargo ship dates from October 6, 1941. He was bombed by the German aviation while carrying ammunition and war material (trucks, cars, motorcycles, ...). You will see all these remains that are still present in the wreck. It is one of the most famous wrecks in the world.

Ras Mohamed 

  • Marine park located at the southern tip of Sinaï, ultimate separation between the Gulf of Aqaba and Suez. The water masses of the two straits meet and generate strong currents. Many pelagics evolve on these vertiginous drop offs (schools of barracudas, snappers ...) Drift on the extreme southern tip: “Shark Reef“ and “Yolanda Reef“, the most extraordinary sites of the park. We will immerse ourselves on “Shark Reef“ and its steep wall that goes down to -800m! We will follow this vertiginous drop and then go up on the plateau towards “Yolanda Reef“.
  • Chance to observe many coral formations covered with alcyonarians and gorgonians. Cross this beautiful territory inhabited by giant moray eels, napoleons, turtles, groupers, and a huge shoal of batfish, before finishing our dive on the remains of a Cypriot wreck sunk in 1980 which gave its name to the site (the Yolanda). There is only a small part of the debris remaining that slid much lower on the drop. The Yolanda was carrying sanitaries !! We can see a series of bathtubs and toilets where many fishes found shelter.

Small Brother's North Plateau 

  • We will go down to 35/40 m, above the northern plateau. This is where you will have the best chance of seeing gray sharks and hammerheads. It is even possible to cross a Manta ray and / or a moonfish (Mola-mola). We will then leave the plateau and the deep zone to reach the western slope, which is full of lifewith alcyonarians of all colors, magnificent sea fans and an extremely varied fauna :
    groupers, barracudas ... On this island, you have the chance to see an incredible number of shark species : gray reefs, white tips, silky, hammerhead, thresher,
    and of course, often near the surface, the one you all expect : the oceanic white tip.

Aida II Wreck 

  • A wreck of 1 426 tons, sunk in 1957 northwest of Big Brother. The zodiac will drop you along the reef, before the wreck, in the direction of the current. You will descend along the wall down to 30 meters. You will see the wreck of Aida. You will first discover a gaping hole from which hang ropes covered with multicolored alcyonnaires. If you look inside, you will be able to admire clouds of “glassfish“. You can continue your exploration and, coming by the back of the wreck, you will admire an explosion of colors. The railings covered with multicolored alcyonnaires transform the wreck into a beautiful garden.

Numidia Wreck 

  • A 130 meters long and 6 400 tons wreck which has been on the northern tip of Big Brother since it sank in July 1901. The ship was making her first journey from Glasgow to India with railway material. Today it sits on the skew, almost vertically, between 10 and 80 meters deep. Do not forget to look in the blue so you can see gray sharks or hammerheads. We will then drift with the current on one or both sides of the reef. 
  • Descend to admire this wreck covered with a large number of multicolored alcyonaires and teeming with life, especially in the hold. In the early morning, do not forget to look in the water to see gray sharks or hammerheads. This is their spot!

• 2 dives in the morning depending on guest flight schedules and the 24 hour requirement before flying.
  • Take advantage of an evening onshore to purchase souvenirs and enjoy Egypt's famous hospitality before your journey home the next day.
• Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

  • Dive some fantastic wreck, simply breathtaking! The ships are fully preseved, amazing stuff to see, great visibility 
  • Wreck diving, coral reefs, wall dives and pelagic.
  • The underwater scenery is ever changing and guaranteed to leave you breathless. 
  • Barracudas, giant trevallies, shoals of tuna and sometimes a manta ray along with loads of colourful corals and reef fish.
  • Enjoy both day and night dives at the same site, as different creatures come out once the sun goes down.

days.description:
Hamata Marina

Board New Sambo at Hamata Marina, settle into your cabin and prepare your diving equipment. Meet the crew and get familiar with the boat before spending the first night on board. The diving program begins the following day.

Fury Shoals

Begin the diving program around Hammam & Saeed and Abu Galawa. Three daytime dives are planned, followed by a night dive subject to conditions. Total: 4 dives, including 1 night dive.

St. John’s North

Explore the northern St. John’s area, including sites such as Habili, Gotta Kebir and St. John’s Caves. Total: 3 dives.

St. John’s South

Continue through southern St. John’s, with dives at sites such as Dangerous Reef, Paradise Reef and Habili Ali. Three daytime dives and a night dive are planned, subject to conditions. Total: 4 dives, including 1 night dive.

Rocky Island

Spend the day exploring Rocky Island, renowned for its spectacular walls and rich marine life. Total: 3 dives.

Zabargad Island

Explore the reefs around Zabargad Island, including the famous Russian Wreck. Total: 3 dives.

Fury Shoals

Return to Fury Shoals for the final diving day, with dives around Shaab Maksour, Sataya Reef and Abu Galawa. After the diving program, New Sambo returns to Hamata Marina for the final night on board. Total: 3 dives.

Hamata Marina

After breakfast, check out and disembark at Hamata Marina.

new-sambo-safari-boat-2::fury-shoals-ham.highlightsDescription:
Set off on an 8-day/7-night liveaboard adventure exploring some of the most remote and spectacular diving areas of the southern Red Sea. This itinerary takes certified divers through Fury Shoals, St. John’s, Rocky Island and Zabargad Island, combining beautiful coral reefs, dramatic walls, caves and wreck sites.

The diving begins in Fury Shoals, with dives around Hammam & Saeed and Abu Galawa, before continuing south to St. John’s. Two days are dedicated to exploring the northern and southern sections of this renowned area, including sites such as Habili, Gotta Kebir, St. John’s Caves, Dangerous Reef, Paradise Reef and Habili Ali.

The journey continues to remote Rocky Island, known for its spectacular walls and rich marine life, followed by Zabargad Island, where divers can explore its reefs and the famous Russian Wreck. The final diving day brings you back through Fury Shoals, with dives around Shaab Maksour, Sataya Reef and Abu Galawa before returning to Hamata Marina for the final night on board.

A total of 18–20 dives are included, with night dives planned on selected days, subject to weather conditions, local regulations and operational conditions. The exact number and order of dives may vary according to sea conditions and the operational program.

Hamata - Sataya

Transfer from your hotel to Hamata Marina and board New Sambo. After a welcome and safety briefing, set sail for Sataya / Dolphin Reef. Spend the day snorkeling, swimming and observing dolphins, while certified divers can join the scheduled dives with a certified dive guide. Dinner and overnight on board at Sataya.

Sataya - Abu Galawa

Start the day with further snorkeling and diving activities around Sataya before sailing towards Abu Galawa. Enjoy additional snorkeling or diving in the area, depending on sea conditions and the operational program. Dinner and overnight on board.

Shaab Claudia or Malahi - Hamata

After breakfast, cruise to Shaab Claudia or Malahi, depending on weather, sea conditions and the operational program. Enjoy the final snorkeling and diving activities before lunch on board and the return journey to Hamata Marina. Arrival is expected at approximately 16:00, followed by the included transfer back to your hotel.

new-sambo-safari-boat-2::overnight-satay.highlightsDescription:
Set off on a 3-day/2-night Red Sea mini safari combining scuba diving, snorkeling and dolphin encounters around Sataya / Dolphin Reef and the southern reefs of Fury Shoals. Suitable for both certified divers and snorkelers, this short liveaboard adventure is also a great option for groups and families with different experience levels.

The trip begins with a transfer from your hotel to Hamata Marina, where you board New Sambo before setting sail for Sataya. This vast lagoon is renowned for its population of spinner dolphins and offers opportunities for snorkeling, swimming and dolphin observation, while certified divers can explore the surrounding reefs with a certified dive guide.

The journey continues through the Fury Shoals area, with further diving and snorkeling around Abu Galawa before heading to Shaab Claudia or Malahi on the final day. These southern Red Sea reefs offer beautiful coral formations and plenty of opportunities to experience the region's underwater scenery.

After the final activities, lunch is served on board before returning to Hamata Marina at approximately 16:00. A total of 7 dives are included for certified divers, while night and additional dives may be arranged at an extra cost, subject to availability and operational conditions. Dolphin sightings cannot be guaranteed, and the itinerary may vary according to weather, sea conditions and local regulations.

new-sambo-safari-boat-2::sataya-dolphin-.highlightsDescription:
Set off on an 8-day/7-night liveaboard adventure dedicated to some of the Red Sea’s most iconic offshore dive sites, including the Brothers Islands, Daedalus Reef and Elphinstone Reef. Designed for experienced certified divers, this itinerary combines spectacular walls, coral reefs and some of the region’s best opportunities for encounters with pelagic marine life.

The diving program begins around Ras Trombi before heading offshore to the Brothers Islands, renowned for their dramatic walls and rich marine life. The journey then continues to Daedalus Reef, with two full days dedicated to exploring this remote offshore reef and its varied dive sites.

From Daedalus, New Sambo continues to Elphinstone Reef, famous for its impressive walls and open-water setting. The final diving day takes place around Marsa Shouna / Abu Dabbab before the yacht returns to Port Ghalib Marina.

A total of 18–19 dives are planned, including one night dive. This safari is exclusively for certified divers and requires a minimum Advanced Open Water Diver (AOWD) certification or equivalent and at least 50 logged dives. The itinerary and number of dives may vary according to weather, sea conditions and the operational program.

new-sambo-safari-boat-2::st-johns-reef-m.highlightsDescription:
Set off on a 2-day/1-night Red Sea mini safari to the famous Sataya Dolphin Reef, also known as Sha’ab Sataya, in the southern Red Sea. This short liveaboard getaway combines scuba diving, snorkeling and relaxation, with the chance to encounter wild spinner dolphins in their natural environment.

The trip begins with a transfer from your hotel to Hamata Marina for morning boarding. After settling in, New Sambo sets sail at approximately 09:00 towards Sataya / Dolphin Reef. Spend the day exploring the lagoon, with opportunities for snorkeling, swimming and dolphin observation, while certified divers can join scheduled dives with a certified dive guide. Sataya is particularly renowned for its large lagoon and resident population of spinner dolphins.

After dinner and a night on board, the following day offers further snorkeling and diving around Sataya before continuing to the Abu Galawa area for a final snorkeling or diving session. After lunch on board, the yacht returns to Hamata Marina, arriving no later than approximately 16:00.

A total of 4 dives are included for certified divers. Complimentary round-trip hotel transfers are provided for hotels located between El Quseir and Hamata, including Port Ghalib and Marsa Alam. Dolphin encounters cannot be guaranteed, and the itinerary may be adjusted according to weather, sea conditions and local regulations.

days.description:
Hamata Marina

Board New Sambo at Hamata Marina, settle into your cabin and prepare your diving equipment. Meet the crew and get familiar with the boat before spending the first night at Hamata Marina.

Fury Shoals North

Begin the diving adventure in northern Fury Shoals, with dives at Sha’ab Claudia, Malahi and Abu Galawa Soraya. Three daytime dives are planned, with a possible night dive depending on conditions.

Fury Shoals Central

Continue through central Fury Shoals, exploring Sha’ab Maksour, Abu Galawa Kebir and its famous wreck, and Malahi. Three daytime dives are planned, with a possible night dive.

Fury Shoals South

Head south for dives around Sha’ab Hamam and Sha’ab Pinky / Manel. Two to three daytime dives are planned, with a possible night dive depending on conditions and the operational program.

Sataya

Explore Sataya North, Sataya Lagoon and Sataya South. Known for its coral reefs and spinner dolphins, Sataya is one of the highlights of the safari. Three daytime dives are planned, with a possible night dive.

Lahami Area

Continue south to the remote Lahami area and explore Lahami North, Gota Lahami and Lahami South. Three daytime dives are planned, with a possible night dive.

Wadi El Gemal Area

Spend the final diving day exploring Gota Sharm and Wadi El Gemal Reef. Two to three daytime dives are planned before New Sambo returns to Hamata Marina in the evening for the final night on board. A night dive may also be offered depending on conditions.

Hamata Marina

After breakfast, check out of your cabin and disembark at Hamata Marina.

Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforseeable factors.

new-sambo-safari-boat-2::st-johns-reef-m.highlightsDescription:
Set off on an 8-day/7-night liveaboard adventure exploring some of the most beautiful and diverse diving areas of the southern Red Sea, including Fury Shoals, Sataya, Lahami and Wadi El Gemal. This itinerary combines vibrant coral reefs, spectacular reef formations and a variety of marine life, with possible encounters with dolphins, turtles and reef sharks along the way.

The diving begins in the northern and central sections of Fury Shoals, exploring sites such as Sha’ab Claudia, Malahi, Abu Galawa Soraya and Sha’ab Maksour. At Abu Galawa Kebir, divers can also discover its famous wreck surrounded by colorful coral formations. The journey then continues south through Sha’ab Hamam and Sha’ab Pinky / Manel before reaching Sataya.

Sataya is one of the highlights of the itinerary, renowned for its beautiful reefs and the possibility of encountering spinner dolphins. From here, the safari continues to the remote Lahami area, with dives at Lahami North, Gota Lahami and Lahami South, before exploring Gota Sharm and Wadi El Gemal Reef on the final diving day.

A total of 16–18 daytime dives are included, with night dives offered on selected days depending on weather, local regulations and operational conditions. The itinerary and number of dives may vary according to sea and weather conditions.

Payment terms:

Groups (half group or more):

 

  1.   *   A non-refundable, non-transferable deposit of $1,500 accompanied by a signed contract is required within 14 days of the reservation.
  2.   *   Nine (9) months prior to departure date, an additional non-refundable, non-transferable deposit of $3,500 deposit is due.
  3.   *   Six (6) months prior to departure, 40% of the funds are due.
  4.   *   Final payment is due ninety (90) days prior to departure date.

 

Groups (half group or more): If a group reservation is cancelled:

 

  1.   *   More than nine (9) months prior to departure, the $1,500 deposit may be applied to a new individual or group reservation. If you choose not to apply it to a new reservation, the $1500 will be forfeited.
  2.   *   Nine (9) months to 181 days prior to departure, the $5,000 deposit is forfeited.
  3.   *   180 - 91 days prior to departure, 40% of the group rate is forfeited.
  4.   *   90 days or less prior to departure, 100% of the group rate is forfeited and no refund is available.

 

Groups (half group or more): If the number of travelers is reduced from original reservation:

 

  1.   *   More than nine (9) months prior to departure, the reservation may be reduced down to one paying person which will result in reduction/loss of free space(s).
  2.   *   Nine (9) months to 181 days or more prior to departure, 20% of the charter rate per passenger cancelled is forfeited, and there is a reduction/loss of free space(s).
  3.   *   180 - 91 days prior to departure, 40% of the rate per passenger cancelled is forfeited and there is a reduction/loss of free space(s).
  4.   *   90 days or less prior to departure, 100% of the rate per person is forfeited and there is a reduction/loss of free space(s).

red-sea-aggressor-ii::northern-red-sea-r.highlightsDescription:
Northern Red Sea – Best of Wreck Diving is a unique, wreck-dedicated itinerary designed for divers who want to explore the highest concentration of historic shipwrecks in the region in a single week. The route focuses almost entirely on iconic wreck sites such as the SS Thistlegorm, Dunraven and the legendary Abu Nuhas “ships’ graveyard”, together with additional highlights including El Minya, Salem Express, El Khafain and Ulysses, offering an exceptional variety of large, well-preserved structures and atmospheric dive environments.

Up to 19 wreck dives are typically offered during the week, complemented by a small number of reef dives to add colour and marine diversity to the programme. This itinerary combines maritime history, impressive wreck architecture and rich marine life, making it an ideal choice for experienced recreational divers and true wreck-diving enthusiasts looking for an immersive and highly specialised Red Sea safari.
red-sea-aggressor-ii::northern-red-sea-r.logistics:
Before your trip

  • The Red Sea Aggressor II operates from downtown Hurghada at the upscale Hurghada Marina (known locally as New Marina Hurghada) which is a community that includes shops, restaurants, cafes, and bars.
  • Transfers are included in the price of the trip if arriving/departing from the Hurghada Airport on the charter start/end dates to and from New Marina Hurghada Harbor where the yacht docks. (reservations are required at least 7 days in advance for pick up from the Hurghada Airport to the yacht)
  • For guests already in Hurghada, you may make your own way to the for a 3 pm boarding Red Sea Aggressor II on Saturday.

Last day of the trip

  • After a full week of diving, the Red Sea Aggressor II returns back to Hurghada New Marina Friday afternoon between 2 - 4 pm.
  • Friday evening after the sunset cocktail party, guests may go ashore and enjoy one of the many fine restaurants, cafes or pubs in the marina. 
  • Check-out is Saturday morning at 8 am.

More recommendations

  • We recommend guests arrive in Egypt on Friday, one day prior to the start day of the charter. Once guests are onboard and the yacht is given clearance to leave the port by the local authorities, no one can board the yacht after this time or deliver any lost luggage. Arriving early will not only help you get acclimated to the local climate but ensure a timely arrival and that all bags have arrived. No bags or guests can be delivered to the yacht after clearance is given.
  • One-way transfers to or from Hurghada Int’l Airport to/from the hotels inside Hurghada is approx.. $15 for limo car (1-2 guests) and for the micro bus - $20 (3-16pax) (subject to change)
  • If you are already in Hurghada and making your own way to the Red Sea Aggressor II. Please be sure to include your arrival time and/or hotel reservations when completing your online paperwork through the GIS. (Taxis can be arranged to other locations)

red-sea-aggressor-ii::northern-red-sea-r.otherLogisticsInfo:
• Guests arrange their own transfers between Hurghada International Airport (HRG) and El Foley Marina; taxis and Uber are readily available (maximum approx. USD 20 from the airport). The marina is located on Arabia Road next to the Beirut Hotel and is locally known as Public Beach Number 4.
  • Boarding takes place on Saturday between 3:00 pm and 6:00 pm. Guests are strongly advised to arrive in Hurghada at least one day before boarding.
  • The yacht departs on Sunday morning after port authority clearance; no boarding is possible once clearance has been granted.
  • Passports must be valid for at least six months beyond the end of the trip. Guests are required to upload their passport and complete the online Guest Information System (GIS) at least 7 days prior to departure. Completion of all required information is mandatory before boarding.
  • An entry visa for Egypt is required (USD 25 single-entry on arrival; multi-entry USD 60 optional).
  • A completed and signed RSTC Diving Medical History Form is mandatory for all divers and must be printed and brought on board. If any answer is marked “yes”, a doctor’s approval is required before the trip. No medical facilities are available locally to issue certificates.
  • Diving is recreational only, with typically 20–22 dives during the week and a maximum of 3–4 dives per day, including selected night dives, conducted from tenders or directly from the main yacht. An SMB and reel are mandatory for all divers and must be brought or rented on board.
  • Port, marine park fees, and fuel surcharge totaling USD 200 per person (USD 50 port fee + USD 100 marine park fee + USD 50 fuel surcharge) are payable on board. A 14% VAT applies to all on-board charges. Credit card payments incur a 3% service fee.
  • On Friday afternoon the yacht returns to El Foley Marina between approximately 2:00 pm and 4:00 pm. A farewell cocktail party is held on board, followed by dinner served on board.
  • Check-out is on Saturday morning at 8:00 am.

red-sea-aggressor-ii::northern-red-sea-t.highlightsDescription: Northern Red Sea & Dahab is a classic Red Sea itinerary combining world-famous wrecks, vibrant reefs and the unique landscapes of Dahab in one diverse week of diving. The route includes highlights such as the legendary SS Thistlegorm, Ras Mohamed National Park, the reefs of Tiran and signature Dahab sites including the Blue Hole, the Bells and the Canyon. Divers can expect up to 18–21 recreational dives, with a mix of easy drifts, colourful coral walls and historic wreck exploration, as well as frequent encounters with reef sharks, turtles, schooling fish and rich macro life. A special cultural touch is often added with an optional Bedouin dinner at Abu Galom, making this itinerary a balanced blend of iconic Red Sea diving and local experience.
red-sea-aggressor-ii::northern-red-sea-t.logistics:
Before your trip

  • The Red Sea Aggressor II operates from downtown Hurghada at the upscale Hurghada Marina (known locally as New Marina Hurghada) which is a community that includes shops, restaurants, cafes, and bars.
  • Transfers are included in the price of the trip if arriving/departing from the Hurghada Airport on the charter start/end dates to and from New Marina Hurghada Harbor where the yacht docks. (reservations are required at least 7 days in advance for pick up from the Hurghada Airport to the yacht)
  • For guests already in Hurghada, you may make your own way to the for a 3 pm boarding Red Sea Aggressor II on Saturday.

Last day of the trip

  • After a full week of diving, the Red Sea Aggressor II returns back to Hurghada New Marina Friday afternoon between 2 - 4 pm.
  • Friday evening after the sunset cocktail party, guests may go ashore and enjoy one of the many fine restaurants, cafes or pubs in the marina. 
  • Check-out is Saturday morning at 8 am.

More recommendations

  • We recommend guests arrive in Egypt on Friday, one day prior to the start day of the charter. Once guests are onboard and the yacht is given clearance to leave the port by the local authorities, no one can board the yacht after this time or deliver any lost luggage. Arriving early will not only help you get acclimated to the local climate but ensure a timely arrival and that all bags have arrived. No bags or guests can be delivered to the yacht after clearance is given.
  • One-way transfers to or from Hurghada Int’l Airport to/from the hotels inside Hurghada is approx.. $15 for limo car (1-2 guests) and for the micro bus - $20 (3-16pax) (subject to change)
  • If you are already in Hurghada and making your own way to the Red Sea Aggressor II. Please be sure to include your arrival time and/or hotel reservations when completing your online paperwork through the GIS. (Taxis can be arranged to other locations)

red-sea-aggressor-iv::brothersdaedalusel.highlightsDescription:
This itinerary explores some of the most iconic offshore reefs in Egypt’s southern Red Sea, combining dramatic walls, thriving coral formations, and some of the region’s best opportunities for pelagic encounters. It is designed for experienced divers seeking challenging conditions, spectacular underwater scenery, and world-class shark diving.

The legendary Brother Islands feature steep drop-offs, vibrant soft corals, historic wrecks, and frequent sightings of grey reef sharks, thresher sharks, oceanic whitetips (seasonal), and occasional hammerheads. Daedalus Reef is renowned for its pristine coral gardens, colorful reef life, and schools of hammerhead sharks, while Elphinstone offers breathtaking walls, rich coral growth, and the chance to encounter oceanic whitetips, manta rays, and other large pelagic species.

Depending on weather and sea conditions, the itinerary may also include additional southern reefs such as Sha'ab Maksour and local Marsa Alam sites, where healthy coral gardens, turtles, rays, reef fish, and occasional dolphins or dugongs provide a perfect complement to the offshore dives.

With strong currents, deep walls, and exceptional marine biodiversity, this itinerary offers an unforgettable Red Sea adventure for advanced divers looking to experience some of Egypt's most celebrated dive sites.

Depending on weather and sea conditions, the itinerary may also include additional southern reefs such as Sha'ab Maksour and local Marsa Alam sites, where healthy coral gardens, turtles, rays, reef fish, and occasional dolphins or dugongs provide a perfect complement to the offshore dives.

With strong currents, deep walls, and exceptional marine biodiversity, this itinerary offers an unforgettable Red Sea adventure for advanced divers looking to experience some of Egypt's most celebrated dive sites.

Resting place of many intriguing wrecks including several WWII ships that house countless artefacts.

All dives from two tenders that carry 10 divers each for quick and comfortable access.

No night dives are allowed in the Marine Parks.

we may sail to the southernmost islands of Rocky and Zabargad.

we'll moor instead in the vast reef system of St John's to begin the adventure in the South.

This is a chance to explore the southernmost area of Egypt's Red Sea.

The route includes bountiful reefs and playful cave-like formations.

Sharks, mantas, and Rosso dolphins have been spotted on this route.

red-sea-aggressor-iv::st-john-daedalus-p.highlightsDescription:
This itinerary explores the remote reefs of Egypt's southern Red Sea, combining the legendary offshore reef of Daedalus with the pristine coral systems of St. John's and Sataya. Offering dramatic underwater landscapes, vibrant coral gardens, and excellent opportunities for pelagic encounters, it is an ideal route for experienced divers seeking both adventure and variety.

Daedalus Reef is renowned for its spectacular walls, healthy hard and soft corals, and regular sightings of schooling hammerhead sharks, thresher sharks, reef sharks, manta rays, and occasional whale sharks. Further south, the reefs of St. John's feature an impressive network of caverns, tunnels, and swim-throughs, alongside colorful coral gardens teeming with reef fish, turtles, rays, and fascinating macro life.

Depending on weather and sea conditions, the itinerary may also include Sataya and nearby reefs such as Sha'ab Maksour, Sha'ab Claude, and Malahi. These sites offer beautiful coral formations, dramatic pinnacles, easy swim-throughs, healthy reef ecosystems, and the chance to encounter reef sharks, schooling snappers, dolphins, and a wide variety of marine life.

Combining iconic offshore diving with some of the Egyptian Red Sea's most untouched southern reefs, this itinerary delivers an unforgettable mix of big fish encounters, spectacular coral scenery, and diverse underwater landscapes.

red-sea-aggressor-iv::st-johns-daedalus-.highlightsDescription:
This itinerary explores the remote reefs of Egypt's southern Red Sea, combining the legendary offshore reef of Daedalus with the pristine coral systems of St. John's and Sataya. Offering dramatic underwater landscapes, vibrant coral gardens, and excellent opportunities for pelagic encounters, it is an ideal route for experienced divers seeking both adventure and variety.

Daedalus Reef is renowned for its spectacular walls, healthy hard and soft corals, and regular sightings of schooling hammerhead sharks, thresher sharks, reef sharks, manta rays, and occasional whale sharks. Further south, the reefs of St. John's feature an impressive network of caverns, tunnels, and swim-throughs, alongside colorful coral gardens teeming with reef fish, turtles, rays, and fascinating macro life.

Depending on weather and sea conditions, the itinerary may also include Sataya and nearby reefs such as Sha'ab Maksour, Sha'ab Claude, and Malahi. These sites offer beautiful coral formations, dramatic pinnacles, easy swim-throughs, healthy reef ecosystems, and the chance to encounter reef sharks, schooling snappers, dolphins, and a wide variety of marine life.

Combining iconic offshore diving with some of the Egyptian Red Sea's most untouched southern reefs, this itinerary delivers an unforgettable mix of big fish encounters, spectacular coral scenery, and diverse underwater landscapes.

red-sea-aggressor-v::deep-south-elba-ree.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night Deep South itinerary from Hamata to Abu Fendira and Elba Reef immerses divers in one of the Red Sea’s most secluded and untouched regions. Known for its rich biodiversity and expansive coral formations, this route offers a pristine dive experience, far from other liveaboards and teeming with marine life.

Abu Fendira’s 6-kilometer stretch of reefs runs in an east-west direction, with depths ranging from 15 to 25 meters. Divers can expect vivid coral blocks, with sharks gliding nearby, schools of fish, and sightings of magnificent Napoleon wrasse and the rare humphead parrotfish. The reef’s remote beauty makes for an incredible underwater scene, filled with movement and color.

Moving to Elba Reef, divers encounter stunning topography. The North Plateau begins at 20 meters and drops to 45 meters, lined with huge coral fans along its edges, and frequented by big pelagics like grey reef sharks and hammerheads. The South Plateau, shorter but equally captivating, slopes from 20 to 45 meters, with towering pinnacles and steep walls that descend beyond 100 meters. At shallower depths, a beautiful cave system awaits, adding mystery and a unique habitat for marine life.

Adding to the adventure, the wreck of Levanzo lies on Elba Reef’s eastern side. Resting upside down at 22 meters, the wreck’s black and soft coral-covered surfaces attract groupers, trevally, and abundant smaller species. Divers can explore portions of the wreck and finish their dive along the coral-lined reef.

On the fifth day, divers explore the uncharted reefs between Elba and Abu Fendira, part of a 2,700-square-nautical-mile stretch rarely visited. This day of discovery invites divers to venture into unexplored underwater realms, contributing to the selection of top sites for future itineraries, making this Deep South journey an extraordinary blend of exploration, discovery, and natural beauty.

red-sea-aggressor-v::deep-south-elba-ree.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night Deep South itinerary from Hamata takes divers to the pristine Rocky and Zabargad Islands, two of the Red Sea’s most remote and captivating marine parks. The journey offers incredible diversity, from vibrant coral gardens to thrilling walls teeming with pelagics.

Starting with Abu Galawa East & West, these sites offer relaxed dives with excellent visibility, making them ideal for beginners or as checkout dives. The area’s coral gardens and shallow pinnacles sit between 15 and 25 meters, perfect for drift diving and an inviting start to the week.

Moving to Zabargad Island, Egypt’s largest southern marine park, divers encounter a rich ecosystem including Turtle Bay, home to reef fish, cuttlefish, octopuses, blue-spotted rays, and crocodile fish. During August, Zabargad becomes a nesting ground for turtles, adding a unique seasonal spectacle. Beyond the coves, dramatic walls adorned with hard and soft corals reveal stronger currents, bringing encounters with oceanic whitetips, grey reef sharks, hammerheads, silvertips, and manta rays. red-sea-aggressor-v::deep-south-elba-ree.highlightsDescription:
This 9-night Deep South itinerary from Hamata to Abu Fendira and Elba Reef immerses divers in one of the Red Sea’s most secluded and untouched regions. Known for its rich biodiversity and expansive coral formations, this route offers a pristine dive experience, far from other liveaboards and teeming with marine life.

Abu Fendira’s 6-kilometer stretch of reefs runs in an east-west direction, with depths ranging from 15 to 25 meters. Divers can expect vivid coral blocks, with sharks gliding nearby, schools of fish, and sightings of magnificent Napoleon wrasse and the rare humphead parrotfish. The reef’s remote beauty makes for an incredible underwater scene, filled with movement and color.

Moving to Elba Reef, divers encounter stunning topography. The North Plateau begins at 20 meters and drops to 45 meters, lined with huge coral fans along its edges, and frequented by big pelagics like grey reef sharks and hammerheads. The South Plateau, shorter but equally captivating, slopes from 20 to 45 meters, with towering pinnacles and steep walls that descend beyond 100 meters. At shallower depths, a beautiful cave system awaits, adding mystery and a unique habitat for marine life.

Adding to the adventure, the wreck of Levanzo lies on Elba Reef’s eastern side. Resting upside down at 22 meters, the wreck’s black and soft coral-covered surfaces attract groupers, trevally, and abundant smaller species. Divers can explore portions of the wreck and finish their dive along the coral-lined reef.

On the fifth day, divers explore the uncharted reefs between Elba and Abu Fendira, part of a 2,700-square-nautical-mile stretch rarely visited. This day of discovery invites divers to venture into unexplored underwater realms, contributing to the selection of top sites for future itineraries, making this Deep South journey an extraordinary blend of exploration, discovery, and natural beauty.

  • Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforseeable factors

• The "North Route" is the most famous and visited route of the red sea. It is a complete and simple route for diving matching all diving levels.The sailing on this route is very short and pleasant, reaching the furtherst dive sites in about two hours.The wide range of dive sites will give you the opportunity of diving amazing reefs lke those found in Ras Mohamed National Park and the Straits of Tiran, visiting a live WWII museum at the wreck of SS Thistlegorm, explore spectacular wrecks like the Dunraven and the Kingston and enjoying all the underwater wonders of the Red Sea in pristine dive like Small Crack and Shag Rock.
  • Straits of Tiran, are actually a submerged ridge that rises from more than 300 meters depth and extends from the southeast point of Sinai until the island of Tiran. It is basically a passage between the Gulf of Aqaba and th main basin of the Red Sea, forming an area of strong tidal currents. In the Strait we find 4 reefs which are famous for the quality of their coral and abundant sea life. Large oceanic life sightings are typical.
  • Gordon Reef : a circular reef where there is a large sandy plateau and remains of a shipwreck. The wrecks of Lullia lays right atop the reef making her a superb landmark. Night dives are spectacular
  • Thomas Reef is the smallest of the four reefs of Tiran and if conditions are calm it is possible to circle around the entire reef. There are no moornig so all dives are made as drift dives. On the South Plateau you can found the Thomas Canyon, an amazing dive for the technical divers. The walls of Thomas reef are completely covered with soft corals and a lot of Gorgonian fun corals and trees of black corals. In the blue there is always the possibility of finding large pelagic fish cruising by and even hammerhead sharks 
  • Woodhouse Reef is the longest reef of Tiran, ideal for easy drift dives. It is an almost vertical wall with plummets into the deep. It also has an underwater canyon and a couple of caves suitable only for technical divers. In the canyon area we can see one of the few red anemones in the area.
  • Jackson Reef it is considered as the best reef in the area due to the quality of the corals, abundance of wildlife and encounter with pelagic life. It is a round reef with vertical walls and a shallow coral garden on the west side. Continually swept by strong currents sometimes extremely strong. It's great for wild drift dives, large fish life encounters and beautiful coral sighthings. During the summer months. Also on the North side we find remains of the Lara wreck, a cargo ship.
  • Anemone City, Shark Reef & Yolanda Reef: the most famous dive in Red Sea and considered one of the best site in the world. You will start at Anemone city where dozens of huge anemones hosting a moltitude of clown fish and damsel. From here you leap into the blue crossing over the depts below to the walls of shark reef. Along the way possible sights include sharks, tuna, red snapper and other large pelagic marine animals. From there the dives continue on the shallower waters between the two reefs. Here you will be able to see parts of the freighter ship Yolanda which struck the reef and gave it its name. Among the debris you'll find a large collection of toilets and the remains of the captain's BMW. The area around the wreck often houses Lionfish, Blue Spotted Stingray and Mory eels. the entire stretch between the two reefs is strewn with rocks, overgrown with coral as well as lots of coral on the sides of the reef, which contrast nicely with white sandy bottom. The shallow water, the light reflecting off from the bottom and the colorful reefs make this a photographer's paradise. 
  • Jackfish Alley, the dive start at 5 mt which is actually a swim through coming out at 9 mt.the cave is covered with small gorgonian fans and a crack on the roof allows the rays of sun through. From here you will swim on to a long Sandy Alley that gives the name to this site due to the large amount of jack fish found here. You can see barracuda, tuna and the usual Red Sea residents.
  • Ras Ghozlani is a beautiful dive site with a lot of interesting things to see and discover. You start off on a sandy slope and descend to the drop off around 25 meters. Tons of pinnacles in different shapes and sizes, covered with table corals, big gorgonian fans and healthy soft corals in many different colors. The pinnacles are teeming anthias and other colorful reef fish. 
  • SS Thistlegorm is the worlds most famous wreck, it is located in Shaab Ali. Sunk by German aircrafts in 1941 and later discovered by Jaques Custeau. It offers some of the most spectacular dives in the world with its sunken cargo of trucks, motorcycle, car, locomotives, weapons, ammunitions, wagons, aircraft wings, boots. Normally a minimum of two dives are made on the wreck, one outside visiting the propeller, anticraft gun and locomotives and another one going through all its decks and holds. If possible you can make a spectacular night dive on this wreck and even get to see skiddish lantern fish.
  • Kingstone Wreck sinked in 1881 when hit against the reef at full steam, transporting her cargo of coal. Amazing table corals and amount of surgeon fish make it an amazing dive.
  • Small Crack is one of the best reef dives of the area. It's a passage between the lagoon and open sea where a quite shallow corridor became an aquarium with hundreds of table corals, soft corals and sponges.

• 2 dives in the morning depending on guest flight schedules and the 24 hour requirement before flying.
  • Take advantage of an evening onshore to purchase souvenirs and enjoy Egypt's famous hospitality before your journey home the next day.
• Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!

serenity::brothers-daedalus-elphinstone-.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary, departing from and ending in Hurghada, takes you to three of the most iconic dive sites in the Red Sea: Brothers, Daedalus, and Elphinstone.

Brothers Islands offer thrilling dives with steep drop-offs, vibrant coral walls, and a chance to encounter hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetips, and large pelagics. The wrecks of the Aida and Numidia add an intriguing element to your dives here.

Daedalus Reef is a remote, large reef known for its sheer walls and strong currents, making it a magnet for pelagics like hammerheads, manta rays, and occasionally thresher sharks. The reef's coral garden is equally stunning, with a variety of soft and hard corals.

Elphinstone Reef is famous for its steep walls covered in soft corals and frequent sightings of oceanic whitetip sharks. The plateau at the southern tip of the reef is a must-visit for its dramatic underwater landscape and rich marine life.

Throughout the week, you'll experience drift dives, explore vibrant coral gardens, and encounter some of the Red Sea's most impressive marine life. The combination of these three legendary sites makes this itinerary a dream for experienced divers seeking adventure and unforgettable underwater encounters.

serenity::brothers-daedalus-elphinstone-.highlightsDescription:
The "Ras Mohamed & Wrecks" 7-night itinerary combines Egypt’s iconic wrecks with the vibrant marine life of the Ras Mohamed National Park, departing from and returning to Hurghada. This route is perfect for divers eager to explore historic shipwrecks and the stunning underwater ecosystems of the Red Sea.

Key highlights include dives at the famous Thistlegorm wreck, where World War II artifacts rest within the cargo holds, and the Abu Nuhas reef, home to multiple shipwrecks like the Carnatic and Giannis D. These sites offer fascinating insights into history, surrounded by colorful corals and schools of fish.

The itinerary also features Ras Mohamed, known for its clear waters, massive coral formations, and encounters with turtles, jacks, and reef sharks. The diversity of dive sites, from wrecks to vibrant reefs, makes this itinerary ideal for divers looking for a blend of history, marine biodiversity, and stunning seascapes.

serenity::north-ras-mohamed-tiran-hurgha.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary from Hurghada takes you to the northern Red Sea's premier dive sites, including Ras Mohamed and the Straits of Tiran, offering a perfect blend of vibrant coral reefs, dramatic drop-offs, and abundant marine life.

Ras Mohamed National Park, Egypt’s first marine reserve, is renowned for its stunning underwater scenery. You’ll dive at sites like Shark Reef and Yolanda Reef, where towering coral walls plunge into the deep blue, teeming with schools of fish, barracudas, jacks, and the occasional shark. The park's diversity of marine life and pristine coral formations make it a highlight of the trip.

The Straits of Tiran, located at the mouth of the Gulf of Aqaba, feature four main reefs: Jackson, Woodhouse, Thomas, and Gordon. These reefs are famous for their strong currents, which attract large pelagics such as eagle rays, sharks, and sometimes manta rays. The coral gardens here are some of the most beautiful in the Red Sea, with a kaleidoscope of colors and an abundance of reef fish.

Throughout the week, you’ll explore these iconic northern Red Sea sites, experiencing a variety of dive environments from drift dives along vertical walls to exploring vibrant coral gardens. This itinerary is perfect for divers seeking a mix of thrilling pelagic encounters and stunning underwater landscapes in some of the Red Sea’s most famous locations.

serenity::north-tiran-hurghada-hurghada-.highlightsDescription:
This 7-night itinerary from Hurghada explores the northern Red Sea’s most iconic dive destinations, combining the famous reefs of Ras Mohamed and the Straits of Tiran with the dramatic underwater landscapes around Dahab. Expect a diverse mix of coral gardens, steep walls, drift dives, and thriving marine life.

Ras Mohamed National Park, located at the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, is widely considered one of the best diving areas in the Red Sea. Here you will dive legendary sites such as Shark Reef and Yolanda Reef, where spectacular coral walls descend into deep blue water filled with schools of snapper, barracuda, jackfish, and reef sharks. The park’s pristine coral formations and rich biodiversity make it a highlight of any northern Red Sea itinerary.

The Straits of Tiran, situated at the entrance of the Gulf of Aqaba, feature four well-known reefs: Jackson, Woodhouse, Thomas, and Gordon. These reefs are famous for their vibrant coral gardens and frequent currents that attract pelagic species. Divers often encounter eagle rays, large schools of fish, turtles, and occasionally sharks cruising along the reef edges, making every dive dynamic and exciting.

The itinerary also includes dives around Dahab, home to some of the Red Sea’s most famous dive sites such as the Canyon and the Blue Hole. The Canyon is a spectacular underwater fissure that cuts through the reef, creating a dramatic dive with unique rock formations and schools of glassfish sheltering within the walls. Nearby, the Blue Hole is one of the most iconic dive locations in the region, a massive circular sinkhole surrounded by vibrant coral reefs and steep walls. These sites offer striking underwater scenery, abundant reef life, and a very different diving experience compared to the coral plateaus and drift dives found further south.

Throughout the week, divers will experience a wide variety of underwater environments, from colorful coral gardens and drift dives along reef walls to deeper sites with striking geological features. This itinerary is ideal for divers who want to explore the full diversity of the northern Red Sea while visiting some of its most famous and rewarding dive sites.

Ras Mohamed National Park, at the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, is famous for its vibrant coral reefs, clear waters, and diverse marine life, including reef sharks, barracuda, and turtles. The Brothers Islands, located further out into the Red Sea, are known for their dramatic drop-offs, clear visibility, and strong currents that attract pelagic species like hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetips, and large schools of barracuda and tuna. The coral reefs around the Brothers are equally impressive, with colorful fish and abundant marine life.

This liveaboard trip offers multiple dives each day, allowing divers to experience the best of both Ras Mohamed and the Brothers Islands. With warm waters, excellent visibility, and the chance for exhilarating shark encounters, this itinerary is ideal for experienced divers seeking a mix of challenging conditions and breathtaking underwater landscapes.

serenity::reefs-wrecks-gouna-gouna-3-nig.highlightsDescription:
This 3-night itinerary departing from Hurghada focuses on two of the Red Sea’s most famous wreck diving sites, offering a compact yet thrilling experience for wreck enthusiasts.

The SS Thistlegorm, a WWII British cargo ship sunk in 1941, is the centerpiece of this itinerary. Known as one of the world’s most famous wrecks, it offers divers the chance to explore its well-preserved cargo holds filled with motorcycles, trucks, and wartime supplies. The wreck is also a hotspot for marine life, including schools of fish, rays, and sometimes even sharks.

Abu Nuhas, often referred to as the "Ship Graveyard," is home to four wrecks in close proximity: the Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, and Kimon M. Each wreck provides a unique diving experience, from the shallow, coral-covered remains of the Carnatic to the more intact Giannis D, where divers can explore the engine room and crew quarters.

Over the course of these four nights, you’ll dive into history, exploring these iconic wrecks and encountering the vibrant marine life that now calls them home. This itinerary is ideal for divers seeking a shorter trip that still delivers some of the Red Sea’s most renowned wreck diving experiences.

serenity::reefs-wrecks-hurghada-hurghada.highlightsDescription:
This 3-night itinerary out of Hurghada combines the best of both worlds, offering dives at the famous Abu Nuhas wrecks and the vibrant reefs of North Hurghada and Gubal Island.

At Abu Nuhas, known as the "Ship Graveyard," you’ll explore some of the Red Sea’s most renowned wrecks. The Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, and Kimon M lie in close proximity, each offering a unique diving experience. From navigating through the intact sections of the Giannis D to admiring the coral-encrusted remains of the Carnatic, these wrecks are teeming with marine life and rich in history.

The North Hurghada reefs provide a stunning contrast with their colorful coral gardens and abundant marine life. These reefs are home to a variety of species, including reef fish, moray eels, and the occasional turtle, making for relaxed yet captivating dives.

Gubal Island adds another layer of excitement to the trip. Here, you’ll dive the famous Barge Wreck, a shallow wreck dive that’s great for exploring with its resident morays, scorpionfish, and a myriad of other reef creatures. The surrounding reefs are equally vibrant, offering some of the best coral formations in the area.

In just three nights, you’ll experience a rich variety of dive sites, from historic wrecks to pristine reefs, making this itinerary perfect for divers looking for a short but immersive Red Sea adventure.

Guest may also rebook to a different live aboard within the King Snefro Fleet than planned before. Rescheduling is subject to availability. Rescheduled trips must be of equal or lesser value. Should the rescheduled trip be of lesser value, there will be no partial refunds issued.

  • Safety Briefing, Crew Introduction, Necessary Dive Paperwork, Cabin allocation and ship orientation will take place before departing the Harbour.

• In the early morning sail to nearby Temple or Ras Katy for a check dive.
  • The week long safari will cover the area from the Strait of Tiran, Ras Mohamed National Park and the Gulf of Suez which is usual visited first.
  • The National Park begins at the small bay of Marsa Ghazlani followed by the larger and deeper bay of Marsa Bareika.
  • Continuing along the coast to Ras Za'atar, Jackfish Alley, Eel Garden and Shark Observatory, to the southern end of the peninsula with Anemone City, Shark Reef and Yolanda Reef and ending at the Quay.
  • Because of the geographic position this is a privileged area distinguished to strong massive currents that transport large quantities of plankton and other food that give rise to an extraordinary growth of stony and soft corals and attract large schools of both reef and pelagic marine fauna, over a thousand species in all.
  • Schooling barracuda, jackfish, tuna and many kind of sharks swim in these deep blue waters, especially in summer from June to August, sometimes till early October.
  • The safari will also take you to famous sites like the wrecks of Dunraven and Thistlegorm, Shag Rock and the wreck of Kingston, sail to Sha'ab Ali where pods of dolphins are common, explore several spots at Sha'ab Mahmouds reef system.
  • Don't miss the four famous reefs in the Strait of Tiran: Jackson, Thomas, Woodhouse and Gordon Reef, probably the most interesting and richest in marine life.
  • You can choose from several dive sites with superb wall and drift diving

days.description:
Embarkation, Sharm El Sheikh

Board the liveaboard in the evening at New Marina, settle into your cabin, and attend the welcome and safety briefings. Overnight in port.

Ras Mohamed

Check dive followed by dives at some of Ras Mohamed’s most famous reefs, featuring coral gardens, pinnacles, swim-throughs, and abundant marine life. Night dive possible.

Thistlegorm & Gubal Area

Spend the day diving the legendary Thistlegorm wreck, including exterior exploration and possible penetration dives for qualified divers. Additional dive in the Gubal area. Night dive possible.

Ras Mohamed & Tiran Strait

Dive the historic Dunraven wreck and the famous Shark & Yolanda Reef before heading north to the Strait of Tiran for an afternoon dive on one of its renowned reefs. Night dive possible.

Tiran Reefs & Return

Morning dives at Jackson Reef and either Thomas or Woodhouse Reef, followed by a final dive near Sharm El Sheikh before returning to port. Disembarkation in the afternoon.

snefro-love::sinai-classic-sharm-el-shei.highlightsDescription:
Discover the very best of the northern Red Sea on this 4-night mini liveaboard adventure from Sharm El Sheikh. Combining the legendary wreck of Thistlegorm, the world-renowned reefs of Ras Mohamed National Park, and the spectacular coral formations of the Strait of Tiran, this itinerary offers an excellent balance of wreck and reef diving in a short timeframe.

Designed for experienced divers looking to maximize their underwater time, the trip features up to 15 dives across some of Egypt’s most celebrated dive sites. Explore vibrant coral gardens, dramatic walls, pinnacles swept by nutrient-rich currents, and historic shipwrecks teeming with marine life. Encounters may include large schools of barracuda, trevallies, tuna, turtles, eagle rays, dolphins, and reef sharks.

A highlight of the itinerary is the famous Thistlegorm, widely regarded as one of the finest wreck dives in the world. Divers can explore its cargo holds filled with wartime artifacts while also enjoying the rich marine ecosystem that has developed around the wreck. Equally impressive are the reefs of Ras Mohamed and Tiran, where colorful hard and soft corals create breathtaking underwater landscapes.

Perfect for divers who want a complete Red Sea experience without committing to a full week at sea, this itinerary combines iconic dive sites, comfortable liveaboard accommodation, and the opportunity to experience some of Egypt’s most rewarding underwater environments.

days.description:
• Afternoon/Evening: transfer to El Wataneya port and embark
  • Safety briefing, crew introduction, necessary dive paperwork, cabin allocation and ship orientation will take place before departing the harbor.
  •  Please take this opportunity to familiarize yourself with the vessel and make yourself comfortable.
  • Sailing very early next morning

• Check dive at Temple or Ras Katy.
  • Next dive is Jackfish Alley where you can easily enter the small caves there.
  • The third dive will be the Alternatives, a chain of seven pinnacles with numerous sand patches and resident leopard sharks.
  • Night Diving is very popular here.

• Early morning: the boat will sail to the wreck of the Thistlegorm, the most famous of the Red Sea Wrecks, maybe even worldwide. There is so much to explore so the plan is a minimum of two dives. The first one is an orientation of the outside and the second dive a penetrating one.
  • For the third dive your boat will sail to Small Passage where two channels cut the reef system of Sha’ab Mahmoud and connect the sheltered lagoon to the open sea.
  • A night dive inside the lagoon is optional.

• Last day of the trip
  • Morning: first dive of the day will take you to the historical wreck of the Dunraven, which sank in April 1876 - an old wooden wreck with plenty of room for passing through thousands of glassfish that live here in the shade of the wreck.
  • Next dive is Shark and Yolanda Reef, the southernmost tip of the Sinai Peninsula with an endless wall unique in the Red Sea.
  • Sailing back towards Sharm for your third dive at Ras Zatar, Ras Ghozlani or may be Ras Um Sid.
  • Unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!
  • Return to port and disembark
  • Transfer to hotel or airport
  • It is your responsibility to ensure you respect the 24 hour no-fly time after your last dive!
  • Please Note: This is a sample itinerary and nº of dives, dive sites, etc. may be subject to change due to weather conditions and other unforeseeable factors.

days.description:
• Afternoon/Evening: transfer to El Wataneya port and embark
  • Safety Briefing, Crew Introduction, Necessary Dive Paperwork, Cabin allocation and ship orientation will take place before departing the Harbour.
  • Please take this opportunity to familiarize yourselves with the vessel and make yourself comfortable.
  • Sailing very early next morning

• In the early morning sail to nearby Temple or Ras Katy for a check dive.
  • The week long safari will cover the area from the Strait of Tiran, Ras Mohamed National Park and the Gulf of Suez which is usual visited first.
  • The National Park begins at the small bay of Marsa Ghazlani followed by the larger and deeper bay of Marsa Bareika.
  • Continuing along the coast to Ras Za'atar, Jackfish Alley, Eel Garden and Shark Observatory, to the southern end of the peninsula with Anemone City, Shark Reef and Yolanda Reef and ending at the Quay.
  • Because of the geographic position this is a privileged area distinguished to strong massive currents that transport large quantities of plankton and other food that give rise to an extraordinary growth of stony and soft corals and attract large schools of both reef and pelagic marine fauna, over a thousand species in all.
  • Schooling barracuda, jackfish, tuna and many kind of sharks swim in these deep blue waters, especially in summer from June to August, sometimes till early October.
  • The safari will also take you to famous sites like the wrecks of Dunraven and Thistlegorm, Shag Rock and the wreck of Kingston, sail to Sha'ab Ali where pods of dolphins are common, explore several spots at Sha'ab Mahmouds reef system.
  • Don't miss the four famous reefs in the Strait of Tiran: Jackson, Thomas, Woodhouse and Gordon Reef, probably the most interesting and richest in marine life.
  • You can choose from several dive sites with superb wall and drift diving

• Last diving day with the last dive being around noon
  • In the afternoon of the 7th day the boat will return to Sharm area
  • Depending on customer wishes, boat might return to port in the late afternoon/early evening of the penultimate day or in the morning of the last day

• Last day of the trip;  unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!
  • Return to port and disembark
  • Check out from early morning until 12:00 noon at the latest
  • Transfer to airport or hotel
  • It is your responsibility to ensure you respect the 24 hour no-fly time after your last dive!

Before your trip

  • Transfer from your local hotel or airport on departure day is included and will be arranged by the boat. Please provide your arrival details as early as possible
  • Transfer Meeting point: In case of Flight arrival the guide will wait you outside the arrival hall with a sign stating your name, King Snefro Fleet. For hotel pick up meeting point is at the reception

On the boat

The end of your trip

  • Depending on customer wishes, boat might return to port in the late afternoon/early evening of the penultimate day or in the morning of the last day

days.description:
• Afternoon/Evening: transfer to El Wataneya port and embark
  • Safety briefing, crew introduction, necessary dive paperwork, cabin allocation and ship orientation will take place before departing the harbor.
  • Please take this opportunity to familiarize yourself with the vessel and make yourself comfortable.
  • Sailing very early next morning

• Sail to nearby Temple or Ras Katy for a check dive., after into the Gulf of Suez passing Yolanda Reef that is named after a 74 m long Cypriot freighter which struck the reef on the 1st of April 1980.
  • The wreck lies partially submerged on the reef top until a storm caused it to drop. Most of the ship finally has fallen over the drop-off, leaving a huge scar in the slope between Shark and Yolanda Reef.
  • Although, a quantity of the cargo remains for the amusement of the divers: bathtubs, toilets and bathroom fittings. Continue with the historical wrecks of Dunraven. Recovered in early 1970's, the more than 125 years old wreck is largely intact, totally covered in corals and rich in marine life.
  • The most famous of the Red Sea wrecks maybe even worldwide is the Thistlegorm. The wreck first gained fame when Jacques Cousteau dived it in 1956 but left the actual location a mystery until it was rediscovered in 1992.
  • Lying upright on the seabed at 33 m, the 127 m long and 18 m wide wreck is absolutely impressive. Close to Sha'ab Ali in the early hours of 22 February 1881, the 78 m long Kingston ran aground at the northern edge of the reef that is known as Shag Rock.
  • Crossing the Gulf of Suez will take you to Abu Nuhas, a paradise for wreck lovers which is best known for the abundance of ancient and modern wrecks that lie here: Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K and Kimon M.
  • All are located on the northern side of the reef, a sandy seafloor at the bottom of a steep sloping coral reef filled with table corals.
  • The reef is very exposed to the prevailing wind and waves and was named after the oldest wreck which was carrying copper (Nuhas in Arabic).
  • If weather permits you can dive the Ulysses or the Rosalie Moller. Only two days after the sinking of the Thistlegorm, the Rosalie Moller was also lying at anchor when hit and went down upright.
  • The location outside of Gubal Island is extremely exposed to the sea, wind and waves. The dive is deep, bottom time is limited and visibility is lower than elsewhere so this dive is definitely only for very experienced divers.
  • Note May 2012: Dive Sites in the area of Gubal Island can not be dived due to an order from the military. This affects the dive sites of Ulysses, Barge, Malak and the Rosalie Moller. It is unknown how long the restriction will be in place.
  • Optional as located far north of Tiran and only reachable with good sea conditions, a rarely dived wreck is the Million Hope.
  • This wreck is one of the youngest in the Egyptian Red Sea and the second largest of the diveable ones. Its size alone makes it a memorable dive.
  • In between wreck dives you will also visit some outstanding reefs at Sha'ab Mahmoud and Ras Mohammed National Park
  • The itinerary is an example so if you have a special wish for a certain place in this area just let your dive guide know

• Last diving day with the last dive being around noon
  • In the afternoon of the 7th day the boat will return to Sharm area
  • Depending on customer wishes, boat might return to port in the late afternoon/early evening of the penultimate day or in the morning of the last day

• Last day of the trip;  unfortunately our trip has come to an end and we have to say goodbye, but we hope to see you again soon!
  • Return to port and disembark

snefro-target::sinai-wrecks-reefs-sharm-.highlightsDescription:
• A week-long diving safari starting and ending in Sharm El Sheikh concentrating on some of the best wrecks worldwide
  • Dive on Dunraven, World War II wreck Thistlegorm and the ship’s graveyard of Abu Nuhas with Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K and the Kimon M.
  • Wreck diving, coral reefs, wall dives and pelagic.
  • Truly a fantastic place, home to an array of incredible sharks species, majestic manta rays, massive groupers, curious jacks, schools of barracudas and more
  • The visibility is fantastic but the currents can be strong
  • Up to 4 dives per day
snefro-target::sinai-wrecks-reefs-sharm-.logistics:
Before your trip

  • On this trip the boat departs and returns from/to Sharm El Sheikh (El Wataneya)
  • Check-in starts from 18:00 onwards till late night
  • Transfer from your local hotel or airport on departure day is included and will be arranged by the boat. Please provide your arrival details as early as possible
  • Transfer Meeting point: In case of Flight arrival the guide will wait you outside the arrival hall with a sign stating your name, King Snefro Fleet. For hotel pick up meeting point is at the reception
  • The boat departs in the very early morning hours of the following day

On the boat

  • All divers are required to show valid certification, logbook and to sign a medical statement and liability release form prior to the boat’s departure. Diving activities can be restricted if the guide has any doubts about divers safety and/or qualifications
  • Each diver is requested to use a dive computer, to carry a Surface Marker Buoy at each dive and a torch at any night dive. Please bring these pieces of equipment with you or give a note that you will need to rent it
  • The boat has DIN bottles with INT adapters
  • Toiletries are not provided
  • Rental equipment has to be prearranged but can be paid on board
  • No Night Diving in Marine Parks

The end of your trip

  • On the penultimate day you will have the option to dive 2-3 times, depending on the itinerary
  • Usually the last dive is on the penultimate day around noon
  • Depending on customer wishes, boat might return to port in the late afternoon/early evening of the penultimate day or in the morning of the last day
  • On the last day check-out is before noon and you will then be transferred to the airport or local hotel as early as needed
